<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api">MongoDB Atlas Administration API v2.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

The MongoDB Atlas Administration API allows developers to manage all components in MongoDB Atlas.

The Atlas Administration API supports OAuth2 Service Accounts and HTTP Digest-based API keys. Service accounts are the recommended authentication method and API keys are considered a legacy option.

To authenticate with a Service Account, first exchange its client ID and secret for an access token using the OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow. Atlas provides a token endpoint at `POST https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/oauth/token`, which returns a Bearer token that is reusable and valid for 1 hour (3600 seconds).

For example, to [return a list of your organizations](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/operation/operation-listorgs) with [cURL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CURL), first generate an access token and then use that token to call the same Atlas Administration API endpoint shown in the current example:

```
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(curl -fsS --request POST https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/oauth/token \
  --header "Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' "${CLIENT_ID}:${CLIENT_SECRET}" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  --header "Accept: application/json" \
  --data "grant_type=client_credentials" | jq -r '.access_token')

curl --header "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  --header "Accept: application/vnd.atlas.2025-03-12+json" \
  -X GET "https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/orgs?pretty=true"
```

If your organization requires an IP access list for the Atlas Administration API, the token can be created from any IP address, but the API call that uses the token must originate from an allowed IP.

To learn more, see [Get Started with the Atlas Administration API](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access/). For support, see [MongoDB Support](https://www.mongodb.com/support/get-started).

You can also explore the various endpoints available through the Atlas Administration API in MongoDB's [Postman workspace](https://www.postman.com/mongodb-devrel/workspace/mongodb-atlas-administration-apis/) (requires a Postman account).

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://cloud.mongodb.com">https://cloud.mongodb.com</a>

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/mongodb-management-service-terms-and-conditions">Terms of service</a>

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: digest

- oAuth2 authentication. Learn more about [Service Accounts](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/api/service-accounts-overview).

    - Flow: clientCredentials
    - Token URL = [https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/oauth/token](https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/oauth/token)

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-access-tracking">Access Tracking</h1>

Returns access logs for authentication attempts made to Atlas database deployments.

## Return Database Access History for One Cluster by Cluster Name

<a id="opIdgetGroupDbAccessHistoryCluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/dbAccessHistory/clusters/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/dbAccessHistory/clusters/{clusterName}`

Returns the access logs of one cluster identified by the cluster's name. Access logs contain a list of authentication requests made against your cluster. You can't use this feature on tenant-tier clusters (M0, M2, M5).

<a href="https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/access-tracking/">Database Access History</a>

<h3 id="return-database-access-history-for-one-cluster-by-cluster-name-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|authResult|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response returns the successful authentication attempts only.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|end|query|integer(int64)|false|Date and time when to stop retrieving database history. If you specify **end**, you must also specify **start**. This parameter uses UNIX epoch time in milliseconds.|
|ipAddress|query|string|false|One Internet Protocol address that attempted to authenticate with the database.|
|nLogs|query|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of lines from the log to return.|
|start|query|integer(int64)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud begins retrieving database history. If you specify **start**, you must also specify **end**. This parameter uses UNIX epoch time in milliseconds.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "accessLogs": [
    {
      "authResult": true,
      "authSource": "string",
      "failureReason": "string",
      "groupId": "string",
      "hostname": "string",
      "ipAddress": "string",
      "logLine": "string",
      "timestamp": "string",
      "username": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-activity-feed">Activity Feed</h1>

Returns pre-filtered activity feed links for projects and organizations. The returned links can be shared and opened to view the activity feed with the specified filters applied.

## Return Pre-Filtered Activity Feed Link for One Project

<a id="opIdgetGroupActivityFeed"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/activityFeed \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/activityFeed`

Returns a pre-filtered activity feed link for the specified project based on the provided date range and event types. The returned link can be shared and opened to view the activity feed with the same filters applied.

<h3 id="return-pre-filtered-activity-feed-link-for-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|eventType|query|[[EventTypeForNdsGroup](#schemaeventtypeforndsgroup)]|false|Category of incident recorded at this moment in time.<br><br>**IMPORTANT**: The complete list of event type values changes frequently.|
|maxDate|query|string(date-time)|false|End date and time for events to include in the activity feed link. ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|minDate|query|string(date-time)|false|Start date and time for events to include in the activity feed link. ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|clusterName|query|[string]|false|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "link": "https://cloud.mongodb.com/redirect/1234567890abcdef12345678",
  "links": [
    {
      "href": "https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas",
      "rel": "self"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-ai-model-api-keys">AI Model API Keys</h1>

Returns, adds, edits, and removes API Keys for your AI Models.

## Return AI Model API Keys for One Group

<a id="opIdlistGroupAiModelApiKeys"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/aiModelApiKeys \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/aiModelApiKeys`

Retrieve AI model API keys for the given group.

Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/aiModelApiClouds/{cloud}/geographies/{geography}/modelGroupNames/{modelGroupName}/rateLimits`

```json
  "tokensPerMinuteLimit": 1
}
```

`PUT /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/alertConfigs/{alertConfigId}`

**NOTE**: To enable or disable the alert configuration, see Toggle One State of One Alert Configuration in One Project.

This resource remains under revision and may change.

```bash
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/alertConfigs/{alertConfigId}`

Enables or disables the specified alert configuration in the specified project. The resource enables the specified alert configuration if currently enabled. The resource disables the specified alert configuration if currently disabled.

**NOTE**: This endpoint updates only the enabled/disabled state for the alert configuration. To update more than just this configuration, see Update One Alert Configuration.

This resource remains under revision and may change.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Alert-Configurations/operation/updateAlertConfiguration">Update One Alert Configuration</a>

```json
}
```

## Return All Alerts from One Project

<a id="opIdlistGroupAlerts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/alerts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/alerts`

Returns all alerts. These alerts apply to all components in one project. You receive an alert when a monitored component meets or exceeds a value you set.

This resource remains under revision and may change.

<h3 id="return-all-alerts-from-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|includeCount|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud calculates the total number of items for the response. When set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may skip an additional count operation. The response may still include `totalCount` when the count is available without additional calculation.|
|itemsPerPage|query|integer|false|Number of items that the response returns per page.|
|pageNum|query|integer|false|Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|status|query|string|false|Status of the alerts to return. Omit this parameter to return all alerts in all statuses. TRACKING indicates the alert condition exists but has not persisted for the minimum notification delay. OPEN indicates the alert condition currently exists. CLOSED indicates the alert condition has been resolved.|

|status|TRACKING|
|status|CLOSED|

## Acknowledge One Alert from One Project

<a id="opIdacknowledgeGroupAlert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/alerts/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "acknowledgedUntil": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "acknowledgementComment": "Expiration on 3/19.  Silencing for 7 days."
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/alerts/{alertId}`

Confirms receipt of one existing alert. This alert applies to any component in one project. Acknowledging an alert prevents successive notifications. You receive an alert when a monitored component meets or exceeds a value you set until you acknowledge the alert. Use the Return All Alerts from One Project endpoint to retrieve all alerts to which the authenticated user has access.

This resource remains under revision and may change.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Alerts/operation/listAlerts">Return All Alerts from One Project</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "acknowledgedUntil": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "acknowledgementComment": "Expiration on 3/19.  Silencing for 7 days."
}
```

<h3 id="acknowledge-one-alert-from-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|alertId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the alert.|
|body|body|[AlertView](#schemaalertview)|true|Acknowledges or unacknowledges one alert.|
|» acknowledgedUntil|body|string(date-time)|false|Date and time until which this alert has been acknowledged. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. The resource returns this parameter if a MongoDB User previously acknowledged this alert.<br><br>- To acknowledge this alert forever, set the parameter value to 100 years in the future.<br><br>- To unacknowledge a previously acknowledged alert, do not set this parameter value.|
|» acknowledgementComment|body|string|false|Comment that a MongoDB Cloud user submitted when acknowledging the alert.|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-atlas-search">Atlas Search</h1>

Returns, adds, edits, and removes Atlas Search indexes for the specified cluster. Also returns and updates user-defined analyzers for the specified cluster.

## Create One Atlas Search Index

<a id="opIdcreateGroupClusterFtsIndex"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/fts/indexes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "collectionName": "string",
    "database": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "numPartitions": 1,
    "storedSource": {
      "include | exclude": [
        "field1",
        "field2"
      ]
    },
    "type": "search"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/fts/indexes`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Creates one Atlas Search index on the specified collection. Atlas Search indexes define the fields on which to create the index and the analyzers to use when creating the index. Only clusters running MongoDB v4.2 or later can use Atlas Search.

<a href="https://dochub.mongodb.org/core/index-definitions-fts">Atlas Search Indexes</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "collectionName": "string",
  "database": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "numPartitions": 1,
  "storedSource": {
    "include | exclude": [
      "field1",
      "field2"
    ]
  },
  "type": "search"
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-atlas-search-index-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Name of the cluster that contains the collection on which to create an Atlas Search index.|
|body|body|[ClusterSearchIndex](#schemaclustersearchindex)|true|Creates one Atlas Search index on the specified collection.|
|» collectionName|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the collection that contains one or more Atlas Search indexes.|
|» database|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the database that contains the collection with one or more Atlas Search indexes.|
|» name|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies this index. Within each namespace, names of all indexes in the namespace must be unique.|
|» numPartitions|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of index partitions. Allowed values are [1, 2, 4].|
|» storedSource|body|object|false|Flag that indicates whether to store all fields (true) on Atlas Search. By default, Atlas doesn't store (false) the fields on Atlas Search.  Alternatively, you can specify an object that only contains the list of fields to store (include) or not store (exclude) on Atlas Search. Note that storing all fields (true) is not allowed for vector search indexes. To learn more, see documentation.|
|» type|body|string|false|Type of the index. Default type is search.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|search|
|» type|vectorSearch|

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/fts/indexes/{indexId}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Updates one Atlas Search index that you identified with its unique ID. Atlas Search indexes define the fields on which to create the index and the analyzers to use when creating the index.

<a href="https://dochub.mongodb.org/core/index-definitions-fts">Atlas Search Indexes</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "collectionName": "string",
  "database": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "numPartitions": 1,
  "storedSource": {
    "include | exclude": [
      "field1",
      "field2"
    ]
  },
  "type": "search"
}
```

<h3 id="update-one-atlas-search-index-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Name of the cluster that contains the collection whose Atlas Search index to update.|
|indexId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the Atlas Search [index](https://dochub.mongodb.org/core/index-definitions-fts). Use the [Get All Atlas Search Indexes for a Collection API](https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/reference/api/fts-indexes-get-all/) endpoint to find the IDs of all Atlas Search indexes.|
|body|body|[ClusterSearchIndex](#schemaclustersearchindex)|true|Details to update on the Atlas Search index.|
|» collectionName|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the collection that contains one or more Atlas Search indexes.|
|» database|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the database that contains the collection with one or more Atlas Search indexes.|
|» name|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies this index. Within each namespace, names of all indexes in the namespace must be unique.|
|» numPartitions|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of index partitions. Allowed values are [1, 2, 4].|
|» storedSource|body|object|false|Flag that indicates whether to store all fields (true) on Atlas Search. By default, Atlas doesn't store (false) the fields on Atlas Search.  Alternatively, you can specify an object that only contains the list of fields to store (include) or not store (exclude) on Atlas Search. Note that storing all fields (true) is not allowed for vector search indexes. To learn more, see documentation.|
|» type|body|string|false|Type of the index. Default type is search.|

|» type|vectorSearch|

## Create One Atlas Search Index

<a id="opIdcreateGroupClusterSearchIndex"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/search/indexes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2024-05-30+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "collectionName": "string",
    "database": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "type": "search"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/search/indexes`

Creates one Atlas Search index on the specified collection. Atlas Search indexes define the fields on which to create the index and the analyzers to use when creating the index. Only clusters running MongoDB v4.2 or later can use Atlas Search.

<a href="https://dochub.mongodb.org/core/index-definitions-fts">Atlas Search Indexes</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "collectionName": "string",
  "database": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "type": "search"
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-atlas-search-index-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Name of the cluster that contains the collection on which to create an Atlas Search index.|
|body|body|[SearchIndexCreateRequest](#schemasearchindexcreaterequest)|true|Creates one Atlas Search index on the specified collection.|
|» collectionName|body|string|true|Label that identifies the collection to create an Atlas Search index in.|
|» database|body|string|true|Label that identifies the database that contains the collection to create an Atlas Search index in.|
|» name|body|string|true|Label that identifies this index. Within each namespace, names of all indexes in the namespace must be unique.|
|» type|body|string|false|Type of the index. The default type is search.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|search|
|» type|vectorSearch|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-auditing">Auditing</h1>

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-aws-clusters-dns">AWS Clusters DNS</h1>

Returns and edits custom DNS configurations for MongoDB Cloud database deployments on AWS. The resource requires your Project ID. If you use the VPC peering on AWS and you use your own DNS servers instead of Amazon Route 53, enable custom DNS. Before 31 March 2020, applications deployed within AWS using custom DNS services and VPC-peered with MongoDB Cloud couldn't connect over private IP addresses. Custom DNS resolved to public IP addresses. AWS internal DNS resolved to private IP addresses. Applications deployed with custom DNS services in AWS should use Private IP for Peering connection strings.

## Return One Custom DNS Configuration for Atlas Clusters on AWS

<a id="opIdgetGroupAwsCustomDns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/awsCustomDNS \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/backup/exportBuckets`

Creates a Snapshot Export Bucket for an AWS S3 Bucket, Azure Blob Storage Container, or Google Cloud Storage Bucket. Once created, an snapshots can be exported to the Export Bucket and its referenced AWS S3 Bucket, Azure Blob Storage Container, or Google Cloud Storage Bucket.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "bucketName": "export-bucket",
  "cloudProvider": "AWS",
  "iamRoleId": "668c5f0ed436263134491592",
  "requirePrivateNetworking": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-snapshot-export-bucket-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[DiskBackupSnapshotAWSExportBucketRequest](#schemadiskbackupsnapshotawsexportbucketrequest)|true|Specifies the role and AWS S3 Bucket, Azure Blob Storage Container, or Google Cloud Storage Bucket that the Export Bucket should reference.|
|» cloudProvider|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cloud provider.|
|» bucketName|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the AWS S3 Bucket that the role is authorized to export to.|
|» iamRoleId|body|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal character string that identifies the Unified AWS Access role ID that MongoDB Cloud uses to access the AWS S3 bucket.|
|» requirePrivateNetworking|body|boolean|false|Indicates whether to do exports over PrivateLink as opposed to public IPs. Defaults to False.|

```json
      "frequencyType": "daily",
      "retentionUnit": "days",
      "retentionValue": 0
    }
```
```bash
  ]
```
```json
}
```

<h3 id="update-backup-compliance-policy-settings-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|overwriteBackupPolicies|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to overwrite non complying backup policies with the new data protection settings or not.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[DataProtectionSettings](#schemadataprotectionsettings)|true|The new Backup Compliance Policy settings.|
|» authorizedEmail|body|string(email)|true|Email address of the user who authorized to update the Backup Compliance Policy  settings.|
|» authorizedUserFirstName|body|string|false|First name of the user who authorized to update the Backup Compliance Policy  settings.|
|» authorizedUserLastName|body|string|false|Last name of the user who authorized to update the Backup Compliance Policy  settings.|
|» copyProtectionEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to prevent cluster users from deleting backups copied to other regions, even if those additional snapshot regions are removed. If unspecified, this value defaults to false.|
|» encryptionAtRestEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Encryption at Rest using Customer Key  Management is required for all clusters with a Backup Compliance Policy. If unspecified, this value defaults to false.|
|» onDemandPolicyItem|body|[BackupComplianceOnDemandPolicyItem](#schemabackupcomplianceondemandpolicyitem)|false|Specifications for on-demand policy.|
|» pitEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the cluster uses Continuous Cloud Backups with a Backup Compliance Policy. If unspecified, this value defaults to false.|
|» projectId|body|string|false|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the project for the Backup Compliance Policy.|
|» restoreWindowDays|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of previous days that you can restore back to with Continuous Cloud Backup with a Backup Compliance Policy. You must specify a positive, non-zero integer, and the maximum retention window can't exceed the hourly retention time. This parameter applies only to Continuous Cloud Backups with a Backup Compliance Policy.|
|» scheduledPolicyItems|body|[[BackupComplianceScheduledPolicyItem](#schemabackupcompliancescheduledpolicyitem)]|false|List that contains the specifications for one scheduled policy.|

## Create One Restore Job of One Cluster

<a id="opIdcreateGroupClusterBackupRestoreJob"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/backup/restoreJobs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "deliveryType": "automated",
    "oplogInc": 1,
    "oplogTs": 1199145600,
    "pointInTimeUTCSeconds": 1199145600,
    "snapshotId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
    "targetClusterName": "string",
    "targetGroupId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/backup/restoreJobs`

Restores one snapshot of one cluster from the specified project. Atlas takes on-demand snapshots immediately and scheduled snapshots at regular intervals. If an on-demand snapshot with a status of `queued` or `inProgress` exists, before taking another snapshot, wait until Atlas completes processing the previously taken on-demand snapshot.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "deliveryType": "automated",
  "oplogInc": 1,
  "oplogTs": 1199145600,
  "pointInTimeUTCSeconds": 1199145600,
  "snapshotId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "targetClusterName": "string",
  "targetGroupId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8"
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-restore-job-of-one-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|body|body|[DiskBackupSnapshotRestoreJob](#schemadiskbackupsnapshotrestorejob)|true|Restores one snapshot of one cluster from the specified project.|
|» deliveryType|body|string|true|Human-readable label that categorizes the restore job to create.|
|» oplogInc|body|integer(int32)|false|Oplog operation number from which you want to restore this snapshot. This number represents the second part of an Oplog timestamp. The resource returns this parameter when `"deliveryType" : "pointInTime"` and `oplogTs` exceeds `0`.|
|» oplogTs|body|integer(int32)|false|Date and time from which you want to restore this snapshot. This parameter expresses this timestamp in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch. This number represents the first part of an Oplog timestamp. The resource returns this parameter when `"deliveryType" : "pointInTime"` and `oplogTs` exceeds `0`.|
|» pointInTimeUTCSeconds|body|integer(int32)|false|Date and time from which MongoDB Cloud restored this snapshot. This parameter expresses this timestamp in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch. The resource returns this parameter when `"deliveryType" : "pointInTime"` and `pointInTimeUTCSeconds` exceeds `0`.|
|» snapshotId|body|string|false|Unique 24-hexadecimal character string that identifies the snapshot.|
|» targetClusterName|body|string|false|Human-readable label that identifies the target cluster to which the restore job restores the snapshot. The resource returns this parameter when `"deliveryType":` `"automated"`. Required for `automated` and `pointInTime` restore types.|
|» targetGroupId|body|string|false|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the target project for the specified `targetClusterName`. Required for `automated` and `pointInTime` restore types.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» deliveryType|automated|
|» deliveryType|download|
|» deliveryType|pointInTime|

|body|body|[DiskBackupSnapshotSchedule](#schemadiskbackupsnapshotschedule)|true|Updates the cloud backup schedule for one cluster within the specified project.<br><br>**Note**: In the request body, provide only the fields that you want to update.|
|» autoExportEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud automatically exports Cloud Backup Snapshots to the Export Bucket.|
|» copyPolicyItemsEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether copy settings use `copyPolicyItems` instead of `frequencies`. When true, requests must supply `copyPolicyItems` and responses return `copyPolicyItems` only. When false or omitted, requests must supply `frequencies` and responses return `frequencies` only.|
|» copySettings|body|[[DiskBackupCopySetting](#schemadiskbackupcopysetting)]|false|List that contains a document for each copy setting item in the desired backup policy.|
|» deleteCopiedBackups|body|[[DeleteCopiedBackups](#schemadeletecopiedbackups)]|false|List that contains a document for each deleted copy setting whose backup copies you want to delete.|
|» deleteCopySnapshots|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to delete Snapshot copies that MongoDB Cloud took previously when their associated `copyPolicyItems` are removed from a `copySetting`. This option requires `copyPolicyItemsEnabled` to be true.|
|» deleteSnapshots|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to delete Snapshots that MongoDB Cloud took previously when deleting the associated backup policy.|
|» export|body|[AutoExportPolicyView](#schemaautoexportpolicyview)|false|Policy for automatically exporting Cloud Backup Snapshots.|
|» extraRetentionSettings|body|[[ExtraRetentionSetting](#schemaextraretentionsetting)]|false|List that contains a document for each extra retention setting item in the desired backup policy.|
|» policies|body|[[AdvancedDiskBackupSnapshotSchedulePolicy](#schemaadvanceddiskbackupsnapshotschedulepolicy)]|true|Rules set for this backup schedule.|
|» referenceHourOfDay|body|integer(int32)|false|Hour of day in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) that represents when MongoDB Cloud takes the Snapshot.|
|» referenceMinuteOfHour|body|integer(int32)|false|Minute of the `referenceHourOfDay` that represents when MongoDB Cloud takes the Snapshot.|
|» restoreWindowDays|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of previous days that you can restore back to with Continuous Cloud Backup accuracy. You must specify a positive, non-zero integer. This parameter applies to continuous Cloud Backups only.|
|» updateCopySnapshots|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to apply the retention changes for updated copy policy items to Snapshot copies that MongoDB Cloud took previously.|
|» updateSnapshots|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to apply the retention changes in the updated backup policy to Snapshots that MongoDB Cloud took previously.|
|» useOrgAndGroupNamesInExportPrefix|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to use organization and project names instead of organization and project UUIDs in the path to the metadata files that MongoDB Cloud uploads to your Export Bucket.|

## Take One On-Demand Snapshot

<a id="opIdtakeGroupClusterBackupSnapshots"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/backup/snapshots \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "retentionInDays": 1
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/backup/snapshots`

Takes one on-demand snapshot for the specified cluster. Atlas takes on-demand snapshots immediately and scheduled snapshots at regular intervals. If an on-demand snapshot with a status of `queued` or `inProgress` exists, before taking another snapshot, wait until Atlas completes processing the previously taken on-demand snapshot.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "retentionInDays": 1
}
```

<h3 id="take-one-on-demand-snapshot-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|body|body|[DiskBackupOnDemandSnapshotRequest](#schemadiskbackupondemandsnapshotrequest)|true|Takes one on-demand snapshot.|
|» description|body|string|false|Human-readable phrase or sentence that explains the purpose of the snapshot. The resource returns this parameter when `"status" : "onDemand"`.|
|» retentionInDays|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of days that MongoDB Cloud should retain the on-demand snapshot. Must be at least **1**.|

## Update Expiration Date for One Cloud Backup

<a id="opIdupdateGroupClusterBackupSnapshot"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/backup/snapshots/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "retentionUnit": "DAYS",
    "retentionValue": 5
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/backup/snapshots/{snapshotId}`

Changes the expiration date for one cloud backup snapshot for one cluster in the specified project, the requesting Service Account or API Key must have the Project Backup Manager role.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "retentionUnit": "DAYS",
  "retentionValue": 5
}
```

<h3 id="update-expiration-date-for-one-cloud-backup-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|snapshotId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the desired snapshot.|
|body|body|[BackupSnapshotRetention](#schemabackupsnapshotretention)|true|Changes the expiration date for one cloud backup snapshot for one cluster in the specified project.|
|» retentionUnit|body|string|true|Quantity of time in which MongoDB Cloud measures snapshot retention.|
|» retentionValue|body|integer(int32)|true|Number that indicates the amount of days, weeks, months, or years that MongoDB Cloud retains the snapshot. For less frequent policy items, MongoDB Cloud requires that you specify a value greater than or equal to the value specified for more frequent policy items. If the hourly policy item specifies a retention of two days, specify two days or greater for the retention of the weekly policy item.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» retentionUnit|DAYS|
|» retentionUnit|WEEKS|
|» retentionUnit|MONTHS|
|» retentionUnit|YEARS|

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/collectionRestoreJobs`

Creates one collection-level restore job for one cluster from the specified project. Collection-level restores allow restoring specific databases or collections from a snapshot or point-in-time.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "collectionSuffix": "string",
  "collections": [
    {
      "sourceNamespace": "string",
      "targetNamespace": "string"
    }
  ],
  "databaseSuffix": "string",
  "databases": [
    {
      "sourceNamespace": "string",
      "targetNamespace": "string"
    }
  ],
  "indexStrategy": "ALL",
  "oplogInc": 0,
  "oplogTs": 0,
  "pointInTimeUtcSeconds": 0,
  "snapshotId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "targetClusterName": "string",
  "targetGroupId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "writeStrategy": "CREATE_NEW"
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-collection-restore-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the source cluster for the restore.|
|body|body|[ApiAtlasCollectionRestoreJobRequest](#schemaapiatlascollectionrestorejobrequest)|true|Creates one collection-level restore job for one cluster from the specified project.|
|» collectionSuffix|body|string \| null|false|Optional suffix applied to restored collection names.|
|» collections|body|[[ApiAtlasRestoreCollectionNamespaceView](#schemaapiatlasrestorecollectionnamespaceview)]|false|List of collections to restore (up to 100 items).|
|» databaseSuffix|body|string \| null|false|Optional suffix applied to restored database names.|
|» databases|body|[[ApiAtlasRestoreDatabaseNamespaceView](#schemaapiatlasrestoredatabasenamespaceview)]|false|List of databases to restore (up to 100 items).|
|» indexStrategy|body|string|true|Strategy for restoring indexes (all, none, or all except TTL).|
|» oplogInc|body|integer(int32) \| null|false|Oplog increment for point-in-time restore.|
|» oplogTs|body|integer(int32) \| null|false|Oplog timestamp (seconds part) for point-in-time restore.|
|» pointInTimeUtcSeconds|body|integer(int32) \| null|false|Point-in-time restore time in seconds since UNIX epoch.|
|» snapshotId|body|string|false|ID of the snapshot to restore.|
|» targetClusterName|body|string|true|Target cluster name.|
|» targetGroupId|body|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the target group.|
|» writeStrategy|body|string|true|Strategy for writing data on the target (create as new or overwrite existing). With `OVERWRITE_EXISTING`, any writes to the affected databases or collections during the restore will be lost when the existing namespaces are dropped and replaced. To avoid data loss, stop writes to the affected namespaces before starting the restore.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» indexStrategy|ALL|
|» indexStrategy|NONE|
|» indexStrategy|ALL_EXCEPT_TTL|
|» writeStrategy|CREATE_NEW|
|» writeStrategy|OVERWRITE_EXISTING|

<a id="opIdlistGroupClusterCollectionRestoreJobCollections"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/collectionRestoreJobs/string/collections \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/collectionRestoreJobs/{jobId}/collections`

Returns all collection-level restore states for one collection restore job from the specified project. Note: If the restore job is in the INITIALIZING state, this endpoint returns an empty list because collection-level states have not yet been created.

<h3 id="return-all-collection-states-for-one-collection-restore-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|itemsPerPage|query|integer|false|Number of items that the response returns per page.|
|pageNum|query|integer|false|Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster with the collection restore job you want to return.|
|jobId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the collection restore job.|
|state|query|string|false|Collection-level state to filter by.|
|sourceNamespace|query|string|false|Source namespace to filter by (e.g. `db.collection`).|
|targetNamespace|query|string|false|Target namespace to filter by (e.g. `db.collection`).|

|state|FAILED|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-cloud-migration-service">Cloud Migration Service</h1>

Manages the Cloud Migration Service. Source organizations, projects, and MongoDB clusters reside on Cloud Manager or Ops Manager. Destination organizations, projects, and MongoDB clusters reside on MongoDB Cloud. Source databases can't use any authentication except SCRAM-SHA.

## Create One Migration for One Local Managed Cluster to MongoDB Atlas

<a id="opIdcreateGroupLiveMigration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/liveMigrations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "destination": {
      "clusterName": "string",
      "groupId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
      "hostnameSchemaType": "PUBLIC",
      "privateLinkId": "string"
    },
    "dropEnabled": true,
    "migrationHosts": [
      "vm001.example.com"
    ],
    "sharding": {
      "createSupportingIndexes": true,
      "shardingEntries": [
        {
          "collection": "string",
          "database": "string",
          "shardCollection": {
            "key": [
              {
                "property1": {},
                "property2": {}
              }
            ]
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    "source": {
      "caCertificatePath": "string",
      "clusterName": "string",
      "groupId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
      "managedAuthentication": true,
      "password": "string",
      "ssl": true,
      "username": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/liveMigrations`

Migrate one cluster that Cloud or Ops Manager manages to MongoDB Atlas.

 Please make sure to validate your migration before initiating it.

 You can use this API endpoint for push live migrations only. Your API Key must have the Organization Owner role to successfully call this resource.

 **NOTE**: Migrating time-series collections is not yet supported on MongoDB 6.0 or higher. Migrations on MongoDB 6.0 or higher will skip any time-series collections on the source cluster.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Cloud-Migration-Service/operation/validateMigration">Validate Migration</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "destination": {
    "clusterName": "string",
    "groupId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
    "hostnameSchemaType": "PUBLIC",
    "privateLinkId": "string"
  },
  "dropEnabled": true,
  "migrationHosts": [
    "vm001.example.com"
  ],
  "sharding": {
    "createSupportingIndexes": true,
    "shardingEntries": [
      {
        "collection": "string",
        "database": "string",
        "shardCollection": {
          "key": [
            {
              "property1": {},
              "property2": {}
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "source": {
    "caCertificatePath": "string",
    "clusterName": "string",
    "groupId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
    "managedAuthentication": true,
    "password": "string",
    "ssl": true,
    "username": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-migration-for-one-local-managed-cluster-to-mongodb-atlas-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|

`PUT /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/liveMigrations/{liveMigrationId}/cutover`

Cut over the migrated cluster to MongoDB Atlas. Confirm when the cut over completes. When the cut over completes, MongoDB Atlas completes the live migration process and stops synchronizing with the source cluster. Your API Key must have the Organization Owner role to successfully call this resource.

`POST /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/liveMigrations/linkTokens`

Create one link-token that contains all the information required to complete the link. MongoDB Atlas uses the link-token for push live migrations only. Live migration (push) allows you to securely push data from Cloud Manager or Ops Manager into MongoDB Atlas. Your API Key must have the Organization Owner role to successfully call this resource.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "accessListIps": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[TargetOrgRequest](#schematargetorgrequest)|true|IP address access list entries associated with the migration.|
|» accessListIps|body|[string]|false|IP address access list entries associated with the API key.|

## Create One Cloud Provider Access Role

<a id="opIdcreateGroupCloudProviderAccess"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/cloudProviderAccess \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "providerName": "AWS"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/cloudProviderAccess`

Creates one access role for the specified cloud provider. Some MongoDB Cloud features use these cloud provider access roles for authentication. For the GCP provider, if the project folder is not yet provisioned, Atlas will now create the role asynchronously. An intermediate role with status `IN_PROGRESS` will be returned, and the final service account will be provisioned. Once the GCP project is set up, subsequent requests will create the service account synchronously.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/cloud-provider-access/">Set Up Access to Cloud Providers</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "providerName": "AWS"
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-cloud-provider-access-role-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[CloudProviderAccessRoleRequest](#schemacloudprovideraccessrolerequest)|true|Creates one role for the specified cloud provider.|
|» providerName|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cloud provider of the role.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[CloudProviderAccessAWSIAMRoleRequest](#schemacloudprovideraccessawsiamrolerequest)|false|Details that describe the features linked to the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Identity and Access Management (IAM) role.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[CloudProviderAccessAzureServicePrincipalRequest](#schemacloudprovideraccessazureserviceprincipalrequest)|false|Details that describe the features linked to the Azure Service Principal.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[CloudProviderAccessGCPServiceAccountRequest](#schemacloudprovideraccessgcpserviceaccountrequest)|false|Details that describe the features linked to the GCP Service Account.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» providerName|AWS|
|» providerName|AZURE|
|» providerName|GCP|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "atlasAWSAccountArn": "arn:aws:iam::772401394250:role/my-test-aws-role",
  "atlasAssumedRoleExternalId": "feb2dfc7-f760-4288-a403-01c7c2345005",
  "authorizedDate": "2024-05-30T14:12:00Z",
```

## Return All Clusters in One Project

<a id="opIdlistGroupClusters"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters`

Returns the details for all clusters in the specific project to which you have access. Clusters contain a group of hosts that maintain the same data set. The response includes clusters with asymmetrically-sized shards. This feature is not  available for serverless clusters.

This endpoint can also be used on Flex clusters that were created using the [Create Cluster](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Clusters/operation/createCluster) endpoint or former M2/M5 clusters that have been migrated to Flex clusters until January 2026. Please use the List Flex Clusters endpoint for Flex clusters instead.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Flex-Clusters/operation/listFlexClusters">List Flex Clusters</a>

<h3 id="return-all-clusters-in-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|includeCount|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud calculates the total number of items for the response. When set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may skip an additional count operation. The response may still include `totalCount` when the count is available without additional calculation.|
|itemsPerPage|query|integer|false|Number of items that the response returns per page.|
|pageNum|query|integer|false|Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|includeDeletedWithRetainedBackups|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to return Clusters with retain backups.|
|Use-Effective-Instance-Fields|header|boolean|false|Controls how hardware specification fields are returned in the response. When set to true, returns the original client-specified values and provides separate effective fields showing current operational values. When false (default), hardware specification fields show current operational values directly. Primarily used for autoscaling compatibility.|

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters`

Creates one cluster in the specified project. Clusters contain a group of hosts that maintain the same data set. This resource can create clusters with asymmetrically-sized shards. Each project supports up to 25 database deployments. This feature is not available for serverless clusters.

Please note that using an `instanceSize` of M2 or M5 will create a Flex cluster instead. Support for the `instanceSize` of M2 or M5 will be discontinued in January 2026. We recommend using the Create Flex Cluster API for such configurations moving forward.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Flex-Clusters/operation/createFlexCluster">Create Flex Cluster</a>

<h3 id="create-one-cluster-in-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|Use-Effective-Instance-Fields|header|boolean|false|Controls how hardware specification fields are returned in the response after cluster creation. When set to true, returns the original client-specified values and provides separate effective fields showing current operational values. When false (default), hardware specification fields show current operational values directly. Primarily used for autoscaling compatibility.|
|Use-Effective-Fields-Replication-Specs|header|boolean|false|Controls how `replicationSpecs` fields are returned in the response. When set to `true`, stores the client's view of `replicationSpecs` and returns it in `replicationSpecs`, while the actual cluster state (including auto-scaled hardware and auto-added shards) is returned in `effectiveReplicationSpecs`. When `false` (default), `replicationSpecs` contains the actual cluster state.|
|body|body|[LegacyAtlasCluster](#schemalegacyatlascluster)|true|Cluster to create in this project.|
|» acceptDataRisksAndForceReplicaSetReconfig|body|string(date-time)|false|If reconfiguration is necessary to regain a primary due to a regional outage, submit this field alongside your topology reconfiguration to request a new regional outage resistant topology. Forced reconfigurations during an outage of the majority of electable nodes carry a risk of data loss if replicated writes (even majority committed writes) have not been replicated to the new primary node. MongoDB Atlas docs contain more information. To proceed with an operation which carries that risk, set `acceptDataRisksAndForceReplicaSetReconfig` to the current date. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|» advancedConfiguration|body|[ApiAtlasClusterAdvancedConfigurationView](#schemaapiatlasclusteradvancedconfigurationview)|false|Group of settings that configures a subset of the advanced configuration details.|
|» autoScaling|body|[ClusterAutoScalingSettings](#schemaclusterautoscalingsettings)|false|Range of instance sizes to which your cluster can scale.|
|» backupEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the cluster can perform backups. If set to `true`, the cluster can perform backups. You must set this value to `true` for NVMe clusters. Backup uses Cloud Backups for dedicated clusters and Shared Cluster Backups for tenant clusters. If set to `false`, the cluster doesn't use MongoDB Cloud backups.|
|» biConnector|body|[BiConnector](#schemabiconnector)|false|Settings needed to configure the MongoDB Connector for Business Intelligence for this cluster.|
|» clusterType|body|string|false|Configuration of nodes that comprise the cluster.|
|» configServerManagementMode|body|string|false|Config Server Management Mode for creating or updating a sharded cluster. When configured as `ATLAS_MANAGED`, Atlas may automatically switch the cluster's config server type for optimal performance and savings. When configured as `FIXED_TO_DEDICATED`, the cluster will always use a dedicated config server.|
|» databaseEdition|body|string|false|Available in Public Preview: Optional field that indicates whether your cluster will be Atlas INFINITE or CORE. This field applies only to flex and shared clusters. You can set it only when you create the cluster, or when you upgrade a flex cluster to a dedicated cluster. This value is immutable once the dedicated cluster exists; attempting to change it on an update request returns an error.|
|» deleteAfterCreationHours|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of hours after cluster creation that this cluster will be automatically deleted.<br><br>This field is used to derive `deleteAfterDate` relative to `createDate`.<br><br>When set to null or zero on cluster creation, the cluster will not be automatically deleted.<br><br>When set to a positive value on cluster creation, the cluster will be automatically deleted after the specified number of hours.<br><br>When updating this field on an existing (non-deleted) cluster, and this is set to null, then existing values are preserved for this & `deleteAfterDate`.<br><br>When updating this field on an existing (non-deleted) cluster, and this is set to zero, then `deleteAfterDate` is reset to null (disable auto deletion) regardless of previous configurations.<br><br>When updating this field on an existing (non-deleted) cluster, and this is set to a positive value, then `createDate` + `deleteAfterCreationHours` must be later than now else the field update is ignored and existing values are preserved for this & `deleteAfterDate`.|
|» diskSizeGB|body|number(double)|false|Storage capacity of instance data volumes expressed in gigabytes. Increase this number to add capacity.<br><br> This value is not configurable on M0/M2/M5 clusters.<br><br> MongoDB Cloud requires this parameter if you set `replicationSpecs`.<br><br> If you specify a disk size below the minimum (10 GB), this parameter defaults to the minimum disk size value. <br><br> Storage charge calculations depend on whether you choose the default value or a custom value.<br><br> The maximum value for disk storage cannot exceed 50 times the maximum RAM for the selected cluster. If you require more storage space, consider upgrading your cluster to a higher tier.|
|» diskWarmingMode|body|string|false|Disk warming mode selection.|
|» encryptionAtRestProvider|body|string|false|Cloud service provider that manages your customer keys to provide an additional layer of encryption at rest for the cluster. To enable customer key management for encryption at rest, the cluster `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].{type}Specs.instanceSize` setting must be `M10` or higher and `"backupEnabled" : false` or omitted entirely.|
|» globalClusterSelfManagedSharding|body|boolean|false|Set this field to configure the Sharding Management Mode when creating a new Global Cluster.<br><br>When set to false, the management mode is set to Atlas-Managed Sharding. This mode fully manages the sharding of your Global Cluster and is built to provide a seamless deployment experience.<br><br>When set to true, the management mode is set to Self-Managed Sharding. This mode leaves the management of shards in your hands and is built to provide an advanced and flexible deployment experience.<br><br>This setting cannot be changed once the cluster is deployed.|
|» labels|body|[[ComponentLabel](#schemacomponentlabel)]|false|**Deprecated.** Collection of key-value pairs between 1 to 255 characters in length that tag and categorize the cluster. The MongoDB Cloud console doesn't display your labels.<br><br>Cluster labels are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. We strongly recommend that you use Resource Tags instead.|
|» mongoDBMajorVersion|body|string|false|MongoDB major version of the cluster.<br><br>On creation: Choose from the available versions of MongoDB, or leave unspecified for the current recommended default in the MongoDB Cloud platform. The recommended version is a recent Long Term Support version. The default is not guaranteed to be the most recently released version throughout the entire release cycle. For versions available in a specific project, see the linked documentation or use the API endpoint for [project LTS versions endpoint](#tag/Projects/operation/getProjectLTSVersions).<br><br> On update: Increase version only by 1 major version at a time. If the cluster is pinned to a MongoDB feature compatibility version exactly one major version below the current MongoDB version, the MongoDB version can be downgraded to the previous major version.|
|» mongoDBVersion|body|string|false|Version of MongoDB that the cluster runs.|
|» name|body|string|false|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|» numShards|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of shards up to 50 to deploy for a sharded cluster. The resource returns `1` to indicate a replica set and values of `2` and higher to indicate a sharded cluster. The returned value equals the number of shards in the cluster.|
|» paused|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the cluster is paused.|
|» pitEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the cluster uses continuous cloud backups.|
|» providerBackupEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the M10 or higher cluster can perform Cloud Backups. If set to `true`, the cluster can perform backups. If this and `backupEnabled` are set to `false`, the cluster doesn't use MongoDB Cloud backups.|
|» providerSettings|body|[ClusterProviderSettings](#schemaclusterprovidersettings)|false|Group of cloud provider settings that configure the provisioned MongoDB hosts.|
|» replicaSetScalingStrategy|body|string|false|Set this field to configure the replica set scaling mode for your cluster.<br><br>By default, Atlas scales under `WORKLOAD_TYPE`. This mode allows Atlas to scale your analytics nodes in parallel to your operational nodes.<br><br>When configured as `SEQUENTIAL`, Atlas scales all nodes sequentially. This mode is intended for steady-state workloads and applications performing latency-sensitive secondary reads.<br><br>When configured as `NODE_TYPE`, Atlas scales your electable nodes in parallel with your read-only and analytics nodes. This mode is intended for large, dynamic workloads requiring frequent and timely cluster tier scaling. This is the fastest scaling strategy, but it might impact latency of workloads when performing extensive secondary reads.|
|» replicationFactor|body|integer(int32)|false|**Deprecated.** Number of members that belong to the replica set. Each member retains a copy of your databases, providing high availability and data redundancy. Use `replicationSpecs` instead.|
|» replicationSpec|body|object|false|Physical location where MongoDB Cloud provisions cluster nodes.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[RegionSpec](#schemaregionspec)|false|Physical location where MongoDB Cloud provisions cluster nodes.|
|» replicationSpecs|body|[[LegacyReplicationSpec](#schemalegacyreplicationspec)]|false|List of settings that configure your cluster regions.<br><br>- For Global Clusters, each object in the array represents one zone where MongoDB Cloud deploys your clusters nodes.<br>- For non-Global sharded clusters and replica sets, the single object represents where MongoDB Cloud deploys your clusters nodes.|
|» rootCertType|body|string|false|Root Certificate Authority that MongoDB Atlas cluster uses. MongoDB Cloud supports Internet Security Research Group.|
|» tags|body|[[ResourceTag](#schemaresourcetag)]|false|List that contains key-value pairs between 1 to 255 characters in length for tagging and categorizing the cluster.|
|» terminationProtectionEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether termination protection is enabled on the cluster. If set to `true`, MongoDB Cloud won't delete the cluster. If set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud will delete the cluster.|
|» versionReleaseSystem|body|string|false|Method by which the cluster maintains the MongoDB versions. If value is `CONTINUOUS`, you must not specify `mongoDBMajorVersion`.|

## Return One Cluster from One Project

<a id="opIdgetGroupCluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}`

Returns the details for one cluster in the specified project. Clusters contain a group of hosts that maintain the same data set. The response includes clusters with asymmetrically-sized shards. This feature is not available for serverless clusters.

This endpoint can also be used on Flex clusters that were created using the [Create Cluster](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Clusters/operation/createCluster) endpoint or former M2/M5 clusters that have been migrated to Flex clusters until January 2026. Please use the Get Flex Cluster endpoint for Flex clusters instead.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Flex-Clusters/operation/getFlexCluster">Get Flex Cluster</a>
