|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies this cluster.|
|Use-Effective-Instance-Fields|header|boolean|false|Controls how hardware specification fields are returned in the response. When set to true, returns the original client-specified values and provides separate effective fields showing current operational values. When false (default), hardware specification fields show current operational values directly. Primarily used for autoscaling compatibility.|
|Use-Effective-Fields-Replication-Specs|header|boolean|false|Controls how `replicationSpecs` are returned in the response. When set to `true`, returns the client-specified view in `replicationSpecs` and the actual cluster state in `effectiveReplicationSpecs`. When `false` (default), `replicationSpecs` contains the actual cluster state.|

## Remove One Cluster from One Project

<a id="opIddeleteGroupCluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}`

Removes one cluster from the specified project. The cluster must have termination protection disabled in order to be deleted. This feature is not available for serverless clusters.

This endpoint can also be used on Flex clusters that were created using the [Create Cluster](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Clusters/operation/createCluster) endpoint or former M2/M5 clusters that have been migrated to Flex clusters until January 2026. Please use the Delete Flex Cluster endpoint for Flex clusters instead.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Flex-Clusters/operation/deleteFlexCluster">Delete Flex Cluster</a>

<h3 id="remove-one-cluster-from-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|retainBackups|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to retain backup snapshots for the deleted dedicated cluster.|

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}`

Updates the details for one cluster in the specified project. Clusters contain a group of hosts that maintain the same data set. This resource can update clusters with asymmetrically-sized shards. To update a cluster's termination protection, the requesting Service Account or API Key must have the Project Owner role. For all other updates, the requesting Service Account or API Key must have the Project Cluster Manager role, the Project Cluster Resilience Tester role, or the Project Replica Set Manager role. You can't modify a paused cluster (`paused : true`). You must call this endpoint to set `paused : false`. After this endpoint responds with `paused : false`, you can call it again with the changes you want to make to the cluster. This feature is not available for serverless clusters.

<h3 id="update-one-cluster-in-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|Use-Effective-Instance-Fields|header|boolean|false|Controls how hardware specification fields are returned in the response after cluster updates. When set to true, returns the original client-specified values and provides separate effective fields showing current operational values. When false (default), hardware specification fields show current operational values directly. Note: When using this header with autoscaling enabled, MongoDB ignores `replicationSpecs` changes during updates. To intentionally override the `replicationSpecs`, disable this header.|
|Use-Effective-Fields-Replication-Specs|header|boolean|false|Controls how `replicationSpecs` fields are returned in the response. When set to `true`, stores the client's view of `replicationSpecs` and returns it in `replicationSpecs`, while the actual cluster state (including auto-scaled hardware and auto-added shards) is returned in `effectiveReplicationSpecs`. When `false` (default), `replicationSpecs` contains the actual cluster state.|
|body|body|[LegacyAtlasCluster](#schemalegacyatlascluster)|true|Cluster to update in the specified project.|
|» acceptDataRisksAndForceReplicaSetReconfig|body|string(date-time)|false|If reconfiguration is necessary to regain a primary due to a regional outage, submit this field alongside your topology reconfiguration to request a new regional outage resistant topology. Forced reconfigurations during an outage of the majority of electable nodes carry a risk of data loss if replicated writes (even majority committed writes) have not been replicated to the new primary node. MongoDB Atlas docs contain more information. To proceed with an operation which carries that risk, set `acceptDataRisksAndForceReplicaSetReconfig` to the current date. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|» advancedConfiguration|body|[ApiAtlasClusterAdvancedConfigurationView](#schemaapiatlasclusteradvancedconfigurationview)|false|Group of settings that configures a subset of the advanced configuration details.|
|» autoScaling|body|[ClusterAutoScalingSettings](#schemaclusterautoscalingsettings)|false|Range of instance sizes to which your cluster can scale.|
|» backupEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the cluster can perform backups. If set to `true`, the cluster can perform backups. You must set this value to `true` for NVMe clusters. Backup uses Cloud Backups for dedicated clusters and Shared Cluster Backups for tenant clusters. If set to `false`, the cluster doesn't use MongoDB Cloud backups.|
|» biConnector|body|[BiConnector](#schemabiconnector)|false|Settings needed to configure the MongoDB Connector for Business Intelligence for this cluster.|
|» clusterType|body|string|false|Configuration of nodes that comprise the cluster.|
|» configServerManagementMode|body|string|false|Config Server Management Mode for creating or updating a sharded cluster. When configured as `ATLAS_MANAGED`, Atlas may automatically switch the cluster's config server type for optimal performance and savings. When configured as `FIXED_TO_DEDICATED`, the cluster will always use a dedicated config server.|
|» databaseEdition|body|string|false|Available in Public Preview: Optional field that indicates whether your cluster will be Atlas INFINITE or CORE. This field applies only to flex and shared clusters. You can set it only when you create the cluster, or when you upgrade a flex cluster to a dedicated cluster. This value is immutable once the dedicated cluster exists; attempting to change it on an update request returns an error.|
|» deleteAfterCreationHours|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of hours after cluster creation that this cluster will be automatically deleted.<br><br>This field is used to derive `deleteAfterDate` relative to `createDate`.<br><br>When set to null or zero on cluster creation, the cluster will not be automatically deleted.<br><br>When set to a positive value on cluster creation, the cluster will be automatically deleted after the specified number of hours.<br><br>When updating this field on an existing (non-deleted) cluster, and this is set to null, then existing values are preserved for this & `deleteAfterDate`.<br><br>When updating this field on an existing (non-deleted) cluster, and this is set to zero, then `deleteAfterDate` is reset to null (disable auto deletion) regardless of previous configurations.<br><br>When updating this field on an existing (non-deleted) cluster, and this is set to a positive value, then `createDate` + `deleteAfterCreationHours` must be later than now else the field update is ignored and existing values are preserved for this & `deleteAfterDate`.|
|» diskSizeGB|body|number(double)|false|Storage capacity of instance data volumes expressed in gigabytes. Increase this number to add capacity.<br><br> This value is not configurable on M0/M2/M5 clusters.<br><br> MongoDB Cloud requires this parameter if you set `replicationSpecs`.<br><br> If you specify a disk size below the minimum (10 GB), this parameter defaults to the minimum disk size value. <br><br> Storage charge calculations depend on whether you choose the default value or a custom value.<br><br> The maximum value for disk storage cannot exceed 50 times the maximum RAM for the selected cluster. If you require more storage space, consider upgrading your cluster to a higher tier.|
|» diskWarmingMode|body|string|false|Disk warming mode selection.|
|» encryptionAtRestProvider|body|string|false|Cloud service provider that manages your customer keys to provide an additional layer of encryption at rest for the cluster. To enable customer key management for encryption at rest, the cluster `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].{type}Specs.instanceSize` setting must be `M10` or higher and `"backupEnabled" : false` or omitted entirely.|
|» globalClusterSelfManagedSharding|body|boolean|false|Set this field to configure the Sharding Management Mode when creating a new Global Cluster.<br><br>When set to false, the management mode is set to Atlas-Managed Sharding. This mode fully manages the sharding of your Global Cluster and is built to provide a seamless deployment experience.<br><br>When set to true, the management mode is set to Self-Managed Sharding. This mode leaves the management of shards in your hands and is built to provide an advanced and flexible deployment experience.<br><br>This setting cannot be changed once the cluster is deployed.|
|» labels|body|[[ComponentLabel](#schemacomponentlabel)]|false|**Deprecated.** Collection of key-value pairs between 1 to 255 characters in length that tag and categorize the cluster. The MongoDB Cloud console doesn't display your labels.<br><br>Cluster labels are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. We strongly recommend that you use Resource Tags instead.|
|» mongoDBMajorVersion|body|string|false|MongoDB major version of the cluster.<br><br>On creation: Choose from the available versions of MongoDB, or leave unspecified for the current recommended default in the MongoDB Cloud platform. The recommended version is a recent Long Term Support version. The default is not guaranteed to be the most recently released version throughout the entire release cycle. For versions available in a specific project, see the linked documentation or use the API endpoint for [project LTS versions endpoint](#tag/Projects/operation/getProjectLTSVersions).<br><br> On update: Increase version only by 1 major version at a time. If the cluster is pinned to a MongoDB feature compatibility version exactly one major version below the current MongoDB version, the MongoDB version can be downgraded to the previous major version.|
|» mongoDBVersion|body|string|false|Version of MongoDB that the cluster runs.|
|» name|body|string|false|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|» numShards|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of shards up to 50 to deploy for a sharded cluster. The resource returns `1` to indicate a replica set and values of `2` and higher to indicate a sharded cluster. The returned value equals the number of shards in the cluster.|
|» paused|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the cluster is paused.|
|» pitEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the cluster uses continuous cloud backups.|
|» providerBackupEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the M10 or higher cluster can perform Cloud Backups. If set to `true`, the cluster can perform backups. If this and `backupEnabled` are set to `false`, the cluster doesn't use MongoDB Cloud backups.|
|» providerSettings|body|[ClusterProviderSettings](#schemaclusterprovidersettings)|false|Group of cloud provider settings that configure the provisioned MongoDB hosts.|
|» replicaSetScalingStrategy|body|string|false|Set this field to configure the replica set scaling mode for your cluster.<br><br>By default, Atlas scales under `WORKLOAD_TYPE`. This mode allows Atlas to scale your analytics nodes in parallel to your operational nodes.<br><br>When configured as `SEQUENTIAL`, Atlas scales all nodes sequentially. This mode is intended for steady-state workloads and applications performing latency-sensitive secondary reads.<br><br>When configured as `NODE_TYPE`, Atlas scales your electable nodes in parallel with your read-only and analytics nodes. This mode is intended for large, dynamic workloads requiring frequent and timely cluster tier scaling. This is the fastest scaling strategy, but it might impact latency of workloads when performing extensive secondary reads.|
|» replicationFactor|body|integer(int32)|false|**Deprecated.** Number of members that belong to the replica set. Each member retains a copy of your databases, providing high availability and data redundancy. Use `replicationSpecs` instead.|
|» replicationSpec|body|object|false|Physical location where MongoDB Cloud provisions cluster nodes.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[RegionSpec](#schemaregionspec)|false|Physical location where MongoDB Cloud provisions cluster nodes.|
|» replicationSpecs|body|[[LegacyReplicationSpec](#schemalegacyreplicationspec)]|false|List of settings that configure your cluster regions.<br><br>- For Global Clusters, each object in the array represents one zone where MongoDB Cloud deploys your clusters nodes.<br>- For non-Global sharded clusters and replica sets, the single object represents where MongoDB Cloud deploys your clusters nodes.|
|» rootCertType|body|string|false|Root Certificate Authority that MongoDB Atlas cluster uses. MongoDB Cloud supports Internet Security Research Group.|
|» tags|body|[[ResourceTag](#schemaresourcetag)]|false|List that contains key-value pairs between 1 to 255 characters in length for tagging and categorizing the cluster.|
|» terminationProtectionEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether termination protection is enabled on the cluster. If set to `true`, MongoDB Cloud won't delete the cluster. If set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud will delete the cluster.|
|» versionReleaseSystem|body|string|false|Method by which the cluster maintains the MongoDB versions. If value is `CONTINUOUS`, you must not specify `mongoDBMajorVersion`.|

|» clusterType|SHARDED|
|» clusterType|GEOSHARDED|

## Return Adaptive Settings for One Cluster

<a id="opIdgetGroupClusterAdaptiveSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/adaptiveSettings \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/adaptiveSettings`

Returns the Adaptive Settings for the specified cluster, including client-provided overrides and the effective settings derived from those overrides and Atlas-managed defaults. To use this resource, the requesting Service Account or API Key must have the Project Read Only role.

<h3 id="return-adaptive-settings-for-one-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|

## Update Adaptive Settings for One Cluster

<a id="opIdupdateGroupClusterAdaptiveSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/adaptiveSettings \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2025-03-12+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "adaptiveSettingsOverrides": {}
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/adaptiveSettings`

Updates the client-provided Adaptive Settings overrides for the specified cluster and returns the resulting Adaptive Settings, including the effective settings derived from those overrides and Atlas-managed defaults. To use this resource, the requesting Service Account or API Key must have the Project Owner role.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "adaptiveSettingsOverrides": {}
}
```

<h3 id="update-adaptive-settings-for-one-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|body|body|[AdaptiveSettingsUpdateRequest](#schemaadaptivesettingsupdaterequest)|true|Adaptive Settings overrides to apply to the specified cluster. The supplied `adaptiveSettingsOverrides` map fully replaces the existing overrides: any override omitted from the map returns to its Atlas-managed default. Omitting the `adaptiveSettingsOverrides` field entirely preserves the existing overrides, an empty map clears all overrides, and `null` resets the field and omits it from responses until it is set again.|
|» adaptiveSettingsOverrides|body|[AdaptiveSettingsOverrides](#schemaadaptivesettingsoverrides)|false|Map of customer-specified overrides for Adaptive Settings, applied on a best-effort basis. Each supported entry that you specify in this object takes precedence over the corresponding Atlas-managed default. For example, if a setting is enabled by default, you can add an override to disable it for your cluster.|

```bash
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/privateEndpointConnectionStrings`

Creates one private endpoint connection string for the specified cluster. The new record is returned with `status = PENDING`; MongoDB Cloud publishes the DNS records asynchronously, so poll the record until it reports `AVAILABLE` before connecting with it.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "reporting-vpc",
  "optimizedModeEnabled": false,
  "privateEndpointIds": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-private-endpoint-connection-string-for-one-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|body|body|[PrivateEndpointConnectionStringCreateRequest](#schemaprivateendpointconnectionstringcreaterequest)|true|Private endpoint connection string to create.|
|» name|body|string|true|Human-readable label of at most 64 characters that identifies this private endpoint connection string. You can change this label without changing the connection string.|
|» optimizedModeEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether this private endpoint connection string uses the optimized load-balanced mode. This mode requires a sharded cluster and a private endpoint selection that satisfies the optimized connection string requirements.|
|» privateEndpointIds|body|[string]|true|Set of private endpoints that this connection string covers. MongoDB Cloud stores this set as a snapshot of your selection and never adds newly created private endpoints to it. The set accepts at most one private endpoint per cloud provider region, and can include private endpoints that the cluster does not use yet. Order is not significant and MongoDB Cloud rejects duplicate values.|

Only `name` and `privateEndpointIds` can change, and each one you omit keeps its current value. An imported record cannot be updated, and a request that carries a connection method property, a published field, or a lifecycle field is rejected.

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/processArgs`

Updates the advanced configuration details for one cluster in the specified project. Clusters contain a group of hosts that maintain the same data set. Advanced configuration details include the read/write concern, index and oplog limits, and other database settings. This feature isn't available for `M0` free clusters, `M2` and `M5` shared-tier clusters, flex clusters, or serverless clusters.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/global-clusters/">Global Clusters</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "changeStreamOptionsPreAndPostImagesExpireAfterSeconds": -1,
  "chunkMigrationConcurrency": 0,
  "customOpensslCipherConfigTls12": [
    "TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384"
  ],
  "customOpensslCipherConfigTls13": [
    "TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384"
  ],
  "defaultMaxTimeMS": 0,
  "defaultReadConcern": "available",
  "defaultWriteConcern": "string",
  "failIndexKeyTooLong": true,
  "javascriptEnabled": true,
  "minimumEnabledTlsProtocol": "TLS1_0",
  "noTableScan": true,
  "oplogMinRetentionHours": 0,
  "oplogSizeMB": 0,
  "queryStatsLogVerbosity": 0,
  "sampleRefreshIntervalBIConnector": 0,
  "sampleSizeBIConnector": 0,
  "tlsCipherConfigMode": "CUSTOM",
  "transactionLifetimeLimitSeconds": 1
}
```

<h3 id="update-advanced-configuration-options-for-one-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|body|body|[ClusterDescriptionProcessArgs](#schemaclusterdescriptionprocessargs)|true|Advanced configuration details to add for one cluster in the specified project.|
|» changeStreamOptionsPreAndPostImagesExpireAfterSeconds|body|integer(int32)|false|The minimum pre- and post-image retention time in seconds.|
|» chunkMigrationConcurrency|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of threads on the source shard and the receiving shard for chunk migration. The number of threads should not exceed the half the total number of CPU cores in the sharded cluster.|
|» customOpensslCipherConfigTls12|body|[string]|false|The custom OpenSSL cipher suite list for TLS 1.2. Requires `tlsCipherConfigMode` = `CUSTOM`; when `tlsCipherConfigMode` is omitted, supplying a non-empty list infers `CUSTOM`.|
|» customOpensslCipherConfigTls13|body|[string]|false|The custom OpenSSL cipher suite list for TLS 1.3. Requires `tlsCipherConfigMode` = `CUSTOM`; when `tlsCipherConfigMode` is omitted, supplying a non-empty list infers `CUSTOM`.|
|» defaultMaxTimeMS|body|integer(int32)|false|Default time limit in milliseconds for individual read operations to complete.|
|» defaultReadConcern|body|string|false|Default level of acknowledgment requested from MongoDB for read operations set for this cluster.<br><br>MongoDB 4.4 clusters default to `available`. MongoDB 5.0 and later clusters default to `local`.|
|» defaultWriteConcern|body|string|false|Default level of acknowledgment requested from MongoDB for write operations when none is specified by the driver.|
|» failIndexKeyTooLong|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Flag that indicates whether you can insert or update documents where all indexed entries don't exceed 1024 bytes. If you set this to false, [mongod](https://docs.mongodb.com/upcoming/reference/program/mongod/#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) writes documents that exceed this limit but doesn't index them. This parameter has been removed as of [MongoDB 4.4](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters/#mongodb-parameter-param.failIndexKeyTooLong).|
|» javascriptEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the cluster allows execution of operations that perform server-side executions of JavaScript. When using 8.0+, we recommend disabling server-side JavaScript and using operators of aggregation pipeline as more performant alternative.|
|» minimumEnabledTlsProtocol|body|string|false|Minimum Transport Layer Security (TLS) version that the cluster accepts for incoming connections. Clusters using TLS 1.0 or 1.1 should consider setting TLS 1.2 as the minimum TLS protocol version.|
|» noTableScan|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the cluster disables executing any query that requires a collection scan to return results.|
|» oplogMinRetentionHours|body|number(double) \| null|false|Minimum retention window for cluster's oplog expressed in hours. A value of null indicates that the cluster uses the default minimum oplog window that MongoDB Cloud calculates.|
|» oplogSizeMB|body|integer(int32) \| null|false|Storage limit of cluster's oplog expressed in megabytes. A value of null indicates that the cluster uses the default oplog size that MongoDB Cloud calculates.|
|» queryStatsLogVerbosity|body|integer(int32)|false|May be set to 1 (disabled) or 3 (enabled). When set to 3, Atlas will include redacted and anonymized `$queryStats` output in MongoDB logs. `$queryStats` output does not contain literals or field values. Enabling this setting might impact the performance of your cluster.|
|» sampleRefreshIntervalBIConnector|body|integer(int32)|false|Interval in seconds at which the mongosqld process re-samples data to create its relational schema.|
|» sampleSizeBIConnector|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of documents per database to sample when gathering schema information.|
|» tlsCipherConfigMode|body|string|false|The TLS cipher suite configuration mode. The default mode uses the default cipher suites. The custom mode allows you to specify custom cipher suites for both TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.|
|» transactionLifetimeLimitSeconds|body|integer(int64)|false|Lifetime, in seconds, of multi-document transactions. Atlas considers the transactions that exceed this limit as expired and so aborts them through a periodic clean-up process.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» customOpensslCipherConfigTls12|TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384|
|» customOpensslCipherConfigTls12|TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256|
|» customOpensslCipherConfigTls13|TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384|
|» customOpensslCipherConfigTls13|TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256|
|» customOpensslCipherConfigTls13|TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256|
|» customOpensslCipherConfigTls13|TLS_AES_128_CCM_SHA256|
|» defaultReadConcern|local|
|» defaultReadConcern|available|
|» minimumEnabledTlsProtocol|TLS1_0|
|» minimumEnabledTlsProtocol|TLS1_1|
|» minimumEnabledTlsProtocol|TLS1_2|
|» minimumEnabledTlsProtocol|TLS1_3|
|» tlsCipherConfigMode|CUSTOM|
|» tlsCipherConfigMode|DEFAULT|

## Test Failover for One Cluster

<a id="opIdrestartGroupClusterPrimaries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/restartPrimaries \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/restartPrimaries`

Starts a failover test for the specified cluster in the specified project. Clusters contain a group of hosts that maintain the same data set. A failover test checks how MongoDB Cloud handles the failure of the cluster's primary node. During the test, MongoDB Cloud shuts down the primary node and elects a new primary.

Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|

## Pin Feature Compatibility Version for One Cluster in One Project

<a id="opIdpinGroupClusterFeatureCompatibilityVersion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string:pinFeatureCompatibilityVersion \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2024-05-30+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "expirationDate": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}:pinFeatureCompatibilityVersion`

Pins the Feature Compatibility Version (FCV) to the current MongoDB version and sets the pin expiration date. If an FCV pin already exists for the cluster, calling this method will only update the expiration date of the existing pin and will not re-pin the FCV.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "expirationDate": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="pin-feature-compatibility-version-for-one-cluster-in-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies this cluster.|
|body|body|[PinFCVView](#schemapinfcvview)|false|Optional request parameters for tuning FCV pinning configuration.|
|» expirationDate|body|string(date-time)|false|Expiration date of the fixed FCV. If not specified, the expiration date will default to 4 weeks from the date FCV was originally pinned. Note that this field cannot exceed 4 weeks from the pinned date. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/tenantUpgrade`

Upgrades a shared-tier cluster to a Flex or Dedicated (M10+) cluster in the specified project. Each project supports up to 25 clusters. 

This endpoint can also be used to upgrade Flex clusters that were created using the [Create Cluster](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Clusters/operation/createCluster) API or former M2/M5 clusters that have been migrated to Flex clusters, using `instanceSizeName` to “M2” or “M5” until January 2026. This functionality will be available until January 22, 2026, after which it will only be available for M0 clusters. Please use the Upgrade Flex Cluster endpoint instead.

<h3 id="upgrade-one-shared-tier-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[LegacyAtlasTenantClusterUpgradeRequest](#schemalegacyatlastenantclusterupgraderequest)|true|Details of the shared-tier cluster upgrade in the specified project.|
|» acceptDataRisksAndForceReplicaSetReconfig|body|string(date-time)|false|If reconfiguration is necessary to regain a primary due to a regional outage, submit this field alongside your topology reconfiguration to request a new regional outage resistant topology. Forced reconfigurations during an outage of the majority of electable nodes carry a risk of data loss if replicated writes (even majority committed writes) have not been replicated to the new primary node. MongoDB Atlas docs contain more information. To proceed with an operation which carries that risk, set `acceptDataRisksAndForceReplicaSetReconfig` to the current date. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|» advancedConfiguration|body|[ApiAtlasClusterAdvancedConfigurationView](#schemaapiatlasclusteradvancedconfigurationview)|false|Group of settings that configures a subset of the advanced configuration details.|
|» autoScaling|body|[ClusterAutoScalingSettings](#schemaclusterautoscalingsettings)|false|Range of instance sizes to which your cluster can scale.|
|» backupEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the cluster can perform backups. If set to `true`, the cluster can perform backups. You must set this value to `true` for NVMe clusters. Backup uses Cloud Backups for dedicated clusters and Shared Cluster Backups for tenant clusters. If set to `false`, the cluster doesn't use MongoDB Cloud backups.|
|» biConnector|body|[BiConnector](#schemabiconnector)|false|Settings needed to configure the MongoDB Connector for Business Intelligence for this cluster.|
|» clusterType|body|string|false|Configuration of nodes that comprise the cluster.|
|» configServerManagementMode|body|string|false|Config Server Management Mode for creating or updating a sharded cluster. When configured as `ATLAS_MANAGED`, Atlas may automatically switch the cluster's config server type for optimal performance and savings. When configured as `FIXED_TO_DEDICATED`, the cluster will always use a dedicated config server.|
|» databaseEdition|body|string|false|Available in Public Preview: Optional field that indicates whether your cluster will be Atlas INFINITE or CORE. This field applies only to flex and shared clusters. You can set it only when you create the cluster, or when you upgrade a flex cluster to a dedicated cluster. This value is immutable once the dedicated cluster exists; attempting to change it on an update request returns an error.|
|» deleteAfterCreationHours|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of hours after cluster creation that this cluster will be automatically deleted.<br><br>This field is used to derive `deleteAfterDate` relative to `createDate`.<br><br>When set to null or zero on cluster creation, the cluster will not be automatically deleted.<br><br>When set to a positive value on cluster creation, the cluster will be automatically deleted after the specified number of hours.<br><br>When updating this field on an existing (non-deleted) cluster, and this is set to null, then existing values are preserved for this & `deleteAfterDate`.<br><br>When updating this field on an existing (non-deleted) cluster, and this is set to zero, then `deleteAfterDate` is reset to null (disable auto deletion) regardless of previous configurations.<br><br>When updating this field on an existing (non-deleted) cluster, and this is set to a positive value, then `createDate` + `deleteAfterCreationHours` must be later than now else the field update is ignored and existing values are preserved for this & `deleteAfterDate`.|
|» diskSizeGB|body|number(double)|false|Storage capacity of instance data volumes expressed in gigabytes. Increase this number to add capacity.<br><br> This value is not configurable on M0/M2/M5 clusters.<br><br> MongoDB Cloud requires this parameter if you set `replicationSpecs`.<br><br> If you specify a disk size below the minimum (10 GB), this parameter defaults to the minimum disk size value. <br><br> Storage charge calculations depend on whether you choose the default value or a custom value.<br><br> The maximum value for disk storage cannot exceed 50 times the maximum RAM for the selected cluster. If you require more storage space, consider upgrading your cluster to a higher tier.|
|» diskWarmingMode|body|string|false|Disk warming mode selection.|
|» encryptionAtRestProvider|body|string|false|Cloud service provider that manages your customer keys to provide an additional layer of encryption at rest for the cluster. To enable customer key management for encryption at rest, the cluster `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].{type}Specs.instanceSize` setting must be `M10` or higher and `"backupEnabled" : false` or omitted entirely.|
|» globalClusterSelfManagedSharding|body|boolean|false|Set this field to configure the Sharding Management Mode when creating a new Global Cluster.<br><br>When set to false, the management mode is set to Atlas-Managed Sharding. This mode fully manages the sharding of your Global Cluster and is built to provide a seamless deployment experience.<br><br>When set to true, the management mode is set to Self-Managed Sharding. This mode leaves the management of shards in your hands and is built to provide an advanced and flexible deployment experience.<br><br>This setting cannot be changed once the cluster is deployed.|
|» labels|body|[[ComponentLabel](#schemacomponentlabel)]|false|**Deprecated.** Collection of key-value pairs between 1 to 255 characters in length that tag and categorize the cluster. The MongoDB Cloud console doesn't display your labels.<br><br>Cluster labels are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. We strongly recommend that you use Resource Tags instead.|
|» mongoDBMajorVersion|body|string|false|MongoDB major version of the cluster.<br><br>On creation: Choose from the available versions of MongoDB, or leave unspecified for the current recommended default in the MongoDB Cloud platform. The recommended version is a recent Long Term Support version. The default is not guaranteed to be the most recently released version throughout the entire release cycle. For versions available in a specific project, see the linked documentation or use the API endpoint for [project LTS versions endpoint](#tag/Projects/operation/getProjectLTSVersions).<br><br> On update: Increase version only by 1 major version at a time. If the cluster is pinned to a MongoDB feature compatibility version exactly one major version below the current MongoDB version, the MongoDB version can be downgraded to the previous major version.|
|» mongoDBVersion|body|string|false|Version of MongoDB that the cluster runs.|
|» name|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|» numShards|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of shards up to 50 to deploy for a sharded cluster. The resource returns `1` to indicate a replica set and values of `2` and higher to indicate a sharded cluster. The returned value equals the number of shards in the cluster.|
|» paused|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the cluster is paused.|
|» pitEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the cluster uses continuous cloud backups.|
|» providerBackupEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the M10 or higher cluster can perform Cloud Backups. If set to `true`, the cluster can perform backups. If this and `backupEnabled` are set to `false`, the cluster doesn't use MongoDB Cloud backups.|
|» providerSettings|body|[ClusterProviderSettings](#schemaclusterprovidersettings)|false|Group of cloud provider settings that configure the provisioned MongoDB hosts.|
|» replicaSetScalingStrategy|body|string|false|Set this field to configure the replica set scaling mode for your cluster.<br><br>By default, Atlas scales under `WORKLOAD_TYPE`. This mode allows Atlas to scale your analytics nodes in parallel to your operational nodes.<br><br>When configured as `SEQUENTIAL`, Atlas scales all nodes sequentially. This mode is intended for steady-state workloads and applications performing latency-sensitive secondary reads.<br><br>When configured as `NODE_TYPE`, Atlas scales your electable nodes in parallel with your read-only and analytics nodes. This mode is intended for large, dynamic workloads requiring frequent and timely cluster tier scaling. This is the fastest scaling strategy, but it might impact latency of workloads when performing extensive secondary reads.|
|» replicationFactor|body|integer(int32)|false|**Deprecated.** Number of members that belong to the replica set. Each member retains a copy of your databases, providing high availability and data redundancy. Use `replicationSpecs` instead.|
|» replicationSpec|body|object|false|Physical location where MongoDB Cloud provisions cluster nodes.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[RegionSpec](#schemaregionspec)|false|Physical location where MongoDB Cloud provisions cluster nodes.|
|» replicationSpecs|body|[[LegacyReplicationSpec](#schemalegacyreplicationspec)]|false|List of settings that configure your cluster regions.<br><br>- For Global Clusters, each object in the array represents one zone where MongoDB Cloud deploys your clusters nodes.<br>- For non-Global sharded clusters and replica sets, the single object represents where MongoDB Cloud deploys your clusters nodes.|
|» rootCertType|body|string|false|Root Certificate Authority that MongoDB Atlas cluster uses. MongoDB Cloud supports Internet Security Research Group.|
|» tags|body|[[ResourceTag](#schemaresourcetag)]|false|List that contains key-value pairs between 1 to 255 characters in length for tagging and categorizing the cluster.|
|» terminationProtectionEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether termination protection is enabled on the cluster. If set to `true`, MongoDB Cloud won't delete the cluster. If set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud will delete the cluster.|
|» versionReleaseSystem|body|string|false|Method by which the cluster maintains the MongoDB versions. If value is `CONTINUOUS`, you must not specify `mongoDBMajorVersion`.|

|» clusterType|SHARDED|
|» clusterType|GEOSHARDED|

## Upgrade One Shared-Tier Cluster to One Serverless Instance

<a id="opIdupgradeGroupClusterTenantUpgradeToServerless"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/tenantUpgradeToServerless \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "providerSettings": {
      "backingProviderName": "AWS",
      "providerName": "SERVERLESS",
      "regionName": "string"
    },
    "serverlessBackupOptions": {
      "serverlessContinuousBackupEnabled": true
    },
    "tags": [
      {
        "key": "string",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ],
    "terminationProtectionEnabled": false
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/tenantUpgradeToServerless`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

This endpoint has been deprecated as of February 2025 as we no longer support the creation of new serverless instances. Please use the Upgrade Flex Cluster endpoint to upgrade Flex clusters.

 Upgrades a shared-tier cluster to a serverless instance in the specified project.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Flex-Clusters/operation/upgradeFlexCluster">Upgrade Flex Cluster</a>

Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|

|» terminationProtectionEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether termination protection is enabled on the serverless instance. If set to `true`, MongoDB Cloud won't delete the serverless instance. If set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud will delete the serverless instance.|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-collection-level-metrics">Collection Level Metrics</h1>

Returns, adds, and edits pinned namespaces for the specified cluster or process. Also returns collection level latency metric data.

## Return Cluster-Level Query Latency

<a id="opIdlistGroupClusterCollStatMeasurements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/PRIMARY/mydb/mycoll/collStats/measurements \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/{clusterView}/{databaseName}/{collectionName}/collStats/measurements`

Get a list of the Coll Stats Latency cluster-level measurements for the given namespace.

<h3 id="return-cluster-level-query-latency-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster to retrieve metrics for.|
|clusterView|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster topology to retrieve metrics for.|
|databaseName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the database.|
|collectionName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the collection.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|metrics|query|[string]|false|List that contains the metrics that you want to retrieve for the associated data series. If you don't set this parameter, this resource returns data series for all Coll Stats Latency metrics.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud begins reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud stops reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|
|period|query|string|false|Duration over which Atlas reports the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 duration format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **start** and **end**.|

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/{clusterView}/collStats/namespaces`

|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud stops reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|
|period|query|string|false|Duration over which Atlas reports the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 duration format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **start** and **end**.|

## Return Host-Level Query Latency

<a id="opIdlistGroupProcessCollStatMeasurements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/processes/my.host.name.com%3A27017/mydb/mycoll/collStats/measurements \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/processes/{processId}/{databaseName}/{collectionName}/collStats/measurements`

Get a list of the Coll Stats Latency process-level measurements for the given namespace.

<h3 id="return-host-level-query-latency-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|processId|path|string|true|Combination of hostname and IANA port that serves the MongoDB process. The host must be the hostname, fully qualified domain name (FQDN), or Internet Protocol address (IPv4 or IPv6) of the host that runs the MongoDB process (mongod or mongos). The port must be the IANA port on which the MongoDB process listens for requests.|
|databaseName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the database.|
|collectionName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the collection.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|metrics|query|[string]|false|List that contains the metrics that you want to retrieve for the associated data series. If you don't set this parameter, this resource returns data series for all Coll Stats Latency metrics.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud begins reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud stops reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|
|period|query|string|false|Duration over which Atlas reports the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 duration format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **start** and **end**.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

|metrics|READS_LATENCY|
|metrics|AVERAGE_READS_LATENCY|
|metrics|READS_P50_VALUE|
|metrics|READS_P95_VALUE|
|metrics|READS_P99_VALUE|
|metrics|WRITES_OPS|
|metrics|WRITES_LATENCY|
|metrics|AVERAGE_WRITES_LATENCY|
|metrics|WRITES_P50_VALUE|
|metrics|WRITES_P95_VALUE|
|metrics|WRITES_P99_VALUE|
|metrics|COMMANDS_OPS|
|metrics|COMMANDS_LATENCY|
|metrics|AVERAGE_COMMANDS_LATENCY|
|metrics|COMMANDS_P50_VALUE|
|metrics|COMMANDS_P95_VALUE|
|metrics|COMMANDS_P99_VALUE|
|metrics|TOTAL_OPS|
|metrics|TOTAL_LATENCY|
|metrics|AVERAGE_TOTAL_OPS_LATENCY|
|metrics|TOTAL_OPS_P50_VALUE|
|metrics|TOTAL_OPS_P95_VALUE|
|metrics|TOTAL_OPS_P99_VALUE|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-custom-database-roles">Custom Database Roles</h1>

Returns, adds, edits, and removes custom database user privilege roles. Use custom roles to specify custom sets of actions that the MongoDB Cloud built-in roles can't describe. You define custom roles at the project level, for all clusters in the project. This resource supports a subset of MongoDB privilege actions. You can create a subset of custom role actions. To create a wider list of custom role actions, use the MongoDB Cloud user interface. Custom roles must include actions that all project's clusters support, and that are compatible with each MongoDB version that your project's clusters use. For example, if your project has MongoDB 4.2 clusters, you can't create custom roles that use actions introduced in MongoDB 4.4.

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-data-federation">Data Federation</h1>

Returns, adds, edits, and removes Federated Database Instances. This resource requires your project ID. Changes to federated database instance configurations can affect costs.

## Return All Federated Database Instances in One Project

<a id="opIdlistGroupDataFederation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/dataFederation \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/dataFederation`

Returns the details of all federated database instances in the specified project.

<h3 id="return-all-federated-database-instances-in-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. `GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/dataFederation/{tenantName}/queryLogs.gz`

## Create One Federated Database Instance and Online Archive Private Endpoint for One Project

<a id="opIdcreateGroupPrivateNetworkSettingEndpointId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/privateNetworkSettings/endpointIds \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "azureLinkId": "string",
    "comment": "string",
    "customerEndpointDNSName": "string",
    "customerEndpointIPAddress": "string",
    "endpointId": "string",
    "errorMessage": "string",
    "provider": "AWS",
    "region": "US_EAST_1",
    "status": "PENDING",
    "type": "DATA_LAKE"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/privateNetworkSettings/endpointIds`

Adds one private endpoint for Federated Database Instances and Online Archives to the specified projects. If the endpoint ID already exists and the associated comment is unchanged, Atlas Data Federation makes no change to the endpoint ID list. If the endpoint ID already exists and the associated comment is changed, Atlas Data Federation updates the comment value only in the endpoint ID list. If the endpoint ID doesn't exist, Atlas Data Federation appends the new endpoint to the list of endpoints in the endpoint ID list. Each region has an associated service name for the various endpoints. For the latest list of supported regions and their service names, see the external documentation.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/tutorial/config-private-endpoint/">Atlas Data Federation Regions and Service Names</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "azureLinkId": "string",
  "comment": "string",
  "customerEndpointDNSName": "string",
  "customerEndpointIPAddress": "string",
  "endpointId": "string",
  "errorMessage": "string",
  "provider": "AWS",
  "region": "US_EAST_1",
  "status": "PENDING",
  "type": "DATA_LAKE"
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-federated-database-instance-and-online-archive-private-endpoint-for-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[PrivateNetworkEndpointIdEntry](#schemaprivatenetworkendpointidentry)|true|Private endpoint for Federated Database Instances and Online Archives to add to the specified project.|
|» azureLinkId|body|string|false|Link ID that identifies the Azure private endpoint connection.|
|» comment|body|string|false|Human-readable string to associate with this private endpoint.|
|» customerEndpointDNSName|body|string|false|Human-readable label to identify customer's VPC endpoint DNS name. If defined, you must also specify a value for `region`.|
|» customerEndpointIPAddress|body|string|false|IP address used to connect to the Azure private endpoint.|
|» endpointId|body|string|true|Unique string that identifies the private endpoint. For AWS, this is a 22-character alphanumeric string in the format `vpce-<17 hex characters>`. For Azure, this is the full resource ID in the format `/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints/{endpointName}`.|
|» errorMessage|body|string|false|Error message describing a failure approving the private endpoint request.|
|» provider|body|string|false|Human-readable label that identifies the cloud service provider. Atlas Data Lake supports Amazon Web Services and Azure.|
|» region|body|string|false|Human-readable label to identify the region of customer's VPC endpoint. If defined, you must also specify a value for `customerEndpointDNSName`.|
|» status|body|string|false|Status of the private endpoint connection request.|
|» type|body|string|false|Human-readable label that identifies the resource type associated with this private endpoint.|

## Create One Database User in One Project

<a id="opIdcreateGroupDatabaseUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/databaseUsers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "awsIAMType": "USER",
    "databaseName": "$external",
    "groupId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
    "roles": [
      {
        "databaseName": "sales",
        "roleName": "readWrite"
      },
      {
        "databaseName": "marketing",
        "roleName": "read"
      }
    ],
    "scopes": [
      {
        "name": "myCluster",
        "type": "CLUSTER"
      }
    ],
    "username": "arn:aws:iam::358363220050:user/mongodb-aws-iam-auth-test-user"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/databaseUsers`

Creates one database user in the specified project. This MongoDB Cloud supports a default limit of 100 and a maximum of 900 database users per project. If you require more than 900 database users on a project, contact Support.

<a href="https://cloud.mongodb.com/support">Contact MongoDB Support</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "awsIAMType": "USER",
  "databaseName": "$external",
  "groupId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "roles": [
    {
      "databaseName": "sales",
      "roleName": "readWrite"
    },
    {
      "databaseName": "marketing",
      "roleName": "read"
    }
  ],
  "scopes": [
    {
      "name": "myCluster",
      "type": "CLUSTER"
    }
  ],
  "username": "arn:aws:iam::358363220050:user/mongodb-aws-iam-auth-test-user"
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-database-user-in-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[CloudDatabaseUser](#schemaclouddatabaseuser)|true|Creates one database user in the specified project.|
|» awsIAMType|body|string|false|Human-readable label that indicates whether the new database user authenticates with the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Identity and Access Management (IAM) credentials associated with the user or the user's role.|
|» databaseName|body|string|true|The database against which the database user authenticates. Database users must provide both a username and authentication database to log into MongoDB. If the user authenticates with AWS IAM, x.509, LDAP, or OIDC Workload this value should be `$external`. If the user authenticates with SCRAM-SHA or OIDC Workforce, this value should be `admin`.|
|» deleteAfterDate|body|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud deletes the user. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC and can include the time zone designation. You must specify a future date that falls within one week of making the Application Programming Interface (API) request.|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of this database user.|
|» groupId|body|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the project.|
|» labels|body|[[ComponentLabel](#schemacomponentlabel)]|false|List that contains the key-value pairs for tagging and categorizing the MongoDB database user. The labels that you define do not appear in the console.|
|» ldapAuthType|body|string|false|Part of the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) record that the database uses to authenticate this database user on the LDAP host.|
|» oidcAuthType|body|string|false|Human-readable label that indicates whether the new database user or group authenticates with OIDC federated authentication. To create a federated authentication user, specify the value of USER in this field. To create a federated authentication group, specify the value of `IDP_GROUP` in this field.|
|» password|body|string|false|Alphanumeric string that authenticates this database user against the database specified in `databaseName`. To authenticate with SCRAM-SHA, you must specify this parameter. This parameter doesn't appear in this response.|
|» roles|body|[[DatabaseUserRole](#schemadatabaseuserrole)]|true|List that provides the pairings of one role with one applicable database.|
|» scopes|body|[[UserScope](#schemauserscope)]|false|List that contains clusters, MongoDB Atlas Data Lakes, and MongoDB Atlas Streams Workspaces that this database user can access. If omitted, MongoDB Cloud grants the database user access to all the clusters, MongoDB Atlas Data Lakes, and MongoDB Atlas Streams Workspaces in the project.|

|» labels|body|[[ComponentLabel](#schemacomponentlabel)]|false|List that contains the key-value pairs for tagging and categorizing the MongoDB database user. The labels that you define do not appear in the console.|
|» ldapAuthType|body|string|false|Part of the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) record that the database uses to authenticate this database user on the LDAP host.|
|» oidcAuthType|body|string|false|Human-readable label that indicates whether the new database user or group authenticates with OIDC federated authentication. To create a federated authentication user, specify the value of USER in this field. To create a federated authentication group, specify the value of `IDP_GROUP` in this field.|
|» password|body|string|false|Alphanumeric string that authenticates this database user against the database specified in `databaseName`. To authenticate with SCRAM-SHA, you must specify this parameter. This parameter doesn't appear in this response.|
|» roles|body|[[DatabaseUserRole](#schemadatabaseuserrole)]|true|List that provides the pairings of one role with one applicable database.|
|» scopes|body|[[UserScope](#schemauserscope)]|false|List that contains clusters, MongoDB Atlas Data Lakes, and MongoDB Atlas Streams Workspaces that this database user can access. If omitted, MongoDB Cloud grants the database user access to all the clusters, MongoDB Atlas Data Lakes, and MongoDB Atlas Streams Workspaces in the project.|
|» username|body|string|true|Human-readable label that represents the user that authenticates to MongoDB. The format of this label depends on the method of authentication:<br><br>\| Authentication Method \| Parameter Needed \| Parameter Value \| username Format \|<br>\|---\|---\|---\|---\|<br>\| AWS IAM \| `awsIAMType` \| `ROLE` \| <abbr title="Amazon Resource Name">ARN</abbr> \|<br>\| AWS IAM \| `awsIAMType` \| `USER` \| <abbr title="Amazon Resource Name">ARN</abbr> \|<br>\| x.509 \| `x509Type` \| `CUSTOMER` \| [RFC 2253](https://tools.ietf.org/html/2253) Distinguished Name \|<br>\| x.509 \| `x509Type` \| `MANAGED` \| [RFC 2253](https://tools.ietf.org/html/2253) Distinguished Name \|<br>\| LDAP \| `ldapAuthType` \| `USER` \| [RFC 2253](https://tools.ietf.org/html/2253) Distinguished Name \|<br>\| LDAP \| `ldapAuthType` \| `GROUP` \| [RFC 2253](https://tools.ietf.org/html/2253) Distinguished Name \|<br>\| OIDC Workforce \| `oidcAuthType` \| `IDP_GROUP` \| Atlas OIDC IdP ID (found in federation settings), followed by a '/', followed by the IdP group name \|<br>\| OIDC Workload \| `oidcAuthType` \| `USER` \| Atlas OIDC IdP ID (found in federation settings), followed by a '/', followed by the IdP user name \|<br>\| SCRAM-SHA \| `awsIAMType`, `x509Type`, `ldapAuthType`, `oidcAuthType` \| `NONE` \| Alphanumeric string \|<br>|
|» x509Type|body|string|false|X.509 method that MongoDB Cloud uses to authenticate the database user.<br><br>- For application-managed X.509, specify `MANAGED`.<br>- For self-managed X.509, specify `CUSTOMER`.<br><br>Users created with the `CUSTOMER` method require a Common Name (CN) in the **username** parameter. You must create externally authenticated users on the `$external` database.|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-encryption-at-rest-using-customer-key-management">Encryption at Rest using Customer Key Management</h1>

Returns and edits the Encryption at Rest using Customer Key Management configuration. MongoDB Cloud encrypts all storage whether or not you use your own key management.

## Return One Configuration for Encryption at Rest Using Customer-Managed Keys for One Project

<a id="opIdgetGroupEncryptionAtRest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/encryptionAtRest \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/encryptionAtRest`

Returns the configuration for encryption at rest using the keys you manage through your cloud provider. MongoDB Cloud encrypts all storage even if you don't use your own key management.

**LIMITED TO M10 OR GREATER:** MongoDB Cloud limits this feature to dedicated cluster tiers of M10 and greater.

<h3 id="return-one-configuration-for-encryption-at-rest-using-customer-managed-keys-for-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
