## Update One Maintenance Window for One Project

<a id="opIdupdateGroupMaintenanceWindow"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/maintenanceWindow \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "autoDeferOnceEnabled": true,
    "dayOfWeek": 1,
    "hourOfDay": 0,
    "protectedHours": {
      "endHourOfDay": 0,
      "startHourOfDay": 0
    },
    "startASAP": true,
    "waveAssignment": 1
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/maintenanceWindow`

Updates the maintenance window for the specified project. Urgent maintenance activities such as security patches can't wait for your chosen window. MongoDB Cloud starts those maintenance activities when needed. After you schedule maintenance for your cluster, you can't change your maintenance window until the current maintenance efforts complete. The maintenance procedure that MongoDB Cloud performs requires at least one replica set election during the maintenance window per replica set. Maintenance always begins as close to the scheduled hour as possible, but in-progress cluster updates or unexpected system issues could delay the start time. Updating the maintenance window will reset any maintenance deferrals for this project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "autoDeferOnceEnabled": true,
  "dayOfWeek": 1,
  "hourOfDay": 0,
  "protectedHours": {
    "endHourOfDay": 0,
    "startHourOfDay": 0
  },
  "startASAP": true,
  "waveAssignment": 1
}
```

<h3 id="update-one-maintenance-window-for-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|body|body|[GroupMaintenanceWindow](#schemagroupmaintenancewindow)|true|Updates the maintenance window for the specified project.|
|» autoDeferOnceEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud should defer all maintenance windows for one week after you enable them. This setting controls the same underlying auto-deferral feature as the `/maintenanceWindow/autoDefer` endpoint. Use either this field (to set a specific value) or that endpoint (to toggle the current value). For most use cases, this field in the PATCH request is preferred because it allows setting an explicit value rather than toggling.|
|» dayOfWeek|body|integer(int32)|false|One-based integer that represents the day of the week, in the project's configured time zone (see `timeZoneId`), that the maintenance window starts.<br><br>- `1`: Sunday.<br>- `2`: Monday.<br>- `3`: Tuesday.<br>- `4`: Wednesday.<br>- `5`: Thursday.<br>- `6`: Friday.<br>- `7`: Saturday.|
|» hourOfDay|body|integer(int32)|false|Zero-based integer that represents the hour of the day, in the project's configured time zone (see `timeZoneId`), that the maintenance window starts according to a 24-hour clock. Use `0` for midnight and `12` for noon. If you haven't changed your project's time zone, this defaults to UTC.|
|» protectedHours|body|[ProtectedHours](#schemaprotectedhours)|false|Defines the a window where maintenance will not begin within.|
|» startASAP|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud starts the maintenance window immediately upon receiving this request. To start the maintenance window immediately for your project, MongoDB Cloud must have maintenance scheduled and you must set a maintenance window. This flag resets to `false` after MongoDB Cloud completes maintenance.|
|» waveAssignment|body|integer(int32) \| null|false|Maintenance wave explicitly assigned to this project. Always returned in GET responses when a value has been set, regardless of the organization's `effectiveWaveAssignmentMode`. When the mode is `ENV_TAG_MAPPING`, this stored assignment is preserved but not used for scheduling — the effective wave is derived from environment tags instead. Not editable when the mode is `ENV_TAG_MAPPING`. Switching back to `MANUAL` restores this value as the effective wave. Must be between 1 and 3, inclusive. Pass `null` to clear an explicit assignment.|

## Toggle Automatic Deferral of Maintenance for One Project

<a id="opIdtoggleGroupMaintenanceWindowAutoDefer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/maintenanceWindow/autoDefer \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/maintenanceWindow/autoDefer`

Toggles automatic deferral of the maintenance window for the specified project. When automatic deferral is enabled, all maintenance windows are deferred for one week. This endpoint controls the same underlying feature as the `autoDeferOnceEnabled` field in the PATCH `/maintenanceWindow` endpoint. The difference is that this endpoint toggles the current value (switches from enabled to disabled or vice versa), while the `autoDeferOnceEnabled` field allows you to set a specific value. For most use cases, the PATCH endpoint with `autoDeferOnceEnabled` is recommended because it allows setting an explicit value rather than toggling.

<h3 id="toggle-automatic-deferral-of-maintenance-for-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. ## Defer One Maintenance Window for One Project

<a id="opIddeferGroupMaintenanceWindow"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/maintenanceWindow/defer \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/maintenanceWindow/defer`

Defers the maintenance window for the specified project. Urgent maintenance activities such as security patches can't wait for your chosen window. MongoDB Cloud starts those maintenance activities when needed. After you schedule maintenance for your cluster, you can't change your maintenance window until the current maintenance efforts complete. The maintenance procedure that MongoDB Cloud performs requires at least one replica set election during the maintenance window per replica set. Maintenance always begins as close to the scheduled hour as possible, but in-progress cluster updates or unexpected system issues could delay the start time. You can only defer maintenance within a limited time window before the scheduled maintenance starts; deferral requests made outside of this window return an error.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/cluster-maintenance-window/#respond-to-required-maintenance">Respond to Required Maintenance</a>

<h3 id="defer-one-maintenance-window-for-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|

```bash
  }'
```

<h3 id="create-one-metric-integration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|

Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[MetricIntegrationRequest](#schemametricintegrationrequest)|true|Metric integration configuration to create.|
|» aggregationTemporality|body|string|true|The temporality to send to the metric integration.|
|» authType|body|string|true|Authentication method the integration uses when exporting metrics to the endpoint. `HEADER` authenticates with the static HTTP headers provided in the `headers` field, which must be set when this value is used. `OAUTH2` acquires a bearer token from an OAuth 2.0 token endpoint using the `oauth` field.|
|» endpoint|body|string|true|OpenTelemetry collector endpoint URL. Must use HTTPS.|
|» headers|body|[[Header](#schemaheader)]|false|HTTP headers for authentication and configuration. Total size limit 2KB. Required when `authType` is `HEADER`.|
|» integrationType|body|string|true|Type of metric integration. Identifies which protocol will be used for the integration. This value cannot be modified after the integration is created.|
|» metricSelection|body|[string]|true|Array of metric categories to export. Determines which types of metrics are sent to the integration.|
|» oauth|body|[OAuthConfigRequest](#schemaoauthconfigrequest)|false|OAuth 2.0 client credentials configuration. Required when `authType` is `OAUTH2`. Secrets are never returned.|
|» providerType|body|string|true|The provider type for the metric integration. Identifies the third-party service provider.|

## Return All MongoDB Cloud Users in One Project

<a id="opIdlistGroupUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/users \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/users`

Returns details about the pending and active MongoDB Cloud users associated with the specified project. 

**Note**: This resource cannot be used to view details about users invited via the deprecated Invite One MongoDB Cloud User to Join One Project endpoint.

**Note**: To return both pending and active users, use v2-{2025-02-19} or later. If using a deprecated version, only active users will be returned.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Projects/operation/createProjectInvitation">Deprecated: Invite One MongoDB Cloud User to Join One Project</a>

<h3 id="return-all-mongodb-cloud-users-in-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|includeCount|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud calculates the total number of items for the response. When set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may skip an additional count operation. The response may still include `totalCount` when the count is available without additional calculation.|
|itemsPerPage|query|integer|false|Number of items that the response returns per page.|
|pageNum|query|integer|false|Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|flattenTeams|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the returned list should include users who belong to a team with a role in this project. You might not have assigned the individual users a role in this project. If `"flattenTeams" : false`, this resource returns only users with a role in the project.  If `"flattenTeams" : true`, this resource returns both users with roles in the project and users who belong to teams with roles in the project.|
|includeOrgUsers|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the returned list should include users with implicit access to the project, the Organization Owner or Organization Read Only role. You might not have assigned the individual users a role in this project. If `"includeOrgUsers": false`, this resource returns only users with a role in the project. If `"includeOrgUsers": true`, this resource returns both users with roles in the project and users who have implicit access to the project through their organization role.|
|orgMembershipStatus|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated: Use `orgMembershipStatuses` instead. Organization membership status to filter users by. Allowed values: `ACTIVE`, `PENDING`, `INVITATION_EXPIRED`, `INVITATION_REJECTED`. If you exclude this parameter, this resource returns ACTIVE and PENDING users. Not supported in deprecated versions.|
|orgMembershipStatuses|query|[string]|false|Organization membership status to filter users by. You can supply this parameter multiple times. Allowed values: `ACTIVE`, `PENDING`, `INVITATION_EXPIRED`, `INVITATION_REJECTED`. Replaces the deprecated `orgMembershipStatus` parameter. If you exclude this parameter, this resource returns ACTIVE and PENDING users. Cannot be combined with `orgMembershipStatus`. Not supported in deprecated versions.|
|username|query|string(email)|false|Email address to filter users by. Not supported in deprecated versions.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|orgMembershipStatuses|PENDING|
|orgMembershipStatuses|ACTIVE|
|orgMembershipStatuses|INVITATION_EXPIRED|
|orgMembershipStatuses|INVITATION_REJECTED|

## Add One MongoDB Cloud User to One Project

<a id="opIdaddGroupUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2025-02-19+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "roles": [
      "string"
    ],
    "username": "user@example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/users`

Adds one MongoDB Cloud user to one project. 
- If the user has a pending invitation to join the project's organization, MongoDB Cloud modifies it and grants project access. 
- If the user doesn't have an invitation to join the organization, MongoDB Cloud sends a new invitation that grants the user organization and project access. 
- If the user is already active in the project's organization, MongoDB Cloud grants access to the project. 
- Replaces `INVITATION_EXPIRED` and `INVITATION_REJECTED` user with the same email. A conflict, if and only if, there is an existing `PENDING` or `ACTIVE` user. 


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "roles": [
    "string"
  ],
  "username": "user@example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="add-one-mongodb-cloud-user-to-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[GroupUserRequest](#schemagroupuserrequest)|true|The active or pending MongoDB Cloud user that you want to add to the specified project.|

## Return One MongoDB Cloud User in One Project

<a id="opIdgetGroupUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/users/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/users/{userId}`

Returns information about the specified MongoDB Cloud user within the context of the specified project. 

**Note**: You can only use this resource to fetch information about MongoDB Cloud human users. To return information about an API Key, use the [Return One Organization API Key](#tag/Programmatic-API-Keys/operation/getApiKey) endpoint.

**Note**: This resource does not return information about pending users invited via the deprecated [Invite One MongoDB Cloud User to Join One Project](#tag/Projects/operation/createProjectInvitation) endpoint.

<h3 id="return-one-mongodb-cloud-user-in-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|userId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the pending or active user in the project. If you need to lookup a user's `userId` or verify a user's status in the organization, use the Return All MongoDB Cloud Users in One Project resource and filter by `username`.|
|orgMembershipStatuses|query|[string]|false|Organization membership status to filter users by. You can supply this parameter multiple times. Allowed values: `ACTIVE`, `PENDING`, `INVITATION_EXPIRED`, `INVITATION_REJECTED`. If you exclude this parameter, this resource returns ACTIVE and PENDING users. Not supported in deprecated versions.|

## Remove One MongoDB Cloud User from One Project

<a id="opIdremoveGroupUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/users/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/users/{userId}`

Removes one MongoDB Cloud user from the specified project. You can remove an active user or a user that has not yet accepted the invitation to join the organization.

**Note**: This resource cannot be used to remove pending users invited via the deprecated Invite One MongoDB Cloud User to Join One Project endpoint.

**Note**: To remove pending or active users, use v2-{2025-02-19} or later. If using a deprecated version, only active users can be removed.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Projects/operation/createProjectInvitation">Deprecated: Invite One MongoDB Cloud User to Join One Project</a>

|---|---|---|---|---|

To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|userId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the pending or active user in the project. If you need to lookup a user's `userId` or verify a user's status in the organization, use the [Return All MongoDB Cloud Users in One Project](#tag/MongoDB-Cloud-Users/operation/listProjectUsers) resource and filter by `username`.|

## Return All MongoDB Cloud Users Assigned to One Team

<a id="opIdlistOrgTeamUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/teams/{teamId}/users`

Returns details about the pending and active MongoDB Cloud users associated with the specified team in the organization. Teams enable you to grant project access roles to MongoDB Cloud users. 

**Note**: This resource cannot be used to view details about users invited via the deprecated [Invite One MongoDB Cloud User to Join One Project](#tag/Projects/operation/createProjectInvitation) endpoint.

**Note**: To return both pending and active users, use v2-{2025-02-19} or later. If using a deprecated version, only active users will be returned.

<a href="https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/access/manage-teams-in-orgs/#std-label-manage-teams">Manage Organization Teams</a>

## Add One MongoDB Cloud User to One Team

<a id="opIdaddOrgTeamUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/orgs/4888442a3354817a7320eb61/teams/string:addUser \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2025-02-19+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "id": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/teams/{teamId}:addUser`

Adds one MongoDB Cloud user to one team. You can add an active user or a user that has not yet accepted the invitation to join the organization. 

**Note**: This resource cannot be used to add a user invited via the deprecated Invite One MongoDB Cloud User to Join One Project endpoint. 

A user whose only organization invitation has `EXPIRED` or been `REJECTED` is treated as not belonging to the organization (`USER_NOT_IN_ORG`); re-invite them to the organization first (which creates a new pending invitation), then add them to the team.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Projects/operation/updateProjectInvitation">Deprecated: Invite One MongoDB Cloud User to Join One Project endpoint</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8"
}
```

<h3 id="add-one-mongodb-cloud-user-to-one-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|orgId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization that contains your projects. Use the [`/orgs`](#tag/Organizations/operation/listOrganizations) endpoint to retrieve all organizations to which the authenticated user has access.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|teamId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the team to add the MongoDB Cloud user to.|
|body|body|[AddOrRemoveUserFromTeam](#schemaaddorremoveuserfromteam)|true|The active or pending MongoDB Cloud user that you want to add to the specified team.|
|» id|body|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the MongoDB Cloud user.|

## Add One MongoDB Cloud User to One Organization

<a id="opIdcreateOrgUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/orgs/4888442a3354817a7320eb61/users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2025-02-19+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "roles": {
      "groupRoleAssignments": [
        {
          "groupId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
          "groupRoles": [
            "string"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "orgRoles": [
        "ORG_OWNER"
      ]
    },
    "teamIds": [
      "string"
    ],
    "username": "user@example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/users`

Invites one new or existing MongoDB Cloud user to join the organization. The invitation to join the organization will be sent to the username provided and must be accepted within 30 days. 

**Note**: If the user does not have an existing MongoDB Cloud account, they will be prompted to finish setting up an account upon accepting the invitation. If the user already has an account, they will still receive an invitation to access the organization. 

Replaces `INVITATION_EXPIRED` and `INVITATION_REJECTED` user with the same email. A conflict, if and only if, there is an existing `PENDING` or `ACTIVE` user.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "roles": {
    "groupRoleAssignments": [
      {
        "groupId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
        "groupRoles": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "orgRoles": [
      "ORG_OWNER"
    ]
  },
  "teamIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "username": "user@example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="add-one-mongodb-cloud-user-to-one-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|orgId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization that contains your projects. Use the [`/orgs`](#tag/Organizations/operation/listOrganizations) endpoint to retrieve all organizations to which the authenticated user has access.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[OrgUserRequest](#schemaorguserrequest)|true|Represents the MongoDB Cloud user to be created within the organization.|
|» roles|body|[OrgUserRolesRequest](#schemaorguserrolesrequest)|true|Organization and project level roles to assign the MongoDB Cloud user within one organization.|
|» teamIds|body|[string]|false|List of unique 24-hexadecimal digit strings that identifies the teams to which this MongoDB Cloud user belongs.|
|» username|body|string(email)|true|Email address that represents the username of the MongoDB Cloud user.|

## Return One MongoDB Cloud User in One Organization

<a id="opIdgetOrgUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/orgs/4888442a3354817a7320eb61/users/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/users/{userId}`

Returns information about the specified MongoDB Cloud user within the context of the specified organization. 

**Note**: This resource can only be used to fetch information about MongoDB Cloud human users. To return information about an API Key, use the [Return One Organization API Key](#tag/Programmatic-API-Keys/operation/getApiKey) endpoint.

**Note**: This resource does not return information about pending users invited via the deprecated [Invite One MongoDB Cloud User to Join One Project](#tag/Projects/operation/createProjectInvitation) endpoint.

<h3 id="return-one-mongodb-cloud-user-in-one-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|orgId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization that contains your projects. Use the [`/orgs`](#tag/Organizations/operation/listOrganizations) endpoint to retrieve all organizations to which the authenticated user has access.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|userId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the pending or active user in the organization. If you need to lookup a user's `userId` or verify a user's status in the organization, use the Return All MongoDB Cloud Users in One Organization resource and filter by `username`.|
|orgMembershipStatuses|query|[string]|false|Organization membership status to filter users by. You can supply this parameter multiple times. Allowed values: `ACTIVE`, `PENDING`, `INVITATION_EXPIRED`, `INVITATION_REJECTED`. If you exclude this parameter, this resource returns ACTIVE and PENDING users. Not supported in deprecated versions.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|orgMembershipStatuses|PENDING|
|orgMembershipStatuses|ACTIVE|
|orgMembershipStatuses|INVITATION_EXPIRED|
|orgMembershipStatuses|INVITATION_REJECTED|

`DELETE /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/users/{userId}`

Removes one MongoDB Cloud user in the specified organization. You can remove an active user or a user that has not yet accepted the invitation to join the organization. 

**Note**: This resource cannot be used to remove pending users invited via the deprecated Invite One MongoDB Cloud User to Join One Project endpoint.

## Create One MongoDB Cloud User

<a id="opIdcreateUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "country": "string",
    "firstName": "string",
    "lastName": "string",
    "mobileNumber": "string",
    "password": "password",
    "roles": [
      {
        "groupId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
        "orgId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
        "roleName": "string"
      }
    ],
    "username": "user@example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/users`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Creates one MongoDB Cloud user account. A MongoDB Cloud user account grants access to only the MongoDB Cloud application. To grant database access, create a database user. MongoDB Cloud sends an email to the users you specify, inviting them to join the project. Invited users don't have access to the project until they accept the invitation. Invitations expire after 30 days.

 MongoDB Cloud limits MongoDB Cloud user membership to a maximum of 250 MongoDB Cloud users per team. MongoDB Cloud limits MongoDB Cloud user membership to 500 MongoDB Cloud users per project and 500 MongoDB Cloud users per organization, which includes the combined membership of all projects in the organization. MongoDB Cloud raises an error if an operation exceeds these limits. For example, if you have an organization with five projects, and each project has 100 MongoDB Cloud users, and each MongoDB Cloud user belongs to only one project, you can't add any MongoDB Cloud users to this organization without first removing existing MongoDB Cloud users from the organization.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "country": "string",
  "firstName": "string",
  "lastName": "string",
  "mobileNumber": "string",
  "password": "password",
  "roles": [
    {
      "groupId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
      "orgId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
      "roleName": "string"
    }
  ],
  "username": "user@example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-mongodb-cloud-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[CloudAppUser](#schemacloudappuser)|true|MongoDB Cloud user account to create.|
|» country|body|string|true|Two alphabet characters that identifies MongoDB Cloud user's geographic location. This parameter uses the ISO 3166-1a2 code format.|
|» firstName|body|string|true|First or given name that belongs to the MongoDB Cloud user.|
|» lastName|body|string|true|Last name, family name, or surname that belongs to the MongoDB Cloud user.|
|» mobileNumber|body|string|true|Mobile phone number that belongs to the MongoDB Cloud user.|
|» password|body|string(password)|true|Password applied with the username to log in to MongoDB Cloud. MongoDB Cloud does not return this parameter except in response to creating a new MongoDB Cloud user. Only the MongoDB Cloud user can update their password after it has been set from the MongoDB Cloud console.|
|» roles|body|[[CloudAccessRoleAssignment](#schemacloudaccessroleassignment)]|true|List of objects that display the MongoDB Cloud user's roles and the corresponding organization or project to which that role applies. A role can apply to one organization or one project but not both.|
|» username|body|string(email)|true|Email address that represents the username of the MongoDB Cloud user.|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-monitoring-and-logs">Monitoring and Logs</h1>

Returns database deployment monitoring and logging data.

## Download Logs for One Cluster Host in One Project

<a id="opIddownloadGroupClusterLog"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/logs/mongodb.gz \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{hostName}/logs/{logName}.gz`

Returns a compressed (.gz) log file that contains a range of log messages for the specified host for the specified project. MongoDB updates process and audit logs from the cluster backend infrastructure every five minutes. Logs are stored in chunks approximately five minutes in length, but this duration may vary. If you poll the API for log files, we recommend polling every five minutes even though consecutive polls could contain some overlapping logs. This feature isn't available for `M0` free clusters, `M2`, `M5`, flex, or serverless clusters. The API does not support direct calls with the json response schema. You must request a gzip response schema using an accept header of the format: `Accept: application/vnd.atlas.YYYY-MM-DD+gzip`.

<h3 id="download-logs-for-one-cluster-host-in-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|hostName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the host that stores the log files that you want to download.|
|logName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the log file that you want to return. To return audit logs, enable *Database Auditing* for the specified project.|
|endDate|query|integer(int64)|false|Specifies the date and time for the ending point of the range of log messages to retrieve, in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch. This value will default to 24 hours after the start date. If the start date is also unspecified, the value will default to the time of the request.|
|startDate|query|integer(int64)|false|Specifies the date and time for the starting point of the range of log messages to retrieve, in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch. This value will default to 24 hours prior to the end date. If the end date is also unspecified, the value will default to 24 hours prior to the time of the request.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|logName|mongodb|
|logName|mongos|
|logName|mongodb-audit-log|
|logName|mongos-audit-log|

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/hosts/{processId}/fts/metrics`

Returns all Atlas Search metric types available for one process in the specified project. You must have the Project Read Only or higher role to view the Atlas Search metric types.

<h3 id="return-all-atlas-search-metric-types-for-one-process-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|processId|path|string|true|Combination of hostname and IANA port that serves the MongoDB process. The host must be the hostname, fully qualified domain name (FQDN), or Internet Protocol address (IPv4 or IPv6) of the host that runs the MongoDB process (mongod or mongos). The port must be the IANA port on which the MongoDB process listens for requests.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|

## Return Atlas Search Metrics for One Index in One Namespace

<a id="opIdgetGroupHostFtsMetricIndexMeasurements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/hosts/my.host.name.com%3A27017/fts/metrics/indexes/mydb/mycoll/myindex/measurements?granularity=PT1M&metrics=INDEX_SIZE_ON_DISK' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/hosts/{processId}/fts/metrics/indexes/{databaseName}/{collectionName}/{indexName}/measurements`

Returns the Atlas Search metrics data series within the provided time range for one namespace and index name on the specified process. You must have the Project Read Only or higher role to view the Atlas Search metric types.

<h3 id="return-atlas-search-metrics-for-one-index-in-one-namespace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|processId|path|string|true|Combination of hostname and IANA port that serves the MongoDB process. The host must be the hostname, fully qualified domain name (FQDN), or Internet Protocol address (IPv4 or IPv6) of the host that runs the MongoDB process (mongod or mongos). The port must be the IANA port on which the MongoDB process listens for requests.|
|indexName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the index.|
|databaseName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the database.|
|collectionName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the collection.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|granularity|query|string|true|Duration that specifies the interval at which Atlas reports the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 duration format in UTC.|
|period|query|string|false|Duration over which Atlas reports the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 duration format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **start** and **end**.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud begins reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud stops reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|metrics|query|[string]|true|List that contains the measurements that MongoDB Atlas reports for the associated data series.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|metrics|INDEX_SIZE_ON_DISK|
|metrics|NUMBER_OF_DELETES|
|metrics|NUMBER_OF_ERROR_QUERIES|
|metrics|NUMBER_OF_GETMORE_COMMANDS|
|metrics|NUMBER_OF_INDEX_FIELDS|
|metrics|NUMBER_OF_INSERTS|
|metrics|NUMBER_OF_SUCCESS_QUERIES|
|metrics|NUMBER_OF_UPDATES|
|metrics|REPLICATION_LAG|
|metrics|TOTAL_NUMBER_OF_QUERIES|

## Return Atlas Search Hardware and Status Metrics

<a id="opIdlistGroupHostFtsMetricMeasurements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/hosts/my.host.name.com%3A27017/fts/metrics/measurements?granularity=PT1M&metrics=FTS_DISK_USAGE' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/hosts/{processId}/fts/metrics/measurements`

Returns the Atlas Search hardware and status data series within the provided time range for one process in the specified project. You must have the Project Read Only or higher role to view the Atlas Search metric types.

<h3 id="return-atlas-search-hardware-and-status-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|processId|path|string|true|Combination of hostname and IANA port that serves the MongoDB process. The host must be the hostname, fully qualified domain name (FQDN), or Internet Protocol address (IPv4 or IPv6) of the host that runs the MongoDB process (mongod or mongos). The port must be the IANA port on which the MongoDB process listens for requests.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|granularity|query|string|true|Duration that specifies the interval at which Atlas reports the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 duration format in UTC.|
|period|query|string|false|Duration over which Atlas reports the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 duration format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **start** and **end**.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud begins reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud stops reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|metrics|query|[string]|true|List that contains the metrics that you want MongoDB Atlas to report for the associated data series. If you don't set this parameter, this resource returns all hardware and status metrics for the associated data series.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|metrics|FTS_DISK_USAGE|
|metrics|FTS_PROCESS_CPU_KERNEL|
|metrics|FTS_PROCESS_CPU_USER|
|metrics|FTS_PROCESS_NORMALIZED_CPU_KERNEL|
|metrics|FTS_PROCESS_NORMALIZED_CPU_USER|
|metrics|FTS_PROCESS_RESIDENT_MEMORY|
|metrics|FTS_PROCESS_SHARED_MEMORY|
|metrics|FTS_PROCESS_VIRTUAL_MEMORY|
|metrics|JVM_CURRENT_MEMORY|
|metrics|JVM_MAX_MEMORY|
|metrics|PAGE_FAULTS|

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/processes`

Returns details of all processes for the specified project. A MongoDB process can be either a `mongod` or `mongos`.

<h3 id="return-all-mongodb-processes-in-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|

## Return Measurements for One Database in One MongoDB Process

<a id="opIdgetGroupProcessDatabaseMeasurements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/processes/mongodb.example.com%3A27017/databases/string/measurements?granularity=PT1M' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/processes/{processId}/databases/{databaseName}/measurements`

Returns the measurements of one database for the specified host for the specified project. Returns the database's on-disk storage space based on the MongoDB `dbStats` command output. To calculate some metric series, Atlas takes the rate between every two adjacent points. For these metric series, the first data point has a null value because Atlas can't calculate a rate for the first data point given the query time range. Atlas retrieves database metrics every 20 minutes but reduces frequency when necessary to optimize database performance.

<h3 id="return-measurements-for-one-database-in-one-mongodb-process-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|databaseName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the database that the specified MongoDB process serves.|
|m|query|[string]|false|One or more types of measurement to request for this MongoDB process. If omitted, the resource returns all measurements. To specify multiple values for `m`, repeat the `m` parameter for each value. Specify measurements that apply to the specified host. MongoDB Cloud returns an error if you specified any invalid measurements.|
|processId|path|string|true|Combination of hostname and Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) port that serves the MongoDB process. The host must be the hostname, fully qualified domain name (FQDN), or Internet Protocol address (IPv4 or IPv6) of the host that runs the MongoDB process (`mongod` or `mongos`). The port must be the IANA port on which the MongoDB process listens for requests.|
|granularity|query|string|true|Duration that specifies the interval at which Atlas reports the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 duration format in UTC.|
|period|query|string|false|Duration over which Atlas reports the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 duration format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **start** and **end**.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud begins reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud stops reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|m|DATABASE_AVERAGE_OBJECT_SIZE|
|m|DATABASE_COLLECTION_COUNT|
|m|DATABASE_DATA_SIZE|
|m|DATABASE_STORAGE_SIZE|
|m|DATABASE_INDEX_SIZE|
|m|DATABASE_INDEX_COUNT|
|m|DATABASE_EXTENT_COUNT|
|m|DATABASE_OBJECT_COUNT|
|m|DATABASE_VIEW_COUNT|

- Throughput of I/O operations for the disk partition used for the MongoDB process
- Percentage of time during which requests the partition issued and serviced
- Latency per operation type of the disk partition used for the MongoDB process

To specify multiple values for `m`, repeat the `m` parameter for each value. Specify measurements that apply to the specified host. ## Return Measurements for One MongoDB Process

<a id="opIdgetGroupProcessMeasurements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/processes/mongodb.example.com%3A27017/measurements?granularity=PT1M' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/processes/{processId}/measurements`

Returns disk, partition, or host measurements per process for the specified host for the specified project. Returned value can be one of the following:
- Throughput of I/O operations for the disk partition used for the MongoDB process
- Percentage of time during which requests the partition issued and serviced
- Latency per operation type of the disk partition used for the MongoDB process
- Amount of free and used disk space on the disk partition used for the MongoDB process
- Measurements for the host, such as CPU usage or number of I/O operations.

<h3 id="return-measurements-for-one-mongodb-process-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|m|query|[string]|false|One or more types of measurement to request for this MongoDB process. If omitted, the resource returns all measurements. To specify multiple values for `m`, repeat the `m` parameter for each value. Specify measurements that apply to the specified host. MongoDB Cloud returns an error if you specified any invalid measurements.|
|period|query|string|false|Duration over which Atlas reports the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 duration format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **start** and **end**.|
|processId|path|string|true|Combination of hostname and Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) port that serves the MongoDB process. The host must be the hostname, fully qualified domain name (FQDN), or Internet Protocol address (IPv4 or IPv6) of the host that runs the MongoDB process (`mongod` or `mongos`). The port must be the IANA port on which the MongoDB process listens for requests.|
|granularity|query|string|true|Duration that specifies the interval at which Atlas reports the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 duration format in UTC.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud begins reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud stops reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-network-peering">Network Peering</h1>

Returns, adds, edits, and removes network peering containers and peering connections.
When you deploy an M10+ dedicated cluster, Atlas creates a VPC for the selected provider and region or regions if no existing VPC or VPC peering connection exists for that provider and region. Atlas assigns the VPC a Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) block.

## Return All Network Peering Containers in One Project for One Cloud Provider

<a id="opIdlistGroupContainers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/containers?providerName=AWS' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/containers`

Returns details about all network peering containers in the specified project for the specified cloud provider. If you do not specify the cloud provider, MongoDB Cloud returns details about all network peering containers in the project for Amazon Web Services (AWS).

<h3 id="return-all-network-peering-containers-in-one-project-for-one-cloud-provider-parameters">Parameters</h3>

To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|includeCount|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud calculates the total number of items for the response. When set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may skip an additional count operation. The response may still include `totalCount` when the count is available without additional calculation.|
|itemsPerPage|query|integer|false|Number of items that the response returns per page.|
|pageNum|query|integer|false|Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|providerName|query|string|true|Cloud service provider that serves the desired network peering containers.|

## Create One Network Peering Container

<a id="opIdcreateGroupContainer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/containers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "providerName": "AWS"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/containers`

Creates one new network peering container in the specified project. MongoDB Cloud can deploy Network Peering connections in a network peering container. GCP can have one container per project. AWS and Azure can have one container per cloud provider region.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "providerName": "AWS"
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-network-peering-container-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[CloudProviderContainer](#schemacloudprovidercontainer)|true|Creates one new network peering container in the specified project.|
|» providerName|body|string|false|Cloud service provider that serves the requested network peering containers.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[AzureCloudProviderContainer](#schemaazurecloudprovidercontainer)|false|Collection of settings that configures the network container for a virtual private connection on Amazon Web Services.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[GCPCloudProviderContainer](#schemagcpcloudprovidercontainer)|false|Collection of settings that configures the network container for a virtual private connection on Amazon Web Services.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[AWSCloudProviderContainer](#schemaawscloudprovidercontainer)|false|Collection of settings that configures the network container for a virtual private connection on Amazon Web Services.|

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/peers`

Creates one new network peering connection in the specified project. Network peering allows multiple cloud-hosted applications to securely connect to the same project. To learn more about considerations and prerequisites, see the Network Peering Documentation.

<a href="https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/reference/api/vpc-create-peering-connection/#prerequisites">Azure Network Peering Prerequisites</a>

```json
  "vpcId": "string"
}
```

## Create One Online Archive

<a id="opIdcreateGroupClusterOnlineArchive"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/onlineArchives \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "collName": "string",
    "collectionType": "STANDARD",
    "criteria": {
      "type": "DATE"
    },
    "dataExpirationRule": {
      "expireAfterDays": 7
    },
    "dataProcessRegion": {
      "cloudProvider": "AWS"
    },
    "dbName": "string",
    "partitionFields": [
      {
        "fieldName": "string",
        "order": 0
      }
    ],
    "paused": true,
    "schedule": {
      "type": "DEFAULT"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/onlineArchives`

Creates one online archive. This archive stores data from one cluster within one project.

<a href="https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/online-archive/manage-online-archive/#std-label-manage-online-archive">Online Archive</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "collName": "string",
  "collectionType": "STANDARD",
  "criteria": {
    "type": "DATE"
  },
  "dataExpirationRule": {
    "expireAfterDays": 7
  },
  "dataProcessRegion": {
    "cloudProvider": "AWS"
  },
  "dbName": "string",
  "partitionFields": [
    {
      "fieldName": "string",
      "order": 0
    }
  ],
  "paused": true,
  "schedule": {
    "type": "DEFAULT"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-online-archive-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster that contains the collection for which you want to create one online archive.|
|body|body|[BackupOnlineArchiveCreate](#schemabackuponlinearchivecreate)|true|Creates one online archive.|
|» collName|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the collection for which you created the online archive.|
|» collectionType|body|string|false|Classification of MongoDB database collection that you want to return.<br><br>If you set this parameter to `TIMESERIES`, set `"criteria.type" : "date"` and `"criteria.dateFormat" : "ISODATE"`.|
|» criteria|body|[CriteriaView](#schemacriteriaview)|true|Rules by which MongoDB Cloud archives data.<br><br>Use the `criteria.type` field to choose how MongoDB Cloud selects data to archive. Choose data using the age of the data or a MongoDB query.<br>`"criteria.type": "DATE"` selects documents to archive based on a date.<br>`"criteria.type": "CUSTOM"` selects documents to archive based on a custom JSON query. MongoDB Cloud doesn't support `"criteria.type": "CUSTOM"` when `"collectionType": "TIMESERIES"`.|
|» dataExpirationRule|body|[DataExpirationRuleView](#schemadataexpirationruleview)|false|Rule for specifying when data should be deleted from the archive.|
|» dataProcessRegion|body|[CreateDataProcessRegionView](#schemacreatedataprocessregionview)|false|Settings to configure the region where you wish to store your archived data.|
|» dbName|body|string|true|Human-readable label of the database that contains the collection that contains the online archive.|
|» partitionFields|body|[[PartitionFieldView](#schemapartitionfieldview)]|false|List that contains document parameters to use to logically divide data within a collection. Partitions provide a coarse level of filtering of the underlying collection data. To divide your data, specify parameters that you frequently query. If you specified `criteria.type`: `DATE` in the Create One Online Archive endpoint, then you can specify up to three parameters by which to query. One of these parameters must be the `DATE` value, which is required in this case. If you specified `criteria.type`: `CUSTOM` in the Create One Online Archive endpoint, then you can specify up to two parameters by which to query. Queries that don't use `criteria.type`: `DATE` or `criteria.type`: `CUSTOM` parameters cause MongoDB to scan a full collection of all archived documents. This takes more time and increases your costs.|
|» paused|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether this online archive exists in the paused state. A request to resume fails if the collection has another active online archive. To pause an active online archive or resume a paused online archive, you must include this parameter. To pause an active archive, set this to **true**. To resume a paused archive, set this to **false**.|
|» schedule|body|[OnlineArchiveSchedule](#schemaonlinearchiveschedule)|false|Regular frequency and duration when archiving process occurs.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» collectionType|TIMESERIES|
|» collectionType|STANDARD|

## Update One Online Archive

<a id="opIdupdateGroupClusterOnlineArchive"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/onlineArchives/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "criteria": {
      "type": "DATE"
    },
    "dataExpirationRule": {
      "expireAfterDays": 7
    },
    "paused": true,
    "schedule": {
      "type": "DEFAULT"
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/onlineArchives/{archiveId}`

Updates, pauses, or resumes one online archive. This archive stores data from one cluster within one project.

<a href="https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/online-archive/manage-online-archive/#std-label-manage-online-archive">Online Archive</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "criteria": {
    "type": "DATE"
  },
  "dataExpirationRule": {
    "expireAfterDays": 7
  },
  "paused": true,
  "schedule": {
    "type": "DEFAULT"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-one-online-archive-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|archiveId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the online archive to update.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster that contains the specified collection from which Application created the online archive.|
|body|body|[BackupOnlineArchive](#schemabackuponlinearchive)|true|Updates, pauses, or resumes one online archive.|
|» criteria|body|[CriteriaView](#schemacriteriaview)|false|Rules by which MongoDB Cloud archives data.<br><br>Use the `criteria.type` field to choose how MongoDB Cloud selects data to archive. Choose data using the age of the data or a MongoDB query.<br>`"criteria.type": "DATE"` selects documents to archive based on a date.<br>`"criteria.type": "CUSTOM"` selects documents to archive based on a custom JSON query. MongoDB Cloud doesn't support `"criteria.type": "CUSTOM"` when `"collectionType": "TIMESERIES"`.|
|» dataExpirationRule|body|[DataExpirationRuleView](#schemadataexpirationruleview)|false|Rule for specifying when data should be deleted from the archive.|
|» paused|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether this online archive exists in the paused state. A request to resume fails if the collection has another active online archive. To pause an active online archive or resume a paused online archive, you must include this parameter. To pause an active archive, set this to **true**. To resume a paused archive, set this to **false**.|
|» schedule|body|[OnlineArchiveSchedule](#schemaonlinearchiveschedule)|false|Regular frequency and duration when archiving process occurs.|

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/onlineArchives/queryLogs.gz`

Downloads query logs for the specified online archive. The API does not support direct calls with the json response schema. You must request a gzip response schema using an accept header of the format: `Accept: application/vnd.atlas.YYYY-MM-DD+gzip`.

<a href="https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/online-archive/manage-online-archive/#std-label-manage-online-archive">Online Archive</a>

<h3 id="download-online-archive-query-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|startDate|query|integer(int64)|false|Date and time that specifies the starting point for the range of log messages to return. This resource expresses this value in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the [UNIX epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time).|
|endDate|query|integer(int64)|false|Date and time that specifies the end point for the range of log messages to return. This resource expresses this value in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the [UNIX epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time).|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster that contains the collection for which you want to return the query logs from one online archive.|
|archiveOnly|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to download logs for queries against your online archive only or both your online archive and cluster.|

## Create One Organization

<a id="opIdcreateOrg"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/orgs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "apiKey": {
      "desc": "string",
      "roles": [
        "ORG_OWNER"
      ]
    },
    "federationSettingsId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
    "name": "string",
    "orgOwnerId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
    "serviceAccount": {
      "description": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "roles": [
        "ORG_MEMBER"
      ],
      "secretExpiresAfterHours": 8,
      "withoutInitialSecret": false
    },
    "skipDefaultAlertsSettings": false
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/orgs`

Creates one organization in MongoDB Cloud and links it to the requesting Service Account's or API Key's organization. The requesting Service Account's or API Key's organization must be a paying organization. To learn more, see Configure a Paying Organization in the MongoDB Atlas documentation. Optionally, if `federationSettingsId` is provided, the new Organization will be linked to the federation. The requesting Service Account or API Key must be an Organization Owner in the federation.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/#configure-a-paying-organization">Configure a Paying Organization</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "apiKey": {
    "desc": "string",
    "roles": [
      "ORG_OWNER"
    ]
  },
  "federationSettingsId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "name": "string",
  "orgOwnerId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "serviceAccount": {
    "description": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "roles": [
      "ORG_MEMBER"
    ],
    "secretExpiresAfterHours": 8,
    "withoutInitialSecret": false
  },
  "skipDefaultAlertsSettings": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[CreateOrganizationRequest](#schemacreateorganizationrequest)|true|Organization that you want to create.|
|» apiKey|body|[CreateAtlasOrganizationApiKey](#schemacreateatlasorganizationapikey)|false|Organization Service Account that Atlas creates for this organization. If omitted, Atlas doesn't create an organization Service Account for this organization. If specified, this object requires all body parameters. Note that API Keys cannot be specified in the same request.|
|» federationSettingsId|body|string|false|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the federation to link the newly created organization to. If specified, the proposed Organization Owner of the new organization must have the Organization Owner role in an organization associated with the federation.|
|» name|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the organization.|
|» orgOwnerId|body|string|false|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the MongoDB Cloud user that you want to assign the Organization Owner role. This user must be a member of the same organization as the calling API key. If you provide `federationSettingsId`,  this user must instead have the Organization Owner role on an organization in the specified federation. This parameter is required only when you authenticate with Programmatic API Keys.|
|» serviceAccount|body|[OrgServiceAccountRequest](#schemaorgserviceaccountrequest)|false|Organization Service Account that Atlas creates for this organization. If omitted, Atlas doesn't create an organization Service Account for this organization. If specified, this object requires all body parameters. Note that API Keys cannot be specified in the same request.|
|» skipDefaultAlertsSettings|body|boolean|false|Disables automatic alert creation. When set to true, no organization level alerts will be created automatically.|

`DELETE /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}`
