## Update Delegation Settings for One Organization

<a id="opIdupdateOrgDelegationSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/orgs/4888442a3354817a7320eb61/delegationSettings \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2025-03-12+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "delegatedMcpAccess": "DISALLOWED",
    "delegatedPartnerAccess": "DISALLOWED",
    "idleRefreshTokenLifetime": 1,
    "maximumRefreshTokenLifetime": 1
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/delegationSettings`

Updates the delegation settings for the specified organization. Only fields present in the request body are updated; omitted fields retain their current values.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "delegatedMcpAccess": "DISALLOWED",
  "delegatedPartnerAccess": "DISALLOWED",
  "idleRefreshTokenLifetime": 1,
  "maximumRefreshTokenLifetime": 1
}
```

<h3 id="update-delegation-settings-for-one-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|orgId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization that contains your projects. Use the [`/orgs`](#tag/Organizations/operation/listOrganizations) endpoint to retrieve all organizations to which the authenticated user has access.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[OrgDelegationSettingsUpdateRequest](#schemaorgdelegationsettingsupdaterequest)|true|Delegation settings to update.|
|» delegatedMcpAccess|body|string \| null|false|Policy that controls how MCP (Model Context Protocol) delegated access is permitted within this organization. Possible values are `DISALLOWED`, `READ_ONLY`, and `READ_WRITE`. Defaults to `DISALLOWED`.|
|» delegatedPartnerAccess|body|string \| null|false|Policy that controls whether partner delegated access is permitted within this organization. Possible values are `DISALLOWED` and `READ_WRITE`. Defaults to `DISALLOWED`.|
|» idleRefreshTokenLifetime|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|Maximum number of seconds a refresh token may be idle before it expires. Omit to leave unchanged; set to null to reset to the system default. Must be between 1 and 31536000 (1 year) when provided.|
|» maximumRefreshTokenLifetime|body|integer(int64) \| null|false|Maximum lifetime of a refresh token in seconds, regardless of activity. Omit to leave unchanged; set to null to reset to the system default. Must be between 1 and 31536000 (1 year) when provided.|

## Return All Projects in One Organization

<a id="opIdgetOrgGroups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/orgs/4888442a3354817a7320eb61/groups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/groups`

Returns multiple projects in the specified organization. Each organization can have multiple projects. Use projects to:

- Isolate different environments, such as development, test, or production environments, from each other.
- Associate different MongoDB Cloud users or teams with different environments, or give different permission to MongoDB Cloud users in different environments.
- Maintain separate cluster security configurations.
- Create different alert settings.

<h3 id="return-all-projects-in-one-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|includeCount|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud calculates the total number of items for the response. When set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may skip an additional count operation. The response may still include `totalCount` when the count is available without additional calculation.|
|itemsPerPage|query|integer|false|Number of items that the response returns per page.|
|orgId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization that contains your projects. Use the [`/orgs`](#tag/Organizations/operation/listOrganizations) endpoint to retrieve all organizations to which the authenticated user has access.|
|pageNum|query|integer|false|Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|name|query|string|false|Human-readable label of the project to use to filter the returned list. Performs a case-insensitive search for a project within the organization which is prefixed by the specified name.|

## Update Maintenance Settings for One Organization

<a id="opIdupdateOrgMaintenanceSettings"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/orgs/4888442a3354817a7320eb61/maintenanceSettings \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2025-03-12+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "waveAssignmentMode": "MANUAL"
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/maintenanceSettings`

Updates maintenance settings for the specified organization. Omit optional fields from the request body to leave their current values unchanged. Specify null on an optional field to reset it to its default value.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "waveAssignmentMode": "MANUAL"
}
```

<h3 id="update-maintenance-settings-for-one-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|orgId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization that contains your projects. Use the [`/orgs`](#tag/Organizations/operation/listOrganizations) endpoint to retrieve all organizations to which the authenticated user has access.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[OrganizationMaintenanceSettingsUpdateRequest](#schemaorganizationmaintenancesettingsupdaterequest)|true|Maintenance settings to update for the specified organization.|
|» waveAssignmentMode|body|string|false|Mode configured for this organization that determines how maintenance waves are assigned to projects. Possible values are `MANUAL` and `ENV_TAG_MAPPING`. Defaults to `MANUAL` when unset. Set the organization to `ENV_TAG_MAPPING` mode to have Atlas derive the maintenance wave from each project's environment tag. The tag key must be `environment`. The tag value determines the wave: `development` or `test` maps to Wave 1, `staging` maps to Wave 2, and `production` maps to Wave 3. Only this field can be updated; Atlas derives read-only `effectiveWaveAssignmentMode` on GET responses and uses that value for scheduling when it differs from `waveAssignmentMode`. Omit this field to leave the current value unchanged. Specify null to reset to the default value (`MANUAL`).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» waveAssignmentMode|MANUAL|
|» waveAssignmentMode|ENV_TAG_MAPPING|

To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|

|» customSessionTimeouts|body|[CustomSessionTimeouts](#schemacustomsessiontimeouts)|false|Defines the session timeout settings for managing user sessions at the organization level. When set to null, the field's value is unset, and the default timeout settings are applied.|

|» multiFactorAuthRequired|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to require users to set up Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) before accessing the specified organization. To learn more, see: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-multi-factor-authentication/.|
|» operationsContact|body|string \| null|false|String that specifies a distribution list email address for the specified organization to receive proactive notifications about its infrastructure. The operations contact is used for notifications only and is not authorized to make decisions or approvals. Passing an explicit null clears the existing operations contact (if any). An empty string is invalid and is rejected with a validation error.|
|» restrictEmployeeAccess|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to block MongoDB Support from accessing Atlas infrastructure and cluster logs for any deployment in the specified organization without explicit permission. Once this setting is turned on, you can grant MongoDB Support a 24-hour bypass access to the Atlas deployment to resolve support issues. To learn more, see: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-restrict-support-access/.|
|» securityContact|body|string|false|String that specifies a single email address for the specified organization to receive security-related notifications. Specifying a security contact does not grant them authorization or access to Atlas for security decisions or approvals. An empty string is valid and clears the existing security contact (if any).|
|» streamsCrossGroupEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether a group's Atlas Stream Processing workspaces in this organization can create connections to other group's clusters in the same organization.|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-overload-protection-simulation">Overload Protection Simulation</h1>

## Create One Overload Protection Simulation

<a id="opIdcreateGroupClusterOverloadSimulation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/overloadSimulations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2025-03-12+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "durationSeconds": 0
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/overloadSimulations`

Starts an overload protection simulation for one cluster. Returns a 409 if a simulation is already in progress or completed; DELETE the existing simulation before starting a new one.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "durationSeconds": 0
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-overload-protection-simulation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|

Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster on which to start the overload protection simulation.|
|body|body|[OverloadProtectionSimulationRequest](#schemaoverloadprotectionsimulationrequest)|true|Details of the overload protection simulation to start. Valid durations (in seconds): 900, 3600, 28800, 86400.|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-performance-advisor">Performance Advisor</h1>

Returns suggested indexes and slow query data for a database deployment. Also enables or disables MongoDB Cloud-managed slow operation thresholds. To view field values in a sample query, you must have the Project Data Access Read Only role or higher. Otherwise, MongoDB Cloud returns redacted data rather than the field values.

## Return All Suggested Indexes to Drop

<a id="opIdlistGroupClusterPerformanceAdvisorDropIndexSuggestions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/performanceAdvisor/dropIndexSuggestions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/performanceAdvisor/dropIndexSuggestions`

Returns the indexes that the Performance Advisor suggests to drop. The Performance Advisor suggests dropping unused, redundant, and hidden indexes to improve write performance and increase storage space.

<h3 id="return-all-suggested-indexes-to-drop-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|

## Return All Suggested Indexes

<a id="opIdlistGroupClusterPerformanceAdvisorSuggestedIndexes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/performanceAdvisor/suggestedIndexes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/performanceAdvisor/suggestedIndexes`

Returns the indexes that the Performance Advisor suggests. The Performance Advisor monitors queries that MongoDB considers slow and suggests new indexes to improve query performance.

<h3 id="return-all-suggested-indexes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|processIds|query|[string]|false|Process IDs from which to retrieve suggested indexes. A `processId` is a combination of host and port that serves the MongoDB process. The host must be the hostname, FQDN, IPv4 address, or IPv6 address of the host that runs the MongoDB process (`mongod` or `mongos`). The port must be the IANA port on which the MongoDB process listens for requests. To include multiple `processIds`, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each `processId`.|
|namespaces|query|[string]|false|Namespaces from which to retrieve suggested indexes. A namespace consists of one database and one collection resource written as `.`: `<database>.<collection>`. To include multiple namespaces, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each namespace. Omit this parameter to return results for all namespaces.|
|since|query|integer(int64)|false|Date and time from which the query retrieves the suggested indexes. This parameter expresses its value in the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since the [UNIX epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time).<br><br>- If you don't specify the **until** parameter, the endpoint returns data covering from the **since** value and the current time.<br>- If you specify neither the **since** nor the **until** parameters, the endpoint returns data from the previous 24 hours.|
|until|query|integer(int64)|false|Date and time up until which the query retrieves the suggested indexes. This parameter expresses its value in the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since the [UNIX epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time).<br><br>- If you specify the **until** parameter, you must specify the **since** parameter.<br>- If you specify neither the **since** nor the **until** parameters, the endpoint returns data from the previous 24 hours.|

## Disable Managed Slow Operation Threshold

<a id="opIddisableGroupManagedSlowMs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/managedSlowMs/disable \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/managedSlowMs/disable`

Disables the slow operation threshold that MongoDB Cloud calculated for the specified project. The threshold determines which operations the Performance Advisor and Query Profiler considers slow. When enabled, MongoDB Cloud uses the average execution time for operations on your cluster to determine slow-running queries. As a result, the threshold is more pertinent to your cluster workload. The slow operation threshold is enabled by default for dedicated clusters (M10+). When disabled, MongoDB Cloud considers any operation that takes longer than 100 milliseconds to be slow.

<h3 id="disable-managed-slow-operation-threshold-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/managedSlowMs/enable \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/managedSlowMs/enable`

Enables MongoDB Cloud to use its slow operation threshold for the specified project. The threshold determines which operations the Performance Advisor and Query Profiler considers slow. When enabled, MongoDB Cloud uses the average execution time for operations on your cluster to determine slow-running queries. As a result, the threshold is more pertinent to your cluster workload. The slow operation threshold is enabled by default for dedicated clusters (M10+). When disabled, MongoDB Cloud considers any operation that takes longer than 100 milliseconds to be slow.

<h3 id="enable-managed-slow-operation-threshold-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|

## Return All Namespaces for One Host

<a id="opIdlistGroupProcessPerformanceAdvisorNamespaces"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/processes/string/performanceAdvisor/namespaces \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/processes/{processId}/performanceAdvisor/namespaces`

Returns up to 20 namespaces for collections experiencing slow queries on the specified host. If you specify a secondary member of a replica set that hasn't received any database read operations, the endpoint doesn't return any namespaces.

<h3 id="return-all-namespaces-for-one-host-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|duration|query|integer(int64)|false|Length of time expressed during which the query finds suggested indexes among the managed namespaces in the cluster. This parameter expresses its value in milliseconds.<br><br>- If you don't specify the **since** parameter, the endpoint returns data covering the duration before the current time.<br>- If you specify neither the **duration** nor **since** parameters, the endpoint returns data from the previous 24 hours.|
|processId|path|string|true|Combination of host and port that serves the MongoDB process. The host must be the hostname, FQDN, IPv4 address, or IPv6 address of the host that runs the MongoDB process (`mongod` or `mongos`). The port must be the IANA port on which the MongoDB process listens for requests.|
|since|query|integer(int64)|false|Date and time from which the query retrieves the suggested indexes. This parameter expresses its value in the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since the [UNIX epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time).<br><br>- If you don't specify the **duration** parameter, the endpoint returns data covering from the **since** value and the current time.<br>- If you specify neither the **duration** nor the **since** parameters, the endpoint returns data from the previous 24 hours.|

## Return Slow Queries

<a id="opIdlistGroupProcessPerformanceAdvisorSlowQueryLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/processes/string/performanceAdvisor/slowQueryLogs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/processes/{processId}/performanceAdvisor/slowQueryLogs`

Returns log lines for slow queries that the Performance Advisor and Query Profiler identified. The Performance Advisor monitors queries that MongoDB considers slow and suggests new indexes to improve query performance. MongoDB Cloud bases the threshold for slow queries on the average time of operations on your cluster. This enables workload-relevant recommendations.

<h3 id="return-slow-queries-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|duration|query|integer(int64)|false|Length of time expressed during which the query finds slow queries among the managed namespaces in the cluster. This parameter expresses its value in milliseconds.<br><br>- If you don't specify the **since** parameter, the endpoint returns data covering the duration before the current time.<br>- If you specify neither the **duration** nor **since** parameters, the endpoint returns data from the previous 24 hours.|
|namespaces|query|[string]|false|Namespaces from which to retrieve slow queries. A namespace consists of one database and one collection resource written as `.`: `<database>.<collection>`. To include multiple namespaces, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each namespace. Omit this parameter to return results for all namespaces.|
|nLogs|query|integer(int64)|false|Maximum number of lines from the log to return.|
|processId|path|string|true|Combination of host and port that serves the MongoDB process. The host must be the hostname, FQDN, IPv4 address, or IPv6 address of the host that runs the MongoDB process (`mongod` or `mongos`). The port must be the IANA port on which the MongoDB process listens for requests.|
|since|query|integer(int64)|false|Date and time from which the query retrieves the slow queries. This parameter expresses its value in the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since the [UNIX epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time).<br><br>- If you don't specify the **duration** parameter, the endpoint returns data covering from the **since** value and the current time.<br>- If you specify neither the **duration** nor the **since** parameters, the endpoint returns data from the previous 24 hours.|
|includeMetrics|query|boolean|false|Whether or not to include metrics extracted from the slow query log as separate fields.|
|includeReplicaState|query|boolean|false|Whether or not to include the replica state of the host when the slow query log was generated as a separate field.|
|includeOpType|query|boolean|false|Whether or not to include the operation type (read/write/command) extracted from the slow query log as a separate field.|

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/serverless/{clusterName}/performanceAdvisor/autoIndexing`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Get whether the Serverless Auto Indexing feature is enabled. This endpoint returns a value for Flex clusters that were created with the Create Serverless Instance endpoint or Flex clusters that were migrated from Serverless instances. However, the value returned is not indicative of the Auto Indexing state as Auto Indexing is unavailable for Flex clusters. This endpoint will be sunset on January 22, 2026.

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/serverless/{clusterName}/performanceAdvisor/autoIndexing`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Set whether the Serverless Auto Indexing feature is enabled. This endpoint sets a value for Flex clusters that were created with the Create Serverless Instance endpoint or Flex clusters that were migrated from Serverless instances. However, the value returned is not indicative of the Auto Indexing state as Auto Indexing is unavailable for Flex clusters. This endpoint will be sunset on January 22, 2026.

## Create One Private Endpoint Service for One Provider

<a id="opIdcreateGroupPrivateEndpointEndpointService"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/privateEndpoint/endpointService \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "portMappingEnabled": false,
    "providerName": "AWS",
    "region": "string",
    "supportedRemoteRegions": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/privateEndpoint/endpointService`

Creates one private endpoint service for the specified cloud service provider. This cloud service provider manages the private endpoint service for the project. When you create a private endpoint service, MongoDB Cloud creates a network container in the project for the cloud provider for which you create the private endpoint service if one doesn't already exist. To learn more about private endpoint terminology in MongoDB Cloud, see Private Endpoint Concepts.

<a href="https://dochub.mongodb.org/core/private-endpoint-concepts">Private Endpoint Concepts</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "portMappingEnabled": false,
  "providerName": "AWS",
  "region": "string",
  "supportedRemoteRegions": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-private-endpoint-service-for-one-provider-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[CloudProviderEndpointServiceRequest](#schemacloudproviderendpointservicerequest)|true|Creates one private endpoint for the specified cloud service provider.|
|» portMappingEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether this endpoint service uses PSC port-mapping. This is only applicable for GCP Private Endpoint Services.|
|» providerName|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cloud service provider for which you want to create the private endpoint service.|
|» region|body|string|true|Cloud provider region in which you want to create the private endpoint service. Regions accepted as values differ for [Amazon Web Services](https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/reference/amazon-aws/), [Google Cloud Platform](https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/reference/google-gcp/), and [Microsoft Azure](https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/reference/microsoft-azure/).|
|» supportedRemoteRegions|body|[string]|false|List of regions that the endpoint service supports. Native cross region support is implemented for AWS only.|

## Toggle Regionalized Private Endpoint Status

<a id="opIdtoggleGroupPrivateEndpointRegionalMode"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/privateEndpoint/regionalMode \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/privateEndpoint/regionalMode`

Enables or disables the ability to create multiple private endpoints per region in all cloud service providers in one project. The cloud service provider manages the private endpoints for the project. Connection strings to existing multi-region and global sharded clusters change when you enable this setting. You must update your applications to use the new connection strings. This might cause downtime. Once enabled, you cannot create replica sets. To use this resource, all clusters in the deployment must be sharded clusters.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="toggle-regionalized-private-endpoint-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[ProjectSettingItemView](#schemaprojectsettingitemview)|true|Enables or disables the ability to create multiple private endpoints per region in all cloud service providers in one project.|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|Flag that indicates whether someone enabled the regionalized private endpoint setting for the specified project.<br><br>- Set this value to `true` to enable regionalized private endpoints. This allows you to create more than one private endpoint in a cloud provider region. You need to enable this setting to connect to multi-region and global MongoDB Cloud sharded clusters. Enabling regionalized private endpoints introduces the following limitations:<br>  - Your applications must use the new connection strings for existing multi-region and global sharded clusters. This might cause downtime.<br>  - Your MongoDB Cloud project can't contain replica sets nor can you create new replica sets in this project.<br><br>  - You can't disable this setting if you have:<br>    - more than one private endpoint in more than one region<br>    - more than one private endpoint in one region and one private endpoint in one or more regions.<br><br>- Set this value to `false` to disable regionalized private endpoints.|

> Example responses

}
```

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-programmatic-api-keys">Programmatic API Keys</h1>

Returns, adds, edits, and removes access tokens to use the MongoDB Cloud API. MongoDB Cloud applies these keys to organizations. These resources can return, assign, or revoke use of these keys within a specified project.

## Update Organization API Key Roles for One Project

<a id="opIdupdateGroupApiKeyRoles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/apiKeys/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "desc": "string",
    "roles": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/apiKeys/{apiUserId}`

Updates the roles of the organization API key that you specify for the project that you specify. You must specify at least one valid role for the project. The application removes any roles that you do not include in this request if they were previously set in the organization API key that you specify for the project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "desc": "string",
  "roles": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-organization-api-key-roles-for-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pageNum|query|integer|false|Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns.|
|itemsPerPage|query|integer|false|Number of items that the response returns per page.|
|includeCount|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud calculates the total number of items for the response. When set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may skip an additional count operation. The response may still include `totalCount` when the count is available without additional calculation.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|apiUserId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies this organization API key that you want to unassign from one project.|
|body|body|[UpdateAtlasProjectApiKey](#schemaupdateatlasprojectapikey)|true|Organization API Key to be updated. This request requires a minimum of one of the two body parameters.|
|» desc|body|string|false|Purpose or explanation provided when someone creates this project API key.|

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/apiKeys/{apiUserId}`

Updates one organization API key in the specified organization. The organization API keys  grant programmatic access to an organization.

<a href="https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/configure-api-access/#std-label-atlas-prog-api-key">Programmatic API Keys</a>

  "desc": "string",
  "roles": [
    "ORG_OWNER"
  ]
}

|---|---|---|---|---|

To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-project-ip-access-list">Project IP Access List</h1>

Returns, adds, edits, and removes network access limits to database deployments in Atlas. This resource replaces the whitelist resource. Atlas removed whitelists in July 2021. Update your applications to use this new resource. This resource manages a project's IP Access List and supports creating temporary Access List entries that automatically expire within a user-configurable 7-day period.

## Return All Project IP Access List Entries

<a id="opIdlistGroupAccessListEntries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/accessList \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/accessList`

Returns all access list entries from the specified project's IP access list. Each entry in the project's IP access list contains either one IP address or one CIDR-notated block of IP addresses. MongoDB Cloud only allows client connections to the cluster from entries in the project's IP access list. This resource replaces the whitelist resource. MongoDB Cloud removed whitelists in July 2021. Update your applications to use this new resource. The `/groups/{GROUP-ID}/accessList` endpoint manages the database IP access list. This endpoint is distinct from the `orgs/{ORG-ID}/apiKeys/{API-KEY-ID}/accesslist` endpoint, which manages the access list for MongoDB Cloud organizations.

<a href="https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/security/ip-access-list/#std-label-access-list">IP access list</a>

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/accessList`

## Remove One Entry from One Project IP Access List

<a id="opIddeleteGroupAccessListEntry"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/accessList/IPv4%3A%20192.0.2.0%252F24%20or%20IPv6%3A%202001%3Adb8%3A85a3%3A8d3%3A1319%3A8a2e%3A370%3A7348%20or%20IPv4%20CIDR%3A%20198.51.100.0%252f24%20or%20IPv6%20CIDR%3A%202001%3Adb8%3A%3A%252f58%20or%20AWS%20SG%3A%20sg-903004f8 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/accessList/{entryValue}`

Removes one access list entry from the specified project's IP access list. Each entry in the project's IP access list contains one IP address, one CIDR-notated block of IP addresses, or one AWS Security Group ID. MongoDB Cloud only allows client connections to the cluster from entries in the project's IP access list. This resource replaces the whitelist resource. MongoDB Cloud removed whitelists in July 2021. Update your applications to use this new resource. The `/groups/{GROUP-ID}/accessList` endpoint manages the database IP access list. This endpoint is distinct from the `orgs/{ORG-ID}/apiKeys/{API-KEY-ID}/accesslist` endpoint, which manages the access list for MongoDB Cloud organizations.

<a href="https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/security/ip-access-list/#std-label-access-list">IP access list</a>

<h3 id="remove-one-entry-from-one-project-ip-access-list-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|entryValue|path|string|true|Access list entry that you want to remove from the project's IP access list. This value can use one of the following: one AWS security group ID, one IP address, or one CIDR block of addresses. For CIDR blocks that use a subnet mask, replace the forward slash (`/`) with its URL-encoded value (`%2F`). When you remove an entry from the IP access list, existing connections from the removed address or addresses may remain open for a variable amount of time. The amount of time it takes MongoDB Cloud to close the connection depends upon several factors, including:<br><br>- how your application established the connection,<br>- how MongoDB Cloud or the driver using the address behaves, and<br>- which protocol (like TCP or UDP) the connection uses.|

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/accessList/{entryValue}/status`

Returns the status of one project IP access list entry. This resource checks if the provided project IP access list entry applies to all cloud providers serving clusters from the specified project.

<h3 id="return-status-of-one-project-ip-access-list-entry-parameters">Parameters</h3>

To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|

Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|

curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups \

  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "orgId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",

    "tags": [
      {
        "key": "string",
        "value": "string"
      }
    ],
    "withDefaultAlertsSettings": true
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups`

Creates one project. Projects group clusters into logical collections that support an application environment, workload, or both. Each project can have its own users, teams, security, tags, and alert settings.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "orgId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "regionUsageRestrictions": "COMMERCIAL_FEDRAMP_REGIONS_ONLY",
  "tags": [
    {
      "key": "string",
      "value": "string"
    }
  ],
  "withDefaultAlertsSettings": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|projectOwnerId|query|string|false|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the MongoDB Cloud user to whom to grant the Project Owner role on the specified project. If you set this parameter, it overrides the default value of the oldest Organization Owner.|
|body|body|[Group](#schemagroup)|true|Creates one project.|
|» name|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the project included in the MongoDB Cloud organization.|
|» orgId|body|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the MongoDB Cloud organization to which the project belongs.|
|» regionUsageRestrictions|body|string|false|Applies to Atlas for Government only.<br><br>In Commercial Atlas, this field will be rejected in requests and missing in responses.<br><br>This field sets restrictions on available regions in the project.<br><br>`COMMERCIAL_FEDRAMP_REGIONS_ONLY`: Only allows deployments in FedRAMP Moderate regions.<br><br>`GOV_REGIONS_ONLY`: Only allows deployments in GovCloud regions.|
|» tags|body|[[ResourceTag](#schemaresourcetag)]|false|List that contains key-value pairs between 1 to 255 characters in length for tagging and categorizing the project.|
|» withDefaultAlertsSettings|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to create the project with default alert settings.|

#### Enumerated Values

## Add One MongoDB Cloud User to One Project

<a id="opIdaddGroupAccessUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/access \
  -X POST \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "roles": [
      "string"
    ],
    "username": "user@example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/access`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Adds one MongoDB Cloud user to the specified project. If the MongoDB Cloud user is not a member of the project's organization, then the user must accept their invitation to the organization to access information within the specified project. If the MongoDB Cloud User is already a member of the project's organization, then they will be added to the project immediately and an invitation will not be returned by this resource.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "roles": [
    "string"
  ],
  "username": "user@example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="add-one-mongodb-cloud-user-to-one-project-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|body|body|[GroupInvitationRequest](#schemagroupinvitationrequest)|true|Adds one MongoDB Cloud user to the specified project.|

curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/settings \

  }'

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/settings`

Updates the settings of the specified project. You can update any of the options available. MongoDB cloud only updates the options provided in the request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "isAtlasHomePageAiAssistantEnabled": true,
  "isClusterAiAssistantEnabled": true,
  "isCollectDatabaseSpecificsStatisticsEnabled": true,
  "isDataExplorerEnabled": true,

  "isPerformanceAdvisorEnabled": true,
  "isRealtimePerformancePanelEnabled": true,
  "isSchemaAdvisorEnabled": true
}

To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|

Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|

|» isDataExplorerEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to enable the Data Explorer for the specified project.|

|» isDataExplorerGenAISampleDocumentPassingEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to enable the passing of sample field values with the use of generative AI features in the Data Explorer for the specified project.|

|» isExtendedStorageSizesEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to enable extended storage sizes for the specified project.|

|» isPerformanceAdvisorEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to enable the Performance Advisor and Profiler for the specified project.|
|» isRealtimePerformancePanelEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to enable the Real Time Performance Panel for the specified project.|

## Migrate One Project to Another Organization

<a id="opIdmigrateGroup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8:migrate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2024-05-30+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "destinationOrgId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
    "destinationOrgPrivateApiKey": "55c3bbb6-b4bb-0be1-e66d20841f3e",
    "destinationOrgPublicApiKey": "zmmrboas"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}:migrate`

Migrates a project from its current organization to another organization. All project users and their roles will be copied to the same project in the destination organization. You must include an organization API key with the Organization Owner role for the destination organization to verify access to the destination organization when you authenticate with Programmatic API Keys. Otherwise, the requesting user must have the Organization Owner role in both organizations.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "destinationOrgId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "destinationOrgPrivateApiKey": "55c3bbb6-b4bb-0be1-e66d20841f3e",
  "destinationOrgPublicApiKey": "zmmrboas"
}
```

<h3 id="migrate-one-project-to-another-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|body|body|[GroupMigrationRequest](#schemagroupmigrationrequest)|true|Migrates a project from its current organization to another organization.|
|» destinationOrgId|body|string|false|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization to move the specified project to.|
|» destinationOrgPrivateApiKey|body|string|false|Unique string that identifies the private part of the API Key used to verify access to the destination organization. This parameter is required only when you authenticate with Programmatic API Keys.|
|» destinationOrgPublicApiKey|body|string|false|Unique string that identifies the public part of the API Key used to verify access to the destination organization. This parameter is required only when you authenticate with Programmatic API Keys.|

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/byName/{groupName}`

Returns details about the specified project. Projects group clusters into logical collections that support an application environment, workload, or both. Each project can have its own users, teams, security, tags, and alert settings.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|groupName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies this project.|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-push-based-log-export">Push-Based Log Export</h1>

You can continually export mongod, mongos, and audit logs to an AWS S3 bucket. The new `/logIntegrations` API provides 1-minute log export on a best-effort basis. The existing `/pushBasedLogExport` API provides 5-minute log export and will be deprecated in the future. The log export integrations are managed at the project level.

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-query-sampling">Query Sampling</h1>

Starts, returns, and stops query sampling on one namespace of one cluster. Sampled queries feed the shard key analysis for the namespace.

## Create Query Sampling for One Namespace

<a id="opIdcreateGroupClusterQuerySampling"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/querySampling \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2025-03-12+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "sales.orders"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/querySampling`

Starts query sampling on one namespace of the specified cluster. Sampled queries feed the shard key analysis for the namespace. The response reports the observed sampling state, in which `active` may still be false: the cluster applies the sampling configuration asynchronously.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "sales.orders"
}
```

<h3 id="create-query-sampling-for-one-namespace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[QuerySamplingCreateRequest](#schemaquerysamplingcreaterequest)|true|Namespace on which to start query sampling.|
|» namespace|body|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the namespace (`<database>.<collection>`) on which to sample queries.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "namespace": "sales.orders",
  "sampledReadsBytes": 0,
  "sampledReadsCount": 0,
  "sampledWritesBytes": 0,
  "sampledWritesCount": 0,
  "samplesPerSecond": 0,
  "startTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "detail": "(This is just an example, the exception may not be related to this endpoint) No provider AWS exists.",
  "error": 400,
  "errorCode": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
  "reason": "Bad Request"
}
```

> 401 Response

## Return Query Sampling State for One Namespace

<a id="opIdgetGroupClusterQuerySampling"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/querySampling/sales.orders \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/querySampling/{namespace}`

Returns the query sampling state of one namespace of the specified cluster, including counters for the operations sampled so far. Returns 404 if query sampling is not configured on the namespace. `active` becomes true asynchronously after query sampling starts.

<h3 id="return-query-sampling-state-for-one-namespace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|namespace|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the namespace (`<database>.<collection>`) on which queries are sampled.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-rate-limiting">Rate Limiting</h1>

Returns details about rate limit policies for the Atlas Administration API.

<a href="http://dochub.mongodb.org/core/atlas-api-rate-limit">Atlas API Rate Limits documentation</a>

## Return All Rate Limits

<a id="opIdlistRateLimits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/rateLimits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/rateLimits`

Get all rate limits for all v2 Atlas Administration API endpoint sets.

<h3 id="return-all-rate-limits-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|itemsPerPage|query|integer|false|Number of items that the response returns per page.|
|pageNum|query|integer|false|Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|query|string|false|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the Atlas Project to request rate limits for. When this parameter is provided, only group scoped endpoint sets are returned and the limits returned are applicable to the specified project. The requesting user must have the Project Read Only role for the specified project.|
|orgId|query|string|false|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the Atlas Organization to request rate limits for. When this parameter is provided, only organization scoped endpoint sets are returned and the limits returned are applicable to the specified organization. The requesting user must have the Organization Read Only role for the specified organization.|
|userId|query|string|false|A string that identifies the Atlas user to request rate limits for. The ID can for example be the Service Account Client ID or the API Public Key. When this parameter is provided, only user scoped endpoint sets are returned and the limits returned are applicable to the specified user. The requesting user must be the same as the specified user.|
|ipAddress|query|string|false|An IP address to request rate limits for. When this parameter is provided, only IP scoped endpoint sets are returned and the limits returned are applicable to the specified IP address. The requesting user must have the same IP address as the one provided in the request.|
|name|query|string|false|Filters the returned endpoint sets by the provided endpoint set name. Multiple names may be provided, for example `/rateLimits?name=Name1&name=Name2`. For names that use spaces, replace the space with its URL-encoded value (`%20`).|
|endpointPath|query|string|false|Filters the returned endpoint sets by the provided endpoint path. Multiple paths may be provided, for example `/rateLimits?endpointPath=%2Fapi%2Fatlas%2Fv2%2Fclusters&endpointPath=%2Fapi%2Fatlas%2Fv2%2Fgroups%2F%7BgroupId%7D%2F`. Replace `/`, `{` and `}` with their URL-encoded values (`%2F`, `%7B` and `%7D` respectively).|

## Create One Atlas Resource Policy

<a id="opIdcreateOrgResourcePolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/orgs/4888442a3354817a7320eb61/resourcePolicies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2024-08-05+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "policies": [
      {
        "body": "  forbid (\n    principal,\n    action == cloud::Action::\"cluster.createEdit\",\n    resource\n  ) when {\n   context.cluster.regions.contains(cloud::region::\"aws:us-east-1\")\n  };\n"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-rolling-index">Rolling Index</h1>

Creates one index to a database deployment in a rolling manner. Rolling indexes build indexes on the applicable nodes sequentially and may reduce the performance impact of an index build if your deployment's average CPU utilization exceeds (N-1)/N-10% where N is the number of CPU threads available to mongod of if the WiredTiger cache fill ratio regularly exceeds 90%. If your deployment does not meet this criteria, use the default index build. You can't create a rolling index on an `M0` free cluster or `M2/M5` shared cluster.

## Create One Rolling Index

<a id="opIdcreateGroupClusterIndexRollingIndex"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/index \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "collation": {
      "alternate": "non-ignorable",
      "backwards": false,
      "caseFirst": "lower",
      "caseLevel": false,
      "locale": "af",
      "maxVariable": "punct",
      "normalization": false,
      "numericOrdering": false,
      "strength": 3
    },
    "collection": "accounts",
    "db": "sample_airbnb",
    "keys": [
      {
        "property_type": "1"
      }
    ],
    "options": {
      "name": "PartialIndexTest",
      "partialFilterExpression": {
        "limit": {
          "$gt": 900
        }
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/index`

Creates an index on the cluster identified by its name in a rolling manner. Creating the index in this way allows index builds on one replica set member as a standalone at a time, starting with the secondary members. Creating indexes in this way requires at least one replica set election.

<a href="https://docs.mongodb.com/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-replica-sets/">Rolling Index Builds on Replica Sets</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "collation": {
    "alternate": "non-ignorable",
    "backwards": false,
    "caseFirst": "lower",
    "caseLevel": false,
    "locale": "af",
    "maxVariable": "punct",
    "normalization": false,
    "numericOrdering": false,
    "strength": 3
  },
  "collection": "accounts",
  "db": "sample_airbnb",
  "keys": [
    {
      "property_type": "1"
    }
  ],
  "options": {
    "name": "PartialIndexTest",
    "partialFilterExpression": {
      "limit": {
        "$gt": 900
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-rolling-index-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster on which MongoDB Cloud creates an index.|
|body|body|[DatabaseRollingIndexRequest](#schemadatabaserollingindexrequest)|true|Rolling index to create on the specified cluster.|
|» collation|body|[Collation](#schemacollation)|false|One or more settings that specify language-specific rules to compare strings within this index.|
|» collection|body|string|true|Human-readable label of the collection for which MongoDB Cloud creates an index.|
|» db|body|string|true|Human-readable label of the database that holds the collection on which MongoDB Cloud creates an index.|
|» keys|body|[object]|true|List that contains one or more objects that describe the parameters that you want to index.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|Key-value pair that sets the parameter to index as the key and the type of index as its value. To create a [multi-key index](https://docs.mongodb.com/manual/core/index-multikey/), list each parameter in its own object within this array.|
|» options|body|[IndexOptions](#schemaindexoptions)|false|One or more settings that determine how the MongoDB Cloud creates this MongoDB index.|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-sandbox">Sandbox</h1>

## Return All Serverless Instances in One Project

<a id="opIdlistGroupServerlessInstances"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/serverless \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/serverless`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Returns details for all serverless instances in the specified project.

This endpoint also lists Flex clusters that were created using the [Create Serverless Instance](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Serverless-Instances/operation/createServerlessInstance) endpoint or former Serverless instances that have been migrated to Flex clusters, until January 15, 2026 after which this endpoint will begin returning an empty list. The endpoint will be removed entirely on January 15, 2027. Continuous backups are not supported and `serverlessContinuousBackupEnabled` will not take effect on these clusters. Please use the List Flex Clusters endpoint instead.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Flex-Clusters/operation/listFlexClusters">List Flex Clusters</a>

<h3 id="return-all-serverless-instances-in-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|includeCount|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud calculates the total number of items for the response. When set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may skip an additional count operation. The response may still include `totalCount` when the count is available without additional calculation.|
|itemsPerPage|query|integer|false|Number of items that the response returns per page.|

This API can also be used on Flex clusters that were created with the [Create Serverless Instance](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Serverless-Instances/operation/createServerlessInstance) endpoint or Flex clusters that were migrated from Serverless instances. Continuous backups are not supported and `serverlessContinuousBackupEnabled` will not take effect on these clusters. This endpoint will be sunset on January 15, 2027. Please use the Get Flex Cluster endpoint instead.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/api-resources-spec/v2/#tag/Flex-Clusters/operation/getFlexCluster">Get Flex Cluster</a>

<h3 id="return-one-serverless-instance-from-one-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|name|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the serverless instance.|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-service-accounts">Service Accounts</h1>

## Create One Project Service Account

<a id="opIdcreateGroupServiceAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/serviceAccounts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2024-08-05+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "roles": [
      "string"
    ],
    "secretExpiresAfterHours": 8,
    "withoutInitialSecret": false
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/serviceAccounts`

Creates one Service Account for the specified Project. The Service Account will automatically be added as an Organization Member to the Organization that the specified Project is a part of.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "roles": [
    "string"
  ],
  "secretExpiresAfterHours": 8,
  "withoutInitialSecret": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-project-service-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[GroupServiceAccountRequest](#schemagroupserviceaccountrequest)|true|Details of the new Service Account.|
|» description|body|string|true|Human readable description for the Service Account.|
|» name|body|string|true|Human-readable name for the Service Account. The name is modifiable and does not have to be unique.|
|» roles|body|[string]|true|A list of project-level roles for the Service Account.|
|» secretExpiresAfterHours|body|integer(int32) \| null|false|The expiration time of the new Service Account secret, provided in hours. The minimum and maximum allowed expiration times are subject to change and are controlled by the organization's settings. Required unless `withoutInitialSecret` is true.|
|» withoutInitialSecret|body|boolean|false|If true, creates the Service Account without generating an initial secret. `secretExpiresAfterHours` must not be set when this is true. Defaults to false, which preserves existing behavior: a secret is generated and returned in the response. Use the `CreateGroupServiceAccountSecret` endpoint to add a secret later.|
