## Create One Organization Service Account

<a id="opIdcreateOrgServiceAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/orgs/4888442a3354817a7320eb61/serviceAccounts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2024-08-05+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "roles": [
      "ORG_MEMBER"
    ],
    "secretExpiresAfterHours": 8,
    "withoutInitialSecret": false
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/serviceAccounts`

Creates one Service Account for the specified Organization.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "roles": [
    "ORG_MEMBER"
  ],
  "secretExpiresAfterHours": 8,
  "withoutInitialSecret": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-organization-service-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|orgId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization that contains your projects. Use the [`/orgs`](#tag/Organizations/operation/listOrganizations) endpoint to retrieve all organizations to which the authenticated user has access.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[OrgServiceAccountRequest](#schemaorgserviceaccountrequest)|true|Details of the new Service Account.|
|» description|body|string|true|Human readable description for the Service Account.|
|» name|body|string|true|Human-readable name for the Service Account. The name is modifiable and does not have to be unique.|
|» roles|body|[string]|true|A list of organization-level roles for the Service Account.|
|» secretExpiresAfterHours|body|integer(int32) \| null|false|The expiration time of the new Service Account secret, provided in hours. The minimum and maximum allowed expiration times are subject to change and are controlled by the organization's settings. Required unless `withoutInitialSecret` is true.|
|» withoutInitialSecret|body|boolean|false|If true, creates the Service Account without generating an initial secret. `secretExpiresAfterHours` must not be set when this is true. Defaults to false, which preserves existing behavior: a secret is generated and returned in the response. Use the `CreateOrgServiceAccountSecret` endpoint to add a secret later.|

|» roles|ORG_OWNER|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-shard-key-analyzer">Shard Key Analyzer</h1>

Analyzes how well a candidate shard key would distribute a collection across the shards of a cluster. Analyzing a shard key samples documents on a live cluster and does not finish within one request, so it is submitted as a long-running operation: the request returns an operation to poll, and the completed analysis is a separate resource that the operation links to. To receive the most common shard key values, you must have the Project Data Access Read Only role or higher. Otherwise, MongoDB Cloud omits those values, because they come from the collection's data rather than from statistics about it.

## Return All Shard Key Analyses for One Cluster

<a id="opIdlistGroupClusterShardKeyAnalyses"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/shardKeyAnalyses \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/shardKeyAnalyses`

Returns all completed shard key analyses for the specified cluster, newest first. An analysis appears here only once the operation that produced it has succeeded, so attempts that failed or are still running are absent; read the operations sub-resource to see those. MongoDB Cloud retains an analysis for 30 days.

<h3 id="return-all-shard-key-analyses-for-one-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|includeCount|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud calculates the total number of items for the response. When set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may skip an additional count operation. The response may still include `totalCount` when the count is available without additional calculation.|
|itemsPerPage|query|integer|false|Number of items that the response returns per page.|
|pageNum|query|integer|false|Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster with the shard key analyses you want to return.|

## Create One Shard Key Analysis for One Cluster

<a id="opIdcreateGroupClusterShardKeyAnalysis"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/shardKeyAnalyses \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2025-03-12+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "includeKeyCharacteristics": true,
    "includeReadWriteDistribution": false,
    "namespace": "sales.orders",
    "shardKey": [
      {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/shardKeyAnalyses`

Analyzes how well one candidate shard key would distribute one collection across the shards of the specified cluster. This endpoint accepts the request and returns immediately: the `Location` header carries the URI of the operation that tracks the analysis. Poll that operation until its `status` is terminal, then follow its `resultHref` to read the analysis. MongoDB Cloud validates and authorizes the request before accepting it, so a rejected submission returns a `4xx` status and never an operation in a failed state. A namespace that is well formed but absent cannot be detected before the analysis runs and surfaces as a failed operation.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "includeKeyCharacteristics": true,
  "includeReadWriteDistribution": false,
  "namespace": "sales.orders",
  "shardKey": [
    {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-shard-key-analysis-for-one-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster that contains the collection to analyze.|
|body|body|[ShardKeyAnalysisRequest](#schemashardkeyanalysisrequest)|true|Shard key to analyze, and which metrics to compute for it.|
|» includeKeyCharacteristics|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to return the cardinality, frequency and monotonicity of the candidate shard key.|
|» includeReadWriteDistribution|body|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether to return how reads and writes would be routed across shards under the candidate shard key. This requires query sampling to have collected operations for the namespace.|
|» namespace|body|string|true|Combination of the database and collection to analyze, written as `<database>.<collection>`.|
|» shardKey|body|[object]|true|Candidate shard key, given as one object per shard key field in the order the fields form the key. Field order is significant: `[{"a": "1"}, {"b": "1"}]` and `[{"b": "1"}, {"a": "1"}]` are different shard keys. At most one field may be `hashed`.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|Key-value pair that sets one shard key field as the key and how to index it as its value. Use `1` for an ascending range-based field and `hashed` for a hashed field. MongoDB rejects any other value.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "detail": "(This is just an example, the exception may not be related to this endpoint) No provider AWS exists.",
  "error": 400,
  "errorCode": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
  "reason": "Bad Request"
}
```

> 401 Response

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/shardKeyAnalyses/{analysisId}`

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/shardKeyAnalyses/operations`

Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|


`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/shardKeyAnalyses/operations/{operationId}`

Returns the progress of one shard key analysis for the specified cluster. Poll this resource until `status` reaches a terminal value. On success it carries `resultHref`, the URI of the analysis it created; on failure it carries `error`. While the status is not terminal it carries `retryAfterSeconds`, how long to wait before polling again. MongoDB Cloud retains an operation for 30 days past its terminal state.

Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-sharding-insights">Sharding Insights</h1>

Returns the cluster-level sharding state of one sharded cluster, including the balancer state, config server availability, and the configured balancing window.

## Return All Shards in One Cluster

<a id="opIdlistGroupClusterShardMetrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/shardMetrics \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/shardMetrics`

Returns the size and load of every shard in one sharded cluster. Each shard reports the data it stores, the CPU utilization of its nodes, the read and write operations it served, and any conditions that MongoDB Cloud observed relative to the rest of the cluster. To retrieve more details about a shard such as the latency, cache throughput and open alerts, request with an exact replica set name.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/shardMetrics/{replicaSetName}`

## Return Measurements for One Shard

<a id="opIdgetGroupClusterShardMetricMeasurements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/shardMetrics/atlas-12vorz-shard-0/measurements \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/shardMetrics/{replicaSetName}/measurements`

Returns time series of the requested measurements for one shard of the specified sharded cluster. The series average the readings of the shard's member processes selected by `nodeType`. Responds with a 404 only when no shard with the given `replicaSetName` exists in the cluster; a shard that exists but has no readings yet returns series of `null` data points. Each series carries one data point per `granularity` interval, starting at `start` and not passing `end`. A data point's `value` is `null` when MongoDB Cloud has no reading for that interval; this includes the first minutes after a cluster or shard is created, before its metrics are collected, so `null` must not be read as zero load. Set `period`, or set both `start` and `end`; when neither is set, the response covers the last hour. A request whose window and `granularity` would produce more than 1000 data points per series is rejected.

<h3 id="return-measurements-for-one-shard-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|replicaSetName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the shard, as the replica set name of its members.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|m|query|[string]|false|One or more measurements to return. If omitted, the resource returns all measurements. To specify multiple values for `m`, repeat the `m` parameter for each value.|
|granularity|query|string|false|Interval between consecutive data points, in ISO 8601 duration format. If omitted, MongoDB Cloud chooses the resolution from the width of the window.|
|period|query|string|false|Duration over which Atlas reports the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 duration format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **start** and **end**.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud begins reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud stops reporting the metrics. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. Include this parameter when you do not set **period**.|
|nodeType|query|string|false|Members of the shard whose readings are averaged into the shard's series.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|m|SYSTEM_CPU|
|m|SYSTEM_MEMORY|
|m|SYSTEM_NETWORK|
|m|DISK_IOPS|
|m|DISK_LATENCY|
|m|DISK_THROUGHPUT|
|m|DISK_SPACE|
|m|CONNECTIONS|
|m|OPCOUNTERS|
|m|QUEUES|
|m|REPLICATION_LAG|
|granularity|PT30S|
|granularity|PT1M|
|granularity|PT3M|
|granularity|PT15M|
|granularity|PT1H|
|granularity|PT3H|
|nodeType|ALL|
|nodeType|PRIMARIES|
|nodeType|SECONDARIES|

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/shardMetrics:listMeasurements`

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-sharding-recommendations">Sharding Recommendations</h1>

Returns Sharding Advisor recommendations for one cluster. Recommendations describe changes that may improve the cluster's data distribution, such as adding shards or sharding a collection, together with the monitored conditions that produced them.

## Return Sharding Recommendations for One Cluster

<a id="opIdgetGroupClusterShardingRecommendations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/shardingRecommendations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/shardingRecommendations`

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/standbyLinks`

```bash
  }'
```

## Download Audit Logs for One Atlas Stream Processing Workspace

<a id="opIddownloadGroupStreamAuditLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/streams/string/auditLogs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/streams/{tenantName}/auditLogs`

Downloads the audit logs for the specified Atlas Streams Processing workspace or stream processor. By default, logs cover periods of 30 days. The API does not support direct calls with the json response schema. You must request a gzip response schema using an accept header of the format: `Accept: application/vnd.atlas.YYYY-MM-DD+gzip`.

<h3 id="download-audit-logs-for-one-atlas-stream-processing-workspace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|endDate|query|integer(int64)|false|Timestamp that specifies the end point for the range of log messages to download.  MongoDB Cloud expresses this timestamp in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch.|
|startDate|query|integer(int64)|false|Timestamp that specifies the starting point for the range of log messages to download. MongoDB Cloud expresses this timestamp in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch.|
|spName|query|string|false|Name of the stream processor to download logs for. An empty string will download logs for all stream processors in the workspace.|
|tenantName|path|string|true|Label that identifies the stream workspace.|

## Download Operational Logs for One Atlas Stream Processing Workspace

<a id="opIddownloadGroupStreamOperationalLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/streams/string:downloadOperationalLogs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/streams/{tenantName}:downloadOperationalLogs`

Downloads the operational logs for the specified Atlas Streams Processing workspace or stream processor. By default, logs cover periods of 30 days. The API does not support direct calls with the json response schema. You must request a gzip response schema using an accept header of the format: "Accept: application/vnd.atlas.2025-03-12+gzip".

<h3 id="download-operational-logs-for-one-atlas-stream-processing-workspace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|endDate|query|integer(int64)|false|Timestamp that specifies the end point for the range of log messages to download.  MongoDB Cloud expresses this timestamp in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch.|
|startDate|query|integer(int64)|false|Timestamp that specifies the starting point for the range of log messages to download. MongoDB Cloud expresses this timestamp in the number of seconds that have elapsed since the UNIX epoch.|
|spName|query|string|false|Name of the stream processor to download logs for. An empty string will download logs for all stream processors in the workspace.|
|tenantName|path|string|true|Label that identifies the stream workspace.|

<h3 id="create-one-private-link-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|

|body|body|[StreamsPrivateLinkConnection](#schemastreamsprivatelinkconnection)|true|Details to create one Private Link connection for a project.|
|» arn|body|string|false|Amazon Resource Name (ARN). Required for AWS Provider and MSK vendor.|
|» authenticationScheme|body|string|false|Authentication mechanism to use with this private networking connection.|
|» azureResourceIds|body|[string]|false|Azure Resource IDs of each availability zone for the Azure Confluent cluster.|
|» dnsDomain|body|string|false|The domain hostname. Required for the following provider and vendor combinations:<br>- AWS provider with CONFLUENT vendor.<br>- AZURE provider with EVENTHUB or CONFLUENT vendor.|
|» dnsSubDomain|body|[string]|false|Sub-Domain name of Confluent cluster. These are typically your availability zones. Required for AWS Provider and CONFLUENT vendor, if your AWS CONFLUENT cluster doesn't use subdomains, you must set this to the empty array [].|
|» gcpConnectionIds|body|[string]|false|List of GCP Private Service Connect connection IDs.|
|» gcpServiceAttachmentUris|body|[string]|false|Service Attachment URIs of each availability zone for the GCP Confluent cluster.|
|» provider|body|string|true|Cloud provider where the private endpoint's target resource is deployed. Valid values are AWS, AZURE, and GCP.|
|» region|body|string|false|The region of the Provider’s cluster. See [AWS](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/amazon-aws/#stream-processing-workspaces), [AZURE](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/microsoft-azure/#stream-processing-workspaces), and [GCP](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/google-gcp/#stream-processing-workspaces) supported regions.|
|» serviceEndpointId|body|string|false|For AZURE EVENTHUB, this is the [namespace endpoint ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/eventhub/namespaces/get). For AWS CONFLUENT cluster, this is the [VPC Endpoint service name](https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/networking/private-links/aws-privatelink.html).|
|» vendor|body|string|false|Vendor that manages the cloud service. The list of supported vendor values is:<br>- AWS<br>-- `MSK` for AWS MSK Kafka clusters<br>-- `CONFLUENT` for Confluent Kafka clusters on AWS<br>-- `KINESIS` for AWS Kinesis Data Streams<br>-- `S3` for AWS S3<br>-- `LAMBDA` for AWS Lambda<br><br>- Azure<br>-- `EVENTHUB` for Azure EventHub.<br>-- `CONFLUENT` for Confluent Kafka clusters on Azure<br>-- `AZURE_BLOB_STORAGE` for Azure Blob Storage<br><br>- GCP<br>-- `CONFLUENT` for Confluent Kafka clusters on GCP<br>-- `PUBSUB` for Google Cloud Pub/Sub<br><br>**NOTE** Omitting the vendor field will default to using the GENERIC vendor.|

## Return All Teams in One Organization

<a id="opIdlistOrgTeams"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/orgs/4888442a3354817a7320eb61/teams \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/teams`

Returns all teams that belong to the specified organization. Teams enable you to grant project access roles to MongoDB Cloud users. MongoDB Cloud only returns teams for which you have access.

<a href="https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/access/manage-teams-in-orgs/#std-label-manage-teams">Manage Organization Teams</a>

<h3 id="return-all-teams-in-one-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|itemsPerPage|query|integer|false|Number of items that the response returns per page.|
|includeCount|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud calculates the total number of items for the response. When set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may skip an additional count operation. The response may still include `totalCount` when the count is available without additional calculation.|
|pageNum|query|integer|false|Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns.|
|orgId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization that contains your projects. Use the [`/orgs`](#tag/Organizations/operation/listOrganizations) endpoint to retrieve all organizations to which the authenticated user has access.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|

## Create One Team in One Organization

<a id="opIdcreateOrgTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/orgs/4888442a3354817a7320eb61/teams \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "usernames": [
      "user@example.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/teams`

Creates one team in the specified organization. Teams enable you to grant project access roles to MongoDB Cloud users. MongoDB Cloud limits the number of teams to a maximum of 250 teams per organization.

<a href="https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/access/manage-teams-in-orgs/#std-label-manage-teams">Manage Organization Teams</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "usernames": [
    "user@example.com"
  ]
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|orgId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization that contains your projects. Use the [`/orgs`](#tag/Organizations/operation/listOrganizations) endpoint to retrieve all organizations to which the authenticated user has access.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[Team](#schemateam)|true|Team that you want to create in the specified organization.|

|» usernames|body|[string(email)]|true|List that contains the MongoDB Cloud users in this team.|

## Assign MongoDB Cloud Users in One Organization to One Team

<a id="opIdaddOrgTeamUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/orgs/4888442a3354817a7320eb61/teams/string/users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "id": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8"
    }
  ]'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/orgs/{orgId}/teams/{teamId}/users`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Adds one or more MongoDB Cloud users from the specified organization to the specified team. Teams enable you to grant project access roles to MongoDB Cloud users. You can assign up to 250 MongoDB Cloud users from one organization to one team.

**Note**: This endpoint is deprecated. Use [Add One MongoDB Cloud User to One Team](#tag/MongoDB-Cloud-Users/operation/addUserToTeam) to add an active or pending user to a team.

<a href="https://docs.atlas.mongodb.com/access/manage-teams-in-orgs/#std-label-manage-teams">Manage Organization Teams</a>

> Body parameter


<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-third-party-integrations">Third-Party Integrations</h1>

Returns, adds, edits, and removes third-party service integration configurations. MongoDB Cloud sends alerts to each third-party service that you configure.

**IMPORTANT**: Each project can only have one configuration per `integrationType`.

## Return All Active Third-Party Service Integrations

<a id="opIdlistGroupIntegrations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/integrations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/integrations`

Returns the settings that permit integrations with all configured third-party services. These settings apply to all databases managed in one MongoDB Cloud project.

`PUT /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/integrations/{integrationType}`

Updates the settings for configuring integration with one third-party service. These settings apply to all databases managed in one MongoDB Cloud project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "region": "US",
  "serviceKey": "****************************7890",
  "type": "PAGER_DUTY"
}
```

<h3 id="update-one-third-party-service-integration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|integrationType|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the service which you want to integrate with MongoDB Cloud.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|includeCount|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud calculates the total number of items for the response. When set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may skip an additional count operation. The response may still include `totalCount` when the count is available without additional calculation.|
|itemsPerPage|query|integer|false|Number of items that the response returns per page.|
|pageNum|query|integer|false|Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|body|body|[ThirdPartyIntegration](#schemathirdpartyintegration)|true|Third-party integration that you want to configure for your project.|
|» id|body|string \| null|false|Integration id.|
|» type|body|string|false|Integration type.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[PagerDuty](#schemapagerduty)|false|Details to integrate one PagerDuty account with one MongoDB Cloud project.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[Slack](#schemaslack)|false|Details to integrate one Slack account with one MongoDB Cloud project.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[Datadog](#schemadatadog)|false|Details to integrate one Datadog account with one MongoDB Cloud project.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[NewRelic](#schemanewrelic)|false|Details to integrate one New Relic account with one MongoDB Cloud project.<br><br>***IMPORTANT**: Effective Wednesday, June 16th, 2021, New Relic no longer supports the plugin-based integration with MongoDB. We do not recommend that you sign up for the plugin-based integration.<br><br>Consider configuring an alternative monitoring integration before June 16th to maintain visibility into your MongoDB deployments.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[OpsGenie](#schemaopsgenie)|false|Details to integrate one OpsGenie account with one MongoDB Cloud project.|

## Create One Third-Party Service Integration

<a id="opIdcreateGroupIntegration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/integrations/PAGER_DUTY \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "id": "string",
    "region": "US",
    "serviceKey": "****************************7890",
    "type": "PAGER_DUTY"
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/integrations/{integrationType}`

Adds the settings for configuring one third-party service integration. These settings apply to all databases managed in the specified MongoDB Cloud project. Each project can have only one configuration per `{INTEGRATION-TYPE}`.

> Body parameter

```json
  "region": "US",
```

## Remove One Third-Party Service Integration

<a id="opIddeleteGroupIntegration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/integrations/PAGER_DUTY \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/integrations/{integrationType}`

Removes the settings that permit configuring one third-party service integration. These settings apply to all databases managed in one MongoDB Cloud project. If you delete an integration from a project, you remove that integration configuration only for that project. This action doesn't affect any other project or organization's configured `{INTEGRATION-TYPE}` integrations.

<h3 id="remove-one-third-party-service-integration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|integrationType|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the service which you want to integrate with MongoDB Cloud.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|

<h1 id="mongodb-atlas-administration-api-x509-authentication">X.509 Authentication</h1>

Returns, edits, and removes user-managed X.509 configurations. Also returns and generates MongoDB Cloud-managed X.509 certificates for database users. The following resources help manage database users who authenticate using X.509 certificates. You can manage these X.509 certificates or let MongoDB Cloud do it for you. If MongoDB Cloud manages your certificates, it also manages your Certificate Authority and can generate certificates for your database users. No additional X.509 configuration is required. If you manage your certificates, you must provide a Certificate Authority and generate certificates for your database users.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-self-managed-x509/">Self-Managed X.509 Certificates</a>

## Return All X.509 Certificates Assigned to One Database User

<a id="opIdlistGroupDatabaseUserCerts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/databaseUsers/string/certs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/databaseUsers/{username}/certs`

Returns all unexpired X.509 certificates for the specified MongoDB user. This MongoDB user belongs to one project. Atlas manages these certificates and the MongoDB user.

<h3 id="return-all-x509-certificates-assigned-to-one-database-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|includeCount|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud calculates the total number of items for the response. When set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud may skip an additional count operation. The response may still include `totalCount` when the count is available without additional calculation.|
|itemsPerPage|query|integer|false|Number of items that the response returns per page.|
|pageNum|query|integer|false|Number of the page that displays the current set of the total objects that the response returns.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|username|path|string|true|Human-readable label that represents the MongoDB database user account whose certificates you want to return.|

## Create One X.509 Certificate for One Database User

<a id="opIdcreateGroupDatabaseUserCert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/databaseUsers/string/certs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "monthsUntilExpiration": 3
  }'
```

`POST /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/databaseUsers/{username}/certs`

Generates one X.509 certificate for the specified MongoDB user. Atlas manages the            certificate and MongoDB user that belong to one project.


To get MongoDB Cloud to generate a managed certificate for a database user, set `"x509Type" : "MANAGED"` on the desired MongoDB Database User.

If you are managing your own Certificate Authority (CA) in Self-Managed X.509 mode, you must generate certificates for database users using your own CA.

<a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-self-managed-x509/#std-label-self-managed-x509">Self-Managed X.509</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "monthsUntilExpiration": 3
}
```

<h3 id="create-one-x509-certificate-for-one-database-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|username|path|string|true|Human-readable label that represents the MongoDB database user account for whom to create a certificate.|
|body|body|[UserCert](#schemausercert)|true|Generates one X.509 certificate for the specified MongoDB user.|
|» monthsUntilExpiration|body|integer(int32)|false|Number of months that the certificate remains valid until it expires.|

## Disable Customer-Managed X.509

<a id="opIddisableGroupUserSecurityCustomerX509"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/userSecurity/customerX509 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/userSecurity/customerX509`

Clears the customer-managed X.509 settings on a project, including the uploaded Certificate Authority, which disables self-managed X.509.

 Updating this configuration triggers a rolling restart of the database. You must have the Project Owner role to use this endpoint.

To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|

## Return Query Shape Details

<a id="opIdgetGroupClusterQueryShapeInsightDetails"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/queryShapeInsights/string/details \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/queryShapeInsights/{queryShapeHash}/details`

Returns the metadata and statistics summary for a given query shape hash.

<h3 id="return-query-shape-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|since|query|integer(int64)|false|Date and time from which to retrieve query shape statistics. This parameter expresses its value in the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since the [UNIX epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time).<br><br>- If you don't specify the **until** parameter, the endpoint returns data covering from the **since** value and the current time.<br>- If you specify neither the **since** nor the **until** parameters, the endpoint returns data from the previous 24 hours.|
|until|query|integer(int64)|false|Date and time up until which to retrieve query shape statistics. This parameter expresses its value in the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since the [UNIX epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time).<br><br>- If you specify the **until** parameter, you must specify the **since** parameter.<br>- If you specify neither the **since** nor the **until** parameters, the endpoint returns data from the previous 24 hours.|
|processIds|query|[string]|false|Process IDs from which to retrieve query shape statistics. A `processId` is a combination of host and port that serves the MongoDB process. The host must be the hostname, FQDN, IPv4 address, or IPv6 address of the host that runs the MongoDB process (`mongod` or `mongos`). The port must be the IANA port on which the MongoDB process listens for requests. To include multiple `processIds`, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each `processId`.|
|queryShapeHash|path|string|true|A SHA256 hash of a query shape, output by MongoDB commands like `$queryStats` and `$explain` or slow query logs.|

## Return Query Statistic Summaries

<a id="opIdlistGroupClusterQueryShapeInsightSummaries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/queryShapeInsights/summaries \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/queryShapeInsights/summaries`

Returns a list of query shape statistics summaries for a given cluster. Query shape statistics provide performance insights about MongoDB queries, helping users identify problematic query patterns and potential optimizations.

<h3 id="return-query-statistic-summaries-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|since|query|integer(int64)|false|Date and time from which to retrieve query shape statistics. This parameter expresses its value in the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since the [UNIX epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time).<br><br>- If you don't specify the **until** parameter, the endpoint returns data covering from the **since** value and the current time.<br>- If you specify neither the **since** nor the **until** parameters, the endpoint returns data from the previous 24 hours.|
|until|query|integer(int64)|false|Date and time up until which to retrieve query shape statistics. This parameter expresses its value in the number of milliseconds that have elapsed since the [UNIX epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time).<br><br>- If you specify the **until** parameter, you must specify the **since** parameter.<br>- If you specify neither the **since** nor the **until** parameters, the endpoint returns data from the previous 24 hours.|
|processIds|query|[string]|false|Process IDs from which to retrieve query shape statistics. A `processId` is a combination of host and port that serves the MongoDB process. The host must be the hostname, FQDN, IPv4 address, or IPv6 address of the host that runs the MongoDB process (`mongod` or `mongos`). The port must be the IANA port on which the MongoDB process listens for requests. To include multiple `processId`, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each `processId`.|
|namespaces|query|[string]|false|Namespaces from which to retrieve query shape statistics. A namespace consists of one database and one collection resource written as `.`: `<database>.<collection>`. To include multiple namespaces, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each namespace. Omit this parameter to return results for all namespaces.|
|commands|query|[string]|false|Retrieve query shape statistics matching specified MongoDB commands. To include multiple commands, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each command. The currently supported parameters are: find, distinct, aggregate, count, insert, update, and delete. The insert, update, and delete commands return results only for clusters running MongoDB 9.0 or later with write query shape statistics enabled for the project. Omit this parameter to return results for all supported commands.|
|nSummaries|query|integer(int64)|false|Maximum number of query statistic summaries to return.|
|series|query|[string]|false|Query shape statistics data series to retrieve. A series represents a specific metric about query execution. To include multiple series, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each series. Omit this parameter to return results for all available series. The `P50_EXECUTION_TIME`, `P90_EXECUTION_TIME`, and `P99_EXECUTION_TIME` series are deprecated as the values they report may be inaccurate. They will be removed in a future release.|
|queryShapeHashes|query|[string]|false|A list of SHA256 hashes of desired query shapes, output by MongoDB commands like `$queryStats` and $explain or slow query logs. To include multiple series, pass the parameter multiple times delimited with an ampersand (`&`) between each series. Omit this parameter to return results for all available series.|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|

`GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/queryShapes`

## Update Query Shape Rejection Status

<a id="opIdupdateGroupClusterQueryShape"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2/groups/32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8/clusters/string/queryShapes/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.atlas.2025-03-12+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "status": "REJECTED"
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/clusters/{clusterName}/queryShapes/{queryShapeHash}`

Updates the rejection status of a query shape. Use this endpoint to reject a query shape (preventing it from executing on the cluster) or to unreject a previously rejected query shape (allowing it to execute again). This operation is idempotent: rejecting an already rejected query shape or unrejecting an already unrejected query shape will return 200 OK.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "status": "REJECTED"
}
```

<h3 id="update-query-shape-rejection-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|envelope|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an `envelope` JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body.|
|pretty|query|boolean|false|Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access.<br><br>**NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups.|
|clusterName|path|string|true|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|queryShapeHash|path|string|true|A SHA256 hash of a query shape, output by MongoDB commands like `$queryStats` and `$explain` or slow query logs.|
|body|body|[QueryShapeUpdateRequest](#schemaqueryshapeupdaterequest)|true|The desired rejection status for the query shape. Provide REJECTED to block the query shape from executing, or UNREJECTED to allow it to execute.|
|» status|body|string|true|The rejection status of a query shape. Use REJECTED to prevent the query shape from executing on the cluster, or UNREJECTED to allow it to execute.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|REJECTED|
|» status|UNREJECTED|

Collection of settings that configures the network container for a virtual private connection on Amazon Web Services.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the network peering container.|
|providerName|string|false|none|Cloud service provider that serves the requested network peering containers.|
|provisioned|boolean|false|read-only|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud clusters exist in the specified network peering container.|
|*oneOf*|[AzureCloudProviderContainer](#schemaazurecloudprovidercontainer)|false|none|Collection of settings that configures the network container for a virtual private connection on Amazon Web Services.|
|*oneOf*|[GCPCloudProviderContainer](#schemagcpcloudprovidercontainer)|false|none|Collection of settings that configures the network container for a virtual private connection on Amazon Web Services.|
|*oneOf*|[AWSCloudProviderContainer](#schemaawscloudprovidercontainer)|false|none|Collection of settings that configures the network container for a virtual private connection on Amazon Web Services.|
|atlasCidrBlock|string|false|none|IP addresses expressed in Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation that MongoDB Cloud uses for the network peering containers in your project. MongoDB Cloud assigns all of the project's clusters deployed to this cloud provider an IP address from this range. MongoDB Cloud locks this value if an M10 or greater cluster or a network peering connection exists in this project.<br><br>These CIDR blocks must fall within the ranges reserved per RFC 1918. AWS and Azure further limit the block to between the `/24` and  `/21` ranges.<br><br>To modify the CIDR block, the target project cannot have:<br><br>- Any M10 or greater clusters<br>- Any other VPC peering connections<br><br> You can also create a new project and create a network peering connection to set the desired MongoDB Cloud network peering container CIDR block for that project. MongoDB Cloud limits the number of MongoDB nodes per network peering connection based on the CIDR block and the region selected for the project.<br><br> **Example:** A project in an Amazon Web Services (AWS) region supporting three availability zones and an MongoDB CIDR network peering container block of limit of `/24` equals 27 three-node replica sets.|
|regionName|string|true|none|Geographic area that Amazon Web Services (AWS) defines to which MongoDB Cloud deployed this network peering container.|
|vpcId|string|false|read-only|Unique string that identifies the MongoDB Cloud VPC on AWS.|

Clusters always have this setting enabled.|

```json
  "ebsVolumeType": "STANDARD",
```

Hardware specifications for nodes deployed in the region.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|diskIOPS|integer(int32)|false|none|Target IOPS (Input/Output Operations Per Second) desired for storage attached to this hardware.<br><br> Change this parameter if you:<br><br>- set `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].providerName` to `AWS`.<br>- set `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].electableSpecs.instanceSize` to `M30` or greater (not including `Mxx_NVME` tiers).<br><br>- set `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].electableSpecs.ebsVolumeType` to `PROVISIONED`.<br><br>The maximum input/output operations per second (IOPS) depend on the selected `.instanceSize` and `.diskSizeGB`.<br>This parameter defaults to the cluster tier's standard IOPS value.<br>Changing this value impacts cluster cost.<br>MongoDB Cloud enforces minimum ratios of storage capacity to system memory for given cluster tiers. This keeps cluster performance consistent with large datasets.<br><br>- Instance sizes `M10` to `M40` have a ratio of disk capacity to system memory of 60:1.<br>- Instance sizes greater than `M40` have a ratio of 120:1.|
|diskThroughput|integer(int32)|false|read-only|Target throughput desired for storage attached to this hardware. Only returned for Gen 2 instance sizes with Standard (GP3) volume type.|
|ebsVolumeType|string|false|none|Type of storage you want to attach to your AWS-provisioned cluster.<br><br>- `STANDARD` volume types can't exceed the default input/output operations per second (IOPS) rate for the selected volume size. <br><br>- `PROVISIONED` volume types must fall within the allowable IOPS range for the selected volume size.<br><br>- `HIGH_PERFORMANCE` volume types use IO2 EBS volumes and must fall within the allowable IOPS range for the selected volume size.<br><br>NVMe clusters require either `PROVISIONED` or `HIGH_PERFORMANCE`.|
|instanceSize|string|false|none|Hardware specification for the instance sizes in this region. Each instance size has a default storage and memory capacity. The instance size you select applies to all the data-bearing hosts of the node type.|
|nodeCount|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of nodes of the given type for MongoDB Cloud to deploy to the region.|

Hardware specifications for nodes deployed in the region.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|diskIOPS|integer(int32)|false|none|Target IOPS (Input/Output Operations Per Second) desired for storage attached to this hardware.<br><br> You can set different IOPS values on different shards when provisioned IOPS are supported.<br><br> Change this parameter if you:<br><br>- set `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].providerName` to `AWS`.<br>- set `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].electableSpecs.instanceSize` to `M30` or greater (not including `Mxx_NVME` tiers).<br><br>- set `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].electableSpecs.ebsVolumeType` to `PROVISIONED`.<br><br>The maximum input/output operations per second (IOPS) depend on the selected `.instanceSize` and `.diskSizeGB`.<br>This parameter defaults to the cluster tier's standard IOPS value.<br>Changing this value impacts cluster cost.<br>MongoDB Cloud enforces minimum ratios of storage capacity to system memory for given cluster tiers. This keeps cluster performance consistent with large datasets.<br><br>- Instance sizes `M10` to `M40` have a ratio of disk capacity to system memory of 60:1.<br>- Instance sizes greater than `M40` have a ratio of 120:1.|
|diskSizeGB|number(double)|false|none|Storage capacity of instance data volumes expressed in gigabytes. Increase this number to add capacity.<br><br> This value must be equal for all shards and node types.<br><br> This value is not configurable on M0/M2/M5 clusters.<br><br> MongoDB Cloud requires this parameter if you set `replicationSpecs`.<br><br> If you specify a disk size below the minimum (10 GB), this parameter defaults to the minimum disk size value. <br><br> Storage charge calculations depend on whether you choose the default value or a custom value.<br><br> The maximum value for disk storage cannot exceed 50 times the maximum RAM for the selected cluster. If you require more storage space, consider upgrading your cluster to a higher tier.|
|diskThroughput|integer(int32)|false|read-only|Target throughput desired for storage attached to this hardware. Only returned for Gen 2 instance sizes with Standard (GP3) volume type.|
|ebsVolumeType|string|false|none|Type of storage you want to attach to your AWS-provisioned cluster.<br><br>- `STANDARD` volume types can't exceed the default input/output operations per second (IOPS) rate for the selected volume size. <br><br>- `PROVISIONED` volume types must fall within the allowable IOPS range for the selected volume size.<br><br>- `HIGH_PERFORMANCE` volume types use IO2 EBS volumes and must fall within the allowable IOPS range for the selected volume size.<br><br>NVMe clusters require either `PROVISIONED` or `HIGH_PERFORMANCE`.|
|instanceSize|string|false|none|Hardware specification for the instance sizes in this region in this shard. Each instance size has a default storage and memory capacity. Electable nodes and read-only nodes (known as "base nodes") within a single shard must use the same instance size. Analytics nodes can scale independently from base nodes within a shard. Both base nodes and analytics nodes can scale independently from their equivalents in other shards.|
|nodeCount|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of nodes of the given type for MongoDB Cloud to deploy to the region.|

```json
}
```

Amazon Web Services (AWS) KMS configuration details and encryption at rest configuration set for the specified project.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accessKeyID|string|false|none|Unique alphanumeric string that identifies an Identity and Access Management (IAM) access key with permissions required to access your Amazon Web Services (AWS) Customer Master Key (CMK).|
|customerMasterKeyID|string|false|none|Unique alphanumeric string that identifies the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Customer Master Key (CMK) you used to encrypt and decrypt the MongoDB master keys.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether someone enabled encryption at rest for the specified project through Amazon Web Services (AWS) Key Management Service (KMS). To disable encryption at rest using customer key management and remove the configuration details, pass only this parameter with a value of `false`.|
|region|string|false|none|Physical location where MongoDB Cloud deploys your AWS-hosted MongoDB cluster nodes. The region you choose can affect network latency for clients accessing your databases. When MongoDB Cloud deploys a dedicated cluster, it checks if a VPC or VPC connection exists for that provider and region. If not, MongoDB Cloud creates them as part of the deployment. MongoDB Cloud assigns the VPC a CIDR block. To limit a new VPC peering connection to one CIDR block and region, create the connection first. Deploy the cluster after the connection starts.|

Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|electableSpecs|[HardwareSpec](#schemahardwarespec)|false|none|Hardware specifications for all electable nodes deployed in the region. Electable nodes can become the primary and can enable local reads. If you don't specify this option, MongoDB Cloud deploys no electable nodes to the region.|
|priority|integer(int32)|false|none|Precedence is given to this region when a primary election occurs. If your `regionConfigs` has only `readOnlySpecs`, `analyticsSpecs`, or both, set this value to `0`. If you have multiple `regionConfigs` objects (your cluster is multi-region or multi-cloud), they must have priorities in descending order. The highest priority is `7`.<br><br>**Example:** If you have three regions, their priorities would be `7`, `6`, and `5` respectively. If you added two more regions for supporting electable nodes, the priorities of those regions would be `4` and `3` respectively.|
|providerName|string|false|none|Cloud service provider on which MongoDB Cloud provisions the hosts. Set dedicated clusters to `AWS`, `GCP`, `AZURE` or `TENANT`.|
|regionName|object|false|none|Physical location of your MongoDB cluster nodes. The region you choose can affect network latency for clients accessing your databases. The region name is only returned in the response for single-region clusters. When MongoDB Cloud deploys a dedicated cluster, it checks if a VPC or VPC connection exists for that provider and region. If not, MongoDB Cloud creates them as part of the deployment. It assigns the VPC a Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) block. To limit a new VPC peering connection to one Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) block and region, create the connection first. Deploy the cluster after the connection starts. GCP Clusters and Multi-region clusters require one VPC peering connection for each region. MongoDB nodes can use only the peering connection that resides in the same region as the nodes to communicate with the peered VPC.|
|*oneOf*|[AWSRegionConfig](#schemaawsregionconfig)|false|none|Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.|
|*oneOf*|[AzureRegionConfig](#schemaazureregionconfig)|false|none|Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.|
|*oneOf*|[GCPRegionConfig](#schemagcpregionconfig)|false|none|Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.|
|*oneOf*|[TenantRegionConfig](#schematenantregionconfig)|false|none|Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.|
|analyticsAutoScaling|[AutoScalingSettings](#schemaautoscalingsettings)|false|none|Options that determine how this cluster handles resource scaling.|
|analyticsSpecs|[DedicatedHardwareSpec](#schemadedicatedhardwarespec)|false|none|Hardware specifications for read-only nodes in the region. Read-only nodes can never become the primary member, but can enable local reads. If you don't specify this parameter, no read-only nodes are deployed to the region.|
|autoScaling|[AutoScalingSettings](#schemaautoscalingsettings)|false|none|Options that determine how this cluster handles resource scaling.|
|readOnlySpecs|[DedicatedHardwareSpec](#schemadedicatedhardwarespec)|false|none|Hardware specifications for read-only nodes in the region. Read-only nodes can never become the primary member, but can enable local reads. If you don't specify this parameter, no read-only nodes are deployed to the region.|

|providerName|AZURE|
|providerName|GCP|
|providerName|TENANT|

|unacknowledgeAlert|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates to unacknowledge a previously acknowledged alert. By default this value is set to false. If set to true, it will override the `acknowledgedUntil` parameter.|

In a request that includes `replicationSpecs`, omitting `storageConfig` or sending it as `null` or `{}` clears the limit. Omitting `replicationSpecs` preserves it.|
