
One or more settings that specify language-specific rules to compare strings within this index.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alternate|string|false|none|Method to handle whitespace and punctuation as base characters for purposes of comparison. `"non-ignorable"` will evaluate Whitespace and Punctuation as Base Characters. `"shifted"` will not, MongoDB Cloud distinguishes these characters when `"strength" > 3`.|
|backwards|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether strings with diacritics sort from back of the string. Some French dictionary orders strings in this way. `true` will compare from back to front. `false` will compare from front to back.|
|caseFirst|string|false|none|Method to handle sort order of case differences during tertiary level comparisons. `"upper"` sorts Uppercase before lowercase. `"lower"` sorts Lowercase before uppercase. `"off"` is similar to "lower" with slight differences.|
|caseLevel|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether to include case comparison when `"strength" : 1` or `"strength" : 2`.<br>- `true` - Include casing in comparison<br>  - Strength Level: 1 - Base characters and case.<br>  - Strength Level: 2 - Base characters, diacritics (and possible other secondary differences),   and case.<br>- `false` - Case is NOT included in comparison.|
|locale|string|true|none|International Components for Unicode (ICU) code that represents a localized language. To specify simple binary comparison, set `"locale" : "simple"`.|
|maxVariable|string|false|none|Field that indicates which characters can be ignored when `"alternate" : "shifted"`.`"punct"` ignores both whitespace and punctuation. `"space"` ignores whitespace. This has no affect if `"alternate" : "non-ignorable"`.|
|normalization|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether to check if the text requires normalization and then perform it. Most text doesn't require this normalization processing.<br><br>`true` will check if fully normalized and perform normalization to compare text. `false` will not check.|
|numericOrdering|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether to compare sequences of digits as numbers or as strings. `true` will compare as numbers, this results in `10 > 2`. `false` will Compare as strings. This results in `"10" < "2"`.|
|strength|integer(int32)|false|none|Degree of comparison to perform when sorting words.<br><br>MongoDB Cloud accepts the following _numeric values_ that correspond to the _comparison level_ and what that _comparison method_ is.<br><br>- `1` - "Primary" - Compares the base characters only, ignoring other differences such as diacritics and case.<br>- `2` - "Secondary" - Compares base characters (primary) and diacritics (secondary). Primary differences take precedence over secondary differences.<br>- `3` - "Tertiary" - Compares base characters (primary), diacritics (secondary), and case and variants (tertiary). Differences between base characters takes precedence over secondary differences which take precedence over tertiary differences.<br>- `4` - "Quaternary" - Compares for the specific use case to consider punctuation when levels 1 through 3 ignore punctuation or for processing Japanese text.<br>- `5` - "Identical" - Compares for the specific use case of tie breaker.|

```json
  "type": "DATE"
}
```

Rules by which MongoDB Cloud archives data.

Use the `criteria.type` field to choose how MongoDB Cloud selects data to archive. Choose data using the age of the data or a MongoDB query.
`"criteria.type": "DATE"` selects documents to archive based on a date.
`"criteria.type": "CUSTOM"` selects documents to archive based on a custom JSON query. MongoDB Cloud doesn't support `"criteria.type": "CUSTOM"` when `"collectionType": "TIMESERIES"`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|Means by which MongoDB Cloud selects data to archive. Data can be chosen using the age of the data or a MongoDB query.<br>`DATE` selects documents to archive based on a date.<br>`CUSTOM` selects documents to archive based on a custom JSON query. MongoDB Cloud doesn't support `CUSTOM` when `"collectionType": "TIMESERIES"`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|DATE|
|type|CUSTOM|

<h2 id="tocS_CustomSessionTimeouts">CustomSessionTimeouts</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacustomsessiontimeouts"></a>
<a id="schema_CustomSessionTimeouts"></a>
<a id="tocScustomsessiontimeouts"></a>
<a id="tocscustomsessiontimeouts"></a>

```json
{
  "absoluteSessionTimeoutInSeconds": 0,
  "idleSessionTimeoutInSeconds": 0
}
```

Defines the session timeout settings for managing user sessions at the organization level. When set to null, the field's value is unset, and the default timeout settings are applied.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|absoluteSessionTimeoutInSeconds|integer(int32)|false|none|Specifies the absolute session timeout duration in seconds. When set to null, the field's value is unset, and the default value of 43,200 seconds (12 hours) is applied. Accepted values range between a minimum of 3,600 seconds (1 hour) and a maximum of 43,200 seconds (12 hours).|
|idleSessionTimeoutInSeconds|integer(int32)|false|none|Specifies the idle session timeout duration in seconds. When set to null, the field's value is unset, and the default behavior depends on the context: no timeout for Atlas Commercial, and 600 seconds (10 minutes) for Atlas for Government. Accepted values start at a minimum of 300 seconds (5 minutes). For Atlas Commercial, the maximum value cannot exceed the configured absolute session timeout. For Atlas for Government, the maximum value is capped at 600 seconds (10 minutes).|

MongoDB Cloud maps the ISO 3166-1a2 code to the nearest geographical zone by default. Include this parameter to override the default mappings.<br><br>This parameter returns an empty object if no custom zones exist.|

Data Explorer accessed event tracks different data operations via Data Explorer interactions.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiKeyId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the API Key that triggered the event. If this resource returns this parameter, it doesn't return the `userId` parameter.|
|collection|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label of the collection on which the event occurred. The resource returns this parameter when the `eventTypeName` includes `DATA_EXPLORER`.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Date and time when this event occurred. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|database|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label of the database on which this incident occurred. The resource returns this parameter when `"eventTypeName" : "DATA_EXPLORER"` or `"eventTypeName" : "DATA_EXPLORER_CRUD"`.|
|delegatePrincipal|[Principal](#schemaprincipal)|false|read-only|Information about a principal, such as an OAuth application, that triggered the event through delegated access.|
|eventTypeName|[DataExplorerAccessedEventTypeView](#schemadataexploreraccessedeventtypeview)|true|none|Unique identifier of event type.|
|groupId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the project in which the event occurred. The `eventId` identifies the specific event.|
|id|string|true|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the event.|
|isGlobalAdmin|boolean|false|read-only|Flag that indicates whether a MongoDB employee triggered the specified event.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|read-only|List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships.|
|opType|string|false|read-only|Action that the database attempted to execute when the event triggered. The response returns this parameter when `eventTypeName" : "DATA_EXPLORER"`.|
|orgId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization to which these events apply.|
|publicKey|string|false|read-only|Public part of the API key that triggered the event. If this resource returns this parameter, it doesn't return the **username** parameter.|
|raw|[raw](#schemaraw)|false|read-only|Additional meta information captured about this event. The response returns this parameter as a JSON object when the query parameter `includeRaw=true`. The list of fields in the raw document may change. Don't rely on raw values for formal monitoring.|
|remoteAddress|string|false|read-only|IPv4 or IPv6 address from which the user triggered this event.|
|userId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the console user who triggered the event. If this resource returns this parameter, it doesn't return the `apiKeyId` parameter.|
|username|string(email)|false|read-only|Email address for the user who triggered this event. If this resource returns this parameter, it doesn't return the `publicApiKey` parameter.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|eventTypeName|DATA_EXPLORER_CRUD|

Details of a tenant-level query limit for Data Federation. Query limit is the limit on the amount of usage during a time period based on cost.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|currentUsage|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Amount that indicates the current usage of the limit.|
|defaultLimit|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Default value of the limit.|
|lastModifiedDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Only used for Data Federation limits. Timestamp that indicates when this usage limit was last modified. This field uses the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|maximumLimit|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Maximum value of the limit.|
|name|string|true|read-only|Human-readable label that identifies the user-managed limit to modify.|
|overrunPolicy|string|false|none|Only used for Data Federation limits. Action to take when the usage limit is exceeded. If limit span is set to QUERY, this is ignored because MongoDB Cloud stops the query when it exceeds the usage limit.|
|tenantName|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label that identifies the Federated Database Instance. If specified, the usage limit is for the specified federated database instance only. If omitted, the usage limit is for all federated database instances in the project.|
|value|integer(int64)|true|none|Amount to set the limit to.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|overrunPolicy|BLOCK|
|overrunPolicy|BLOCK_AND_KILL|

```json
{
```
```json
  "allowInsecure": false,
  "collection": "string",
  "collectionRegex": "string",
  "database": "string",
  "databaseRegex": "string",

  "datasetPrefix": "string",
  "defaultFormat": ".avro",
```

```json
  "trimLevel": 0,
  "urls": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

Data store that maps to a collection for this data lake.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allowInsecure|boolean|false|none|Flag that validates the scheme in the specified URLs. If `true`, allows insecure `HTTP` scheme, doesn't verify the server's certificate chain and hostname, and accepts any certificate with any hostname presented by the server. If `false`, allows secure `HTTPS` scheme only.|
|collection|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the collection in the database. For creating a wildcard (`*`) collection, you must omit this parameter.|
|collectionRegex|string|false|none|Regex pattern to use for creating the wildcard (*) collection. To learn more about the regex syntax, see [Go programming language](https://pkg.go.dev/regexp).|
|database|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the database, which contains the collection in the cluster. You must omit this parameter to generate wildcard (`*`) collections for dynamically generated databases.|
|databaseRegex|string|false|none|Regex pattern to use for creating the wildcard (*) database. To learn more about the regex syntax, see [Go programming language](https://pkg.go.dev/regexp).|
|datasetName|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the dataset that Atlas generates for an ingestion pipeline run or Online Archive.|
|datasetPrefix|string|false|none|Human-readable label that matches against the dataset names for ingestion pipeline runs or Online Archives.|
|defaultFormat|string|false|none|File format that MongoDB Cloud uses if it encounters a file without a file extension while searching **storeName**.|
|path|string|false|none|File path that controls how MongoDB Cloud searches for and parses files in the **storeName** before mapping them to a collection.Specify ``/`` to capture all files and folders from the ``prefix`` path.|
|provenanceFieldName|string|false|none|Name for the field that includes the provenance of the documents in the results. MongoDB Cloud returns different fields in the results for each supported provider.|
|storeName|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the data store that MongoDB Cloud maps to the collection.|
|trimLevel|integer(int32)|false|none|Unsigned integer that specifies how many fields of the dataset name to trim from the left of the dataset name before mapping the remaining fields to a wildcard collection name.|
|urls|[string]|false|none|URLs of the publicly accessible data files. You can't specify URLs that require authentication. Atlas Data Lake creates a partition for each URL. If empty or omitted, Data Lake uses the URLs from the store specified in the **dataSources.storeName** parameter.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the data store. The **databases.[n].collections.[n].dataSources.[n].storeName** field references this values as part of the mapping configuration. To use MongoDB Cloud as a data store, the data lake requires a serverless instance or an `M10` or higher cluster.|
|provider|string|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[DataLakeS3StoreSettings](#schemadatalakes3storesettings)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[DataLakeDLSAWSStore](#schemadatalakedlsawsstore)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[DataLakeDLSAzureStore](#schemadatalakedlsazurestore)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[DataLakeDLSGCPStore](#schemadatalakedlsgcpstore)|false|none|none|

|*oneOf*|[DataLakeHTTPStore](#schemadatalakehttpstore)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[DataLakeAzureBlobStore](#schemadatalakeazureblobstore)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[DataLakeGoogleCloudStorageStore](#schemadatalakegooglecloudstoragestore)|false|none|none|
|additionalStorageClasses|[string]|false|none|Collection of AWS S3 [storage classes](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/storage-classes/). Atlas Data Lake includes the files in these storage classes in the query results.|
|bucket|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the AWS S3 bucket. This label must exactly match the name of an S3 bucket that the data lake can access with the configured AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) credentials.|
|delimiter|string|false|none|The delimiter that separates **databases.[n].collections.[n].dataSources.[n].path** segments in the data store. MongoDB Cloud uses the delimiter to efficiently traverse S3 buckets with a hierarchical directory structure. You can specify any character supported by the S3 object keys as the delimiter. For example, you can specify an underscore (_) or a plus sign (+) or multiple characters, such as double underscores (__) as the delimiter. If omitted, defaults to `/`.|
|includeTags|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether to use S3 tags on the files in the given path as additional partition attributes. If set to `true`, data lake adds the S3 tags as additional partition attributes and adds new top-level BSON elements associating each tag to each document.|
|prefix|string|false|none|Prefix that MongoDB Cloud applies when searching for files in the S3 bucket. The data store prepends the value of prefix to the **databases.[n].collections.[n].dataSources.[n].path** to create the full path for files to ingest. If omitted, MongoDB Cloud searches all files from the root of the S3 bucket.|
|public|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether the bucket is public. If set to `true`, MongoDB Cloud doesn't use the configured AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role to access the S3 bucket. If set to `false`, the configured AWS IAM role must include permissions to access the S3 bucket.|
|region|string|false|none|Physical location where MongoDB Cloud deploys your AWS-hosted MongoDB cluster nodes. The region you choose can affect network latency for clients accessing your databases. When MongoDB Cloud deploys a dedicated cluster, it checks if a VPC or VPC connection exists for that provider and region. If not, MongoDB Cloud creates them as part of the deployment. MongoDB Cloud assigns the VPC a CIDR block. To limit a new VPC peering connection to one CIDR block and region, create the connection first. Deploy the cluster after the connection starts.|

To learn more, see <a href="https://dochub.mongodb.org/core/alert-config-serverless-measurements" target="_blank">Serverless Measurements</a>.|

<h2 id="tocS_Datadog">Datadog</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadatadog"></a>
<a id="schema_Datadog"></a>
<a id="tocSdatadog"></a>
<a id="tocsdatadog"></a>

```json
{
  "apiKey": "****************************a23c",
  "id": "string",
  "region": "US",
  "sendCollectionLatencyMetrics": false,
  "sendDatabaseMetrics": false,
  "sendQueryStatsMetrics": false,
  "sendShardingMetrics": false,
  "sendUserProvidedResourceTags": false,
  "type": "DATADOG"
}
```

Details to integrate one Datadog account with one MongoDB Cloud project.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiKey|string|true|none|Key that allows MongoDB Cloud to access your Datadog account.<br><br>**NOTE**: After you create a notification which requires an API or integration key, the key appears partially redacted when you:<br><br>* View or edit the alert through the Atlas UI.<br><br>* Query the alert for the notification through the Atlas Administration API.|
|id|string \| null|false|none|Integration id.|
|region|string|false|none|Two-letter code that indicates which regional URL MongoDB uses to access the Datadog API.|
|sendCollectionLatencyMetrics|boolean|false|none|Toggle sending collection latency metrics that includes database names and collection names and latency metrics on reads, writes, commands, and transactions.|
|sendDatabaseMetrics|boolean|false|none|Toggle sending database metrics that includes database names and metrics on the number of collections, storage size, and index size.|
|sendQueryStatsMetrics|boolean|false|none|Toggle sending query shape metrics that includes query hash and metrics on latency, execution frequency, documents returned, and timestamps.|
|sendShardingMetrics|boolean|false|none|Toggle sending sharding metrics that includes sharding distribution and chunk metrics per cluster, shard, and collection.|
|sendUserProvidedResourceTags|boolean|false|none|Toggle sending user provided group and cluster resource tags with the Datadog metrics.|
|type|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the service to which you want to integrate with MongoDB Cloud. The value must match the third-party service integration type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|region|US|
|region|EU|
|region|US3|
|region|US5|
|region|AP1|
|region|AP2|
|region|US1_FED|
|type|DATADOG|

<a id="schema_DatadogNotification"></a>
<a id="tocSdatadognotification"></a>
<a id="tocsdatadognotification"></a>

```json
{
  "datadogApiKey": "****************************a23c",
  "datadogRegion": "US",
  "delayMin": 0,
  "integrationId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "intervalMin": 5,
  "notifierId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "typeName": "DATADOG"
}
```

Datadog notification configuration for MongoDB Cloud to send information when an event triggers an alert condition.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|datadogApiKey|string|false|none|Datadog API Key that MongoDB Cloud needs to send alert notifications to Datadog. You can find this API key in the Datadog dashboard. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "DATADOG"`.<br><br>**NOTE**: After you create a notification which requires an API or integration key, the key appears partially redacted when you:<br><br>* View or edit the alert through the Atlas UI.<br><br>* Query the alert for the notification through the Atlas Administration API.|
|datadogRegion|string|false|none|Datadog region that indicates which API Uniform Resource Locator (URL) to use. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "DATADOG"`.|
|delayMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes that MongoDB Cloud waits after detecting an alert condition before it sends out the first notification.|
|integrationId|string|false|none|The id of the associated integration, the credentials of which to use for requests.|
|intervalMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes to wait between successive notifications. MongoDB Cloud sends notifications until someone acknowledges the unacknowledged alert.<br><br>PagerDuty, VictorOps, and OpsGenie notifications don't return this element. Configure and manage the notification interval within each of those services.|
|notifierId|string|false|none|The `notifierId` is a system-generated unique identifier assigned to each notification method. This is needed when updating third-party notifications without requiring explicit authentication credentials.|
|typeName|string|true|none|Human-readable label that displays the alert notification type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|datadogRegion|US|
|datadogRegion|EU|
|datadogRegion|US3|
|datadogRegion|US5|
|datadogRegion|AP1|
|datadogRegion|AP2|
|datadogRegion|US1_FED|
|typeName|DATADOG|

<h2 id="tocS_DateCriteriaView">DateCriteriaView</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemadatecriteriaview"></a>
<a id="schema_DateCriteriaView"></a>
<a id="tocSdatecriteriaview"></a>
<a id="tocsdatecriteriaview"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "DATE",
  "dateField": "string",
  "dateFormat": "ISODATE",
  "expireAfterDays": 0
}
```

Date-Based archival criteria.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|Means by which MongoDB Cloud selects data to archive. Data can be chosen using the age of the data or a MongoDB query.<br>`DATE` selects documents to archive based on a date.<br>`CUSTOM` selects documents to archive based on a custom JSON query. MongoDB Cloud doesn't support `CUSTOM` when `"collectionType": "TIMESERIES"`.|
|dateField|string|false|none|Indexed database parameter that stores the date that determines when data moves to the online archive. MongoDB Cloud archives the data when the current date exceeds the date in this database parameter plus the number of days specified through the `expireAfterDays` parameter. Set this parameter when you set `"criteria.type" : "DATE"`.|
|dateFormat|string|false|none|Syntax used to write the date after which data moves to the online archive. Date can be expressed as ISO 8601, Epoch timestamps, or Object ID. The Epoch timestamp can be expressed as nanoseconds, milliseconds, or seconds. Set this parameter when `criteria.type` : `DATE`.<br>You must set `criteria.type` : `DATE` if `collectionType`: `TIMESERIES`.|
|expireAfterDays|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of days after the value in the `criteria.dateField` when MongoDB Cloud archives data in the specified cluster. Set this parameter when you set `"criteria.type" : "DATE"`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|DATE|
|type|CUSTOM|
|dateFormat|ISODATE|
|dateFormat|EPOCH_SECONDS|
|dateFormat|EPOCH_MILLIS|
|dateFormat|EPOCH_NANOSECONDS|
|dateFormat|OBJECT_ID|

|resolved|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time that this alert changed to `"status" : "CLOSED"`. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. The resource returns this parameter once `"status" : "CLOSED"`.|

OPEN indicates the alert condition currently exists. CLOSED indicates the alert condition has been resolved.|


Specifications for one policy.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|frequencyInterval|integer(int32)|true|none|Number that indicates the frequency interval for a set of Snapshots. A value of `1` specifies the first instance of the corresponding `frequencyType`.<br><br>- In a yearly policy item, `1` indicates that the yearly Snapshot occurs on the first day of January and `12` indicates the first day of December.<br><br>- In a monthly policy item, `1` indicates that the monthly Snapshot occurs on the first day of the month and `40` indicates the last day of the month.<br><br>- In a weekly policy item, `1` indicates that the weekly Snapshot occurs on Monday and `7` indicates Sunday.<br><br>- In an hourly policy item, you can set the frequency interval to `1`, `2`, `4`, `6`, `8`, or `12`. For hourly policy items for NVMe clusters, MongoDB Cloud accepts only `12` as the frequency interval value.<br><br> MongoDB Cloud ignores this setting for non-hourly policy items in Backup Compliance Policy settings.|
|frequencyType|string|true|none|Human-readable label that identifies the frequency type associated with the backup policy.|
|id|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies this backup policy item.|

```json
  ],
```

```json
  "sizeBytes": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accessCount|integer(int64)|false|none|Usage count (since last restart) of index.|
|collation|object|false|none|Collation this index was built with. An index only serves a query that runs with the same collation. Absent when the index uses the default (simple) collation.|
|index|[object]|false|none|List that contains documents that specify a key in the index and its sort order.|
|name|string|false|none|Name of index.|
|namespace|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the namespace on the specified host. The resource expresses this parameter value as `<database>.<collection>`.|
|shards|[string]|false|none|List that contains strings that specifies the shards where the index is found.|
|since|string(date-time)|false|none|Date of most recent usage of index. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|sizeBytes|integer(int64)|false|none|Size of index.|

<h2 id="tocS_EmailNotification">EmailNotification</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaemailnotification"></a>
<a id="schema_EmailNotification"></a>
<a id="tocSemailnotification"></a>
<a id="tocsemailnotification"></a>

```json
{
  "delayMin": 0,
  "emailAddress": "user@example.com",
  "intervalMin": 5,
  "notifierId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "typeName": "EMAIL"
}
```

Email notification configuration for MongoDB Cloud to send information when an event triggers an alert condition.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delayMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes that MongoDB Cloud waits after detecting an alert condition before it sends out the first notification.|
|emailAddress|string(email)|false|none|Email address to which MongoDB Cloud sends alert notifications. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "EMAIL"`. You don't need to set this value to send emails to individual or groups of MongoDB Cloud users including:<br><br>- specific MongoDB Cloud users (`"notifications.[n].typeName" : "USER"`)<br>- MongoDB Cloud users with specific project roles (`"notifications.[n].typeName" : "GROUP"`)<br>- MongoDB Cloud users with specific organization roles (`"notifications.[n].typeName" : "ORG"`)<br>- MongoDB Cloud teams (`"notifications.[n].typeName" : "TEAM"`)<br><br>To send emails to one MongoDB Cloud user or grouping of users, set the `notifications.[n].emailEnabled` parameter.|
|intervalMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes to wait between successive notifications. MongoDB Cloud sends notifications until someone acknowledges the unacknowledged alert.<br><br>PagerDuty, VictorOps, and OpsGenie notifications don't return this element. Configure and manage the notification interval within each of those services.|
|notifierId|string|false|none|The `notifierId` is a system-generated unique identifier assigned to each notification method. This is needed when updating third-party notifications without requiring explicit authentication credentials.|
|typeName|string|true|none|Human-readable label that displays the alert notification type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|typeName|EMAIL|

|restoreScheduledDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud will restore this snapshot. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|snapshotFinishedDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud completed writing this snapshot. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|

|targetDeploymentItemName|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label that identifies the instance or cluster on the target project to which you want to restore the snapshot. You can restore the snapshot to another flex or dedicated cluster tier.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|createDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud created this instance. This parameter expresses its value in ISO 8601 format in UTC.|
|databaseEdition|string|false|none|Available in Public Preview: Optional field that indicates whether your tenant cluster will be upgraded to Atlas INFINITE or CORE.|
|groupId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal character string that identifies the project.|
|id|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the instance.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|read-only|List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships.|
|mongoDBVersion|string|false|read-only|Version of MongoDB that the instance runs.|
|name|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label that identifies the instance.|
|providerSettings|[FlexProviderSettings20241113](#schemaflexprovidersettings20241113)|true|read-only|Group of cloud provider settings that configure the provisioned MongoDB flex cluster.|
|stateName|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label that indicates any current activity being taken on this cluster by the Atlas control plane. With the exception of CREATING and DELETING states, clusters should always be available and have a Primary node even when in states indicating ongoing activity.<br><br> - `IDLE`: Atlas is making no changes to this cluster and all changes requested via the UI or API can be assumed to have been applied.<br> - `CREATING`: A cluster being provisioned for the very first time returns state CREATING until it is ready for connections. Ensure IP Access List and DB Users are configured before attempting to connect.<br> - `UPDATING`: A change requested via the UI, API, AutoScaling, or other scheduled activity is taking place.<br> - `DELETING`: The cluster is in the process of deletion and will soon be deleted.<br> - `REPAIRING`: One or more nodes in the cluster are being returned to service by the Atlas control plane. Other nodes should continue to provide service as normal.|
|tags|[[ResourceTag](#schemaresourcetag)]|false|none|List that contains key-value pairs between 1 to 255 characters in length for tagging and categorizing the instance.|
|terminationProtectionEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether termination protection is enabled on the cluster. If set to `true`, MongoDB Cloud won't delete the cluster. If set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud will delete the cluster.|
|versionReleaseSystem|string|false|read-only|Method by which the cluster maintains the MongoDB versions.|

Flex Metric Alert notifies about changes of measurements or metrics for a Flex cluster.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acknowledgedUntil|string(date-time)|false|none|Date and time until which this alert has been acknowledged. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. The resource returns this parameter if a MongoDB User previously acknowledged this alert.<br><br>- To acknowledge this alert forever, set the parameter value to 100 years in the future.<br><br>- To unacknowledge a previously acknowledged alert, do not set this parameter value.|
|acknowledgementComment|string|false|none|Comment that a MongoDB Cloud user submitted when acknowledging the alert.|
|acknowledgingUsername|string(email)|false|read-only|MongoDB Cloud username of the person who acknowledged the alert. The response returns this parameter if a MongoDB Cloud user previously acknowledged this alert.|
|alertConfigId|string|true|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the alert configuration that sets this alert.|
|clusterName|string|true|read-only|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster to which this alert applies.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud created this alert. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|currentValue|[HostMetricValue](#schemahostmetricvalue)|false|read-only|Value of the metric that triggered the alert. The resource returns this parameter for alerts of events impacting hosts.|
|eventTypeName|[FlexMetricEventTypeViewAlertable](#schemaflexmetriceventtypeviewalertable)|true|none|Event type that triggers an alert.|
|groupId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the project that owns this alert.|
|id|string|true|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies this alert.|
|lastNotified|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time that any notifications were last sent for this alert. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. The resource returns this parameter if MongoDB Cloud has sent notifications for this alert.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|read-only|List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships.|
|metricName|string|false|read-only|Name of the metric against which Atlas checks the configured alert condition.|
|orgId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal character string that identifies the organization that owns the project to which this alert applies.|
|resolved|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time that this alert changed to `"status" : "CLOSED"`. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. The resource returns this parameter once `"status" : "CLOSED"`.|
|severity|string|false|read-only|Severity of the event.|
|status|string|true|read-only|State of this alert at the time you requested its details. TRACKING indicates the alert condition exists but has not persisted for the minimum notification delay. OPEN indicates the alert condition currently exists. CLOSED indicates the alert condition has been resolved.|
|updated|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Date and time when someone last updated this alert. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|

|severity|WARNING|

Collection of settings that configures the network container for a virtual private connection on Amazon Web Services.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the network peering container.|
|providerName|string|false|none|Cloud service provider that serves the requested network peering containers.|
|provisioned|boolean|false|read-only|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud clusters exist in the specified network peering container.|
|*oneOf*|[AzureCloudProviderContainer](#schemaazurecloudprovidercontainer)|false|none|Collection of settings that configures the network container for a virtual private connection on Amazon Web Services.|
|*oneOf*|[GCPCloudProviderContainer](#schemagcpcloudprovidercontainer)|false|none|Collection of settings that configures the network container for a virtual private connection on Amazon Web Services.|
|*oneOf*|[AWSCloudProviderContainer](#schemaawscloudprovidercontainer)|false|none|Collection of settings that configures the network container for a virtual private connection on Amazon Web Services.|
|atlasCidrBlock|string|true|none|IP addresses expressed in Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation that MongoDB Cloud uses for the network peering containers in your project. MongoDB Cloud assigns all of the project's clusters deployed to this cloud provider an IP address from this range. MongoDB Cloud locks this value if an M10 or greater cluster or a network peering connection exists in this project.<br><br>These CIDR blocks must fall within the ranges reserved per RFC 1918. GCP further limits the block to a lower bound of the `/18` range.<br><br>To modify the CIDR block, the target project cannot have:<br><br>- Any M10 or greater clusters<br>- Any other VPC peering connections<br><br> You can also create a new project and create a network peering connection to set the desired MongoDB Cloud network peering container CIDR block for that project. MongoDB Cloud limits the number of MongoDB nodes per network peering connection based on the CIDR block and the region selected for the project.<br><br> **Example:** A project in an Google Cloud (GCP) region supporting three availability zones and an MongoDB CIDR network peering container block of limit of `/24` equals 27 three-node replica sets.|
|gcpProjectId|string|false|read-only|Unique string that identifies the GCP project in which MongoDB Cloud clusters in this network peering container exist. The response returns **null** if no clusters exist in this network peering container.|
|networkName|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label that identifies the network in which MongoDB Cloud clusters in this network peering container exist. MongoDB Cloud returns **null** if no clusters exist in this network peering container.|
|regions|[string]|true|none|List of GCP regions to which you want to deploy this MongoDB Cloud network peering container.  In this MongoDB Cloud project, you can deploy clusters only to the GCP regions in this list. To deploy MongoDB Cloud clusters to other GCP regions, create additional projects.|

```json
    "diskThroughput": 0,
    "ebsVolumeType": "STANDARD",
    "instanceSize": "M10",
    "nodeCount": 0
  }
}
```

Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|electableSpecs|[HardwareSpec](#schemahardwarespec)|false|none|Hardware specifications for all electable nodes deployed in the region. Electable nodes can become the primary and can enable local reads. If you don't specify this option, MongoDB Cloud deploys no electable nodes to the region.|
|priority|integer(int32)|false|none|Precedence is given to this region when a primary election occurs. If your `regionConfigs` has only `readOnlySpecs`, `analyticsSpecs`, or both, set this value to `0`. If you have multiple `regionConfigs` objects (your cluster is multi-region or multi-cloud), they must have priorities in descending order. The highest priority is `7`.<br><br>**Example:** If you have three regions, their priorities would be `7`, `6`, and `5` respectively. If you added two more regions for supporting electable nodes, the priorities of those regions would be `4` and `3` respectively.|
|providerName|string|false|none|Cloud service provider on which MongoDB Cloud provisions the hosts. Set dedicated clusters to `AWS`, `GCP`, `AZURE` or `TENANT`.|
|regionName|object|false|none|Physical location of your MongoDB cluster nodes. The region you choose can affect network latency for clients accessing your databases. The region name is only returned in the response for single-region clusters. When MongoDB Cloud deploys a dedicated cluster, it checks if a VPC or VPC connection exists for that provider and region. If not, MongoDB Cloud creates them as part of the deployment. It assigns the VPC a Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) block. To limit a new VPC peering connection to one Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) block and region, create the connection first. Deploy the cluster after the connection starts. GCP Clusters and Multi-region clusters require one VPC peering connection for each region. MongoDB nodes can use only the peering connection that resides in the same region as the nodes to communicate with the peered VPC.|
|*oneOf*|[AWSRegionConfig](#schemaawsregionconfig)|false|none|Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.|
|*oneOf*|[AzureRegionConfig](#schemaazureregionconfig)|false|none|Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.|
|*oneOf*|[GCPRegionConfig](#schemagcpregionconfig)|false|none|Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.|
|*oneOf*|[TenantRegionConfig](#schematenantregionconfig)|false|none|Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.|
|analyticsAutoScaling|[AutoScalingSettings](#schemaautoscalingsettings)|false|none|Options that determine how this cluster handles resource scaling.|
|analyticsSpecs|[DedicatedHardwareSpec](#schemadedicatedhardwarespec)|false|none|Hardware specifications for read-only nodes in the region. Read-only nodes can never become the primary member, but can enable local reads. If you don't specify this parameter, no read-only nodes are deployed to the region.|
|autoScaling|[AutoScalingSettings](#schemaautoscalingsettings)|false|none|Options that determine how this cluster handles resource scaling.|
|readOnlySpecs|[DedicatedHardwareSpec](#schemadedicatedhardwarespec)|false|none|Hardware specifications for read-only nodes in the region. Read-only nodes can never become the primary member, but can enable local reads. If you don't specify this parameter, no read-only nodes are deployed to the region.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|providerName|AWS|
|providerName|AZURE|
|providerName|GCP|
|providerName|TENANT|

<h2 id="tocS_GeoSharding">GeoSharding</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemageosharding"></a>
<a id="schema_GeoSharding"></a>
<a id="tocSgeosharding"></a>
<a id="tocsgeosharding"></a>

```json
{
  "customZoneMapping": {
    "property1": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
    "property2": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8"
  },
  "managedNamespaces": [
    {
      "collection": "string",
      "customShardKey": "string",
      "db": "string",
      "isCustomShardKeyHashed": false,
      "isShardKeyUnique": false,
      "numInitialChunks": 0,
      "presplitHashedZones": false
    }
  ],
  "selfManagedSharding": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customZoneMapping|object|false|read-only|List that contains comma-separated key value pairs to map zones to geographic regions. These pairs map an ISO 3166-1a2 location code, with an ISO 3166-2 subdivision code when possible, to a unique 24-hexadecimal string that identifies the custom zone.<br><br> The 24-hexadecimal string corresponds to a `Replication Specifications` `id` property.<br><br>This parameter returns an empty object if no custom zones exist.<br><br>Example: `{"US-VA": "6716c5a804f4ce77e899bf99", "DE": "6716c5a804f4ce77e899bf9a"}`.|
|managedNamespaces|[[ManagedNamespaces](#schemamanagednamespaces)]|false|read-only|List that contains a namespace for a Global Cluster. MongoDB Cloud manages this cluster.|
|selfManagedSharding|boolean|false|read-only|Boolean that controls which management mode the Global Cluster is operating under. If this parameter is true Self-Managed Sharding is enabled and users are in control of the zone sharding within the Global Cluster. If this parameter is false Atlas-Managed Sharding is enabled and Atlas is control of zone sharding within the Global Cluster.|

```json
{
```
```json
  "autoDeferOnceEnabled": true,

  },

  "timeZoneId": "string",
  "waveAssignment": 1
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|autoDeferOnceEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud should defer all maintenance windows for one week after you enable them. This setting controls the same underlying auto-deferral feature as the `/maintenanceWindow/autoDefer` endpoint. Use either this field (to set a specific value) or that endpoint (to toggle the current value). For most use cases, this field in the PATCH request is preferred because it allows setting an explicit value rather than toggling.|
|dayOfWeek|integer(int32)|false|none|One-based integer that represents the day of the week, in the project's configured time zone (see `timeZoneId`), that the maintenance window starts.<br><br>- `1`: Sunday.<br>- `2`: Monday.<br>- `3`: Tuesday.<br>- `4`: Wednesday.<br>- `5`: Thursday.<br>- `6`: Friday.<br>- `7`: Saturday.|
|effectiveWaveAssignment|integer(int32)|false|read-only|Maintenance wave that Atlas uses when scheduling maintenance for this project. This read-only value can differ from `waveAssignment` in two scenarios: (1) when the organization's `effectiveWaveAssignmentMode` is `ENV_TAG_MAPPING`, the effective wave is derived from environment tags regardless of any explicit assignment; (2) when cross-organization maintenance sequencing is active and this project's organization is a linked non-paying organization, the effective wave reflects the paying organization's mode.|
|hourOfDay|integer(int32)|false|none|Zero-based integer that represents the hour of the day, in the project's configured time zone (see `timeZoneId`), that the maintenance window starts according to a 24-hour clock. Use `0` for midnight and `12` for noon. If you haven't changed your project's time zone, this defaults to UTC.|
|numberOfDeferrals|integer(int32)|false|read-only|Number of times the current maintenance event for this project has been deferred.|
|protectedHours|[ProtectedHours](#schemaprotectedhours)|false|none|Defines the a window where maintenance will not begin within.|
|startASAP|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud starts the maintenance window immediately upon receiving this request. To start the maintenance window immediately for your project, MongoDB Cloud must have maintenance scheduled and you must set a maintenance window. This flag resets to `false` after MongoDB Cloud completes maintenance.|
|timeZoneId|string|false|read-only|Identifier for the current time zone of the maintenance window. This can only be updated via the Project Settings UI.|
|waveAssignment|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|Maintenance wave explicitly assigned to this project. Always returned in GET responses when a value has been set, regardless of the organization's `effectiveWaveAssignmentMode`. When the mode is `ENV_TAG_MAPPING`, this stored assignment is preserved but not used for scheduling — the effective wave is derived from environment tags instead. Not editable when the mode is `ENV_TAG_MAPPING`. Switching back to `MANUAL` restores this value as the effective wave. Must be between 1 and 3, inclusive. Pass `null` to clear an explicit assignment.|

Use either this field (to set a specific value) or that endpoint (to toggle the current value). For most use cases, this field in the PATCH request is preferred because it allows setting an explicit value rather than toggling.|
|dayOfWeek|integer(int32)|false|none|One-based integer that represents the day of the week, in the project's configured time zone (see `timeZoneId`), that the maintenance window starts.<br><br>- `1`: Sunday.<br>- `2`: Monday.<br>- `3`: Tuesday.<br>- `4`: Wednesday.<br>- `5`: Thursday.<br>- `6`: Friday.<br>- `7`: Saturday.|
|hourOfDay|integer(int32)|false|none|Zero-based integer that represents the hour of the day, in the project's configured time zone (see `timeZoneId`), that the maintenance window starts according to a 24-hour clock. Use `0` for midnight and `12` for noon. If you haven't changed your project's time zone, this defaults to UTC.|
|protectedHours|[ProtectedHours](#schemaprotectedhours)|false|none|Defines the a window where maintenance will not begin within.|
|startASAP|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud starts the maintenance window immediately upon receiving this request. To start the maintenance window immediately for your project, MongoDB Cloud must have maintenance scheduled and you must set a maintenance window. This flag resets to `false` after MongoDB Cloud completes maintenance.|
|waveAssignment|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|Maintenance wave assigned to this project (1–3). Not used for scheduling when the organization's `effectiveWaveAssignmentMode` is `ENV_TAG_MAPPING`. Pass `null` to clear.|

```json
    "string"
  ],
  "smsEnabled": true,
  "typeName": "GROUP"
}
```

Group notification configuration for MongoDB Cloud to send information when an event triggers an alert condition.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delayMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes that MongoDB Cloud waits after detecting an alert condition before it sends out the first notification.|
|emailEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud should send email notifications. The resource requires this parameter when one of the following values have been set:<br><br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "ORG"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "GROUP"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "USER"`|
|intervalMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes to wait between successive notifications. MongoDB Cloud sends notifications until someone acknowledges the unacknowledged alert.<br><br>PagerDuty, VictorOps, and OpsGenie notifications don't return this element. Configure and manage the notification interval within each of those services.|
|notifierId|string|false|none|The `notifierId` is a system-generated unique identifier assigned to each notification method. This is needed when updating third-party notifications without requiring explicit authentication credentials.|
|roles|[string]|false|none|List that contains the one or more project roles that receive the configured alert. This parameter is available when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "GROUP"` or `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "ORG"`. If you include this parameter, MongoDB Cloud sends alerts only to users assigned the roles you specify in the array. If you omit this parameter, MongoDB Cloud sends alerts to users assigned any role.|
|smsEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud should send text message notifications. The resource requires this parameter when one of the following values have been set:<br><br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "ORG"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "GROUP"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "USER"`|
|typeName|string|true|none|Human-readable label that displays the alert notification type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|typeName|GROUP|

HipChat notification configuration for MongoDB Cloud to send information when an event triggers an alert condition.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delayMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes that MongoDB Cloud waits after detecting an alert condition before it sends out the first notification.|
|integrationId|string|false|none|The id of the associated integration, the credentials of which to use for requests.|
|intervalMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes to wait between successive notifications. MongoDB Cloud sends notifications until someone acknowledges the unacknowledged alert.<br><br>PagerDuty, VictorOps, and OpsGenie notifications don't return this element. Configure and manage the notification interval within each of those services.|
|notificationToken|string|false|none|HipChat API token that MongoDB Cloud needs to send alert notifications to HipChat. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "HIP_CHAT"`". If the token later becomes invalid, MongoDB Cloud sends an email to the project owners. If the token remains invalid, MongoDB Cloud removes it.<br><br>**NOTE**: After you create a notification which requires an API or integration key, the key appears partially redacted when you:<br><br>* View or edit the alert through the Atlas UI.<br><br>* Query the alert for the notification through the Atlas Administration API.|
|notifierId|string|false|none|The `notifierId` is a system-generated unique identifier assigned to each notification method. This is needed when updating third-party notifications without requiring explicit authentication credentials.|
|roomName|string|false|none|HipChat API room name to which MongoDB Cloud sends alert notifications. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "HIP_CHAT"`".|
|typeName|string|true|none|Human-readable label that displays the alert notification type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|typeName|HIP_CHAT|

|metricName|string|false|read-only|Name of the metric against which Atlas checks the configured `metricThreshold.threshold`.<br><br>To learn more about the available metrics, see <a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-host-metrics/#std-label-measurement-types" target="_blank">Host Metrics</a>.<br><br>**NOTE**: If you set `eventTypeName` to `OUTSIDE_SERVERLESS_METRIC_THRESHOLD`, you can specify only metrics available for serverless. To learn more, see <a href="https://dochub.mongodb.org/core/alert-config-serverless-measurements" target="_blank">Serverless Measurements</a>.|

OPEN indicates the alert condition currently exists. CLOSED indicates the alert condition has been resolved.|

List of inbound IP addresses to the Atlas control plane, categorized by cloud provider. If your application allows outbound HTTP requests only to specific IP addresses, you must allow access to the following IP addresses so that your API requests can reach the Atlas control plane.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aws|object|false|read-only|Control plane IP addresses in AWS. Each key identifies an Amazon Web Services (AWS) region. Each value identifies control plane IP addresses in the AWS region.|
|azure|object|false|read-only|Control plane IP addresses in Azure. Each key identifies an Azure region. Each value identifies control plane IP addresses in the Azure region.|
|gcp|object|false|read-only|Control plane IP addresses in GCP. Each key identifies a Google Cloud (GCP) region. Each value identifies control plane IP addresses in the GCP region.|

<h2 id="tocS_IndexOptions">IndexOptions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaindexoptions"></a>
<a id="schema_IndexOptions"></a>
<a id="tocSindexoptions"></a>
<a id="tocsindexoptions"></a>

```json
{
  "2dsphereIndexVersion": 3,
  "background": false,
  "bits": 26,
  "bucketSize": 0,
  "columnstoreProjection": {
    "property1": 0,
    "property2": 0
  },
  "default_language": "english",
  "expireAfterSeconds": 0,
  "hidden": false,
  "language_override": "language",
  "max": 180,
  "min": -180,
  "name": "string",
  "partialFilterExpression": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  },
  "sparse": false,
  "storageEngine": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  },
  "textIndexVersion": 3,
  "weights": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  }
}
```

One or more settings that determine how the MongoDB Cloud creates this MongoDB index.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|2dsphereIndexVersion|integer(int32)|false|none|Index version number applied to the 2dsphere index. MongoDB 3.2 and later use version 3. Use this option to override the default version number. This option applies to the **2dsphere** index type only.|
|background|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB should build the index in the background. This applies to MongoDB databases running feature compatibility version 4.0 or earlier. MongoDB databases running FCV 4.2 or later build indexes using an optimized build process. This process holds the exclusive lock only at the beginning and end of the build process. The rest of the build process yields to interleaving read and write operations. MongoDB databases running FCV 4.2 or later ignore this option. This option applies to all index types.|
|bits|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of precision applied to the stored geohash value of the location data. This option applies to the **2d** index type only.|
|bucketSize|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of units within which to group the location values. You could group in the same bucket those location values within the specified number of units to each other. This option applies to the geoHaystack index type only.<br><br>MongoDB 5.0 removed geoHaystack Indexes and the `geoSearch` command.|
|columnstoreProjection|object|false|none|The `columnstoreProjection` document allows to include or exclude sub-schemas schema. One cannot combine inclusion and exclusion statements. Accordingly, the <value> can be either of the following:<br>1 or true to include the field and recursively all fields it is a prefix of in the index<br>0 or false to exclude the field and recursively all fields it is a prefix of from the index.|
|default_language|string|false|none|Human language that determines the list of stop words and the rules for the stemmer and tokenizer. This option accepts the supported languages using its name in lowercase English or the ISO 639-2 code. If you set this parameter to `"none"`, then the text search uses simple tokenization with no list of stop words and no stemming. This option applies to the **text** index type only.|
|expireAfterSeconds|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of seconds that MongoDB retains documents in a Time To Live (TTL) index.|
|hidden|boolean|false|none|Flag that determines whether the index is hidden from the query planner. A hidden index is not evaluated as part of the query plan selection.|
|language_override|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the document parameter that contains the override language for the document. This option applies to the **text** index type only.|
|max|integer(int32)|false|none|Upper inclusive boundary to limit the longitude and latitude values. This option applies to the 2d index type only.|
|min|integer(int32)|false|none|Lower inclusive boundary to limit the longitude and latitude values. This option applies to the 2d index type only.|
|name|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies this index. This option applies to all index types.|
|partialFilterExpression|object|false|none|Rules that limit the documents that the index references to a filter expression. All MongoDB index types accept a `partialFilterExpression` option. `partialFilterExpression` can include following expressions:<br><br>- equality (`"parameter" : "value"` or using the `$eq` operator)<br>- `"$exists": true`<br>, maximum: `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte` comparisons<br>- `$type`<br>- `$and` (top-level only)<br> This option applies to all index types.|
|sparse|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether the index references documents that only have the specified parameter. These indexes use less space but behave differently in some situations like when sorting. The following index types default to sparse and ignore this option: `2dsphere`, `2d`, `geoHaystack`, `text`.<br><br>Compound indexes that includes one or more indexes with `2dsphere` keys alongside other key types, only the `2dsphere` index parameters determine which documents the index references. If you run MongoDB 3.2 or later, use partial indexes. This option applies to all index types.|
|storageEngine|object|false|none|Storage engine set for the specific index. This value can be set only at creation. This option uses the following format: `"storageEngine" : { "<storage-engine-name>" : "<options>" }` MongoDB validates storage engine configuration options when creating indexes. To support replica sets with members with different storage engines, MongoDB logs these options to the oplog during replication. This option applies to all index types.|
|textIndexVersion|integer(int32)|false|none|Version applied to this text index. MongoDB 3.2 and later use version `3`. Use this option to override the default version number. This option applies to the **text** index type only.|
|weights|object|false|none|Relative importance to place upon provided index parameters. This object expresses this as key/value pairs of index parameter and weight to apply to that parameter. You can specify weights for some or all the indexed parameters. The weight must be an integer between 1 and 99,999. MongoDB 5.0 and later can apply **weights** to **text** indexes only.|


One service included in this invoice.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cloudProvider|string|false|read-only|Code identifying the cloud provider this line item's usage is attributed to. Values map as follows: AWS is Amazon Web Services, GCP is Google Cloud, AZURE is Microsoft Azure, and ATLAS is other Atlas usage not tied to a specific cloud provider.|
|clusterName|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster that incurred the charge.|
|created|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud created this line item. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|discountCents|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Sum by which MongoDB discounted this line item. MongoDB Cloud expresses this value in cents (100ths of one US Dollar). The resource returns this parameter when a discount applies.|
|endDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time when when MongoDB Cloud finished charging for this line item. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|groupId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the project associated to this line item.|
|groupName|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the project.|
|note|string|false|read-only|Comment that applies to this line item.|
|percentDiscount|number(float)|false|read-only|Percentage by which MongoDB discounted this line item. The resource returns this parameter when a discount applies.|
|quantity|number(double)|false|read-only|Number of units included for the line item. These can be expressions of storage (GB), time (hours), or other units.|
|sku|string|false|read-only|Human-readable description of the service that this line item provided. This Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) could be the instance type, a support charge, advanced security, or another service.|
|startDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud began charging for this line item. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|stitchAppName|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label that identifies the Atlas App Services application associated with this line item.|
|tags|object|false|read-only|A map of key-value pairs corresponding to the tags associated with the line item resource.|
|tierLowerBound|number(double)|false|read-only|Lower bound for usage amount range in current SKU tier. <br><br>**NOTE**: `lineItems[n].tierLowerBound` appears only if your `lineItems[n].sku` is tiered.|
|tierUpperBound|number(double)|false|read-only|Upper bound for usage amount range in current SKU tier. <br><br>**NOTE**: `lineItems[n].tierUpperBound` appears only if your `lineItems[n].sku` is tiered.|
|totalPriceCents|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Sum of the cost set for this line item. MongoDB Cloud expresses this value in cents (100ths of one US Dollar) and calculates this value as `unitPriceDollars` * `quantity` * 100.|
|unit|string|false|read-only|Element used to express what **quantity** this line item measures. This value can be elements of time, storage capacity, and the like.|
|unitPriceDollars|number(double)|false|read-only|Value per **unit** for this line item expressed in US Dollars.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|cloudProvider|AWS|
|cloudProvider|GCP|
|cloudProvider|AZURE|
|cloudProvider|ATLAS|

```json
{
  "authenticationEnabled": true,
  "authorizationEnabled": true,
  "authzQueryTemplate": "{USER}?memberOf?base",
  "bindPassword": "string",
  "bindUsername": "CN=BindUser,CN=Users,DC=myldapserver,DC=mycompany,DC=com",
  "caCertificate": "string",
  "hostname": "string",
  "links": [
    {
      "href": "https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas",
      "rel": "self"
    }
  ],
  "port": 636,
  "userToDNMapping": [
    {
      "ldapQuery": "string",
      "match": "(.*)",
      "substitution": "CN={0},CN=Users,DC=my-atlas-ldap-server,DC=example,DC=com"
    }
  ]
}
```

Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) over Transport Layer Security (TLS) configuration details that apply to the specified project.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authenticationEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether users can authenticate using an Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) host.|
|authorizationEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether users can authorize access to MongoDB Cloud resources using an Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) host.|
|authzQueryTemplate|string|false|none|Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) query template that MongoDB Cloud runs to obtain the LDAP groups associated with the authenticated user. MongoDB Cloud uses this parameter only for user authorization. Use the `{USER}` placeholder in the Uniform Resource Locator (URL) to substitute the authenticated username. The query relates to the host specified with the hostname. Format this query according to [RFC 4515](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4515) and [RFC 4516](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4516).|
|bindPassword|string|false|write-only|Password that MongoDB Cloud uses to authenticate the `bindUsername`.|
|bindUsername|string|false|none|Full Distinguished Name (DN) of the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) user that MongoDB Cloud uses to connect to the LDAP host. LDAP distinguished names must be formatted according to RFC 2253.|
|caCertificate|string|false|none|Certificate Authority (CA) certificate that MongoDB Cloud uses to verify the identity of the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) host. MongoDB Cloud allows self-signed certificates. To delete an assigned value, pass an empty string: `"caCertificate": ""`.|
|hostname|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the hostname or Internet Protocol (IP) address of the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) host. This host must have access to the internet or have a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) peering connection to your cluster.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|read-only|List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships.|
|port|integer(int32)|false|none|Port to which the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) host listens for client connections.|
|userToDNMapping|[[UserToDNMapping](#schemausertodnmapping)]|false|none|User-to-Distinguished Name (DN) map that MongoDB Cloud uses to transform a Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) username into an LDAP DN.|
