Group of settings that configure a MongoDB cluster.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acceptDataRisksAndForceReplicaSetReconfig|string(date-time)|false|none|If reconfiguration is necessary to regain a primary due to a regional outage, submit this field alongside your topology reconfiguration to request a new regional outage resistant topology. Forced reconfigurations during an outage of the majority of electable nodes carry a risk of data loss if replicated writes (even majority committed writes) have not been replicated to the new primary node. MongoDB Atlas docs contain more information. To proceed with an operation which carries that risk, set `acceptDataRisksAndForceReplicaSetReconfig` to the current date. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|advancedConfiguration|[ApiAtlasClusterAdvancedConfigurationView](#schemaapiatlasclusteradvancedconfigurationview)|false|none|Group of settings that configures a subset of the advanced configuration details.|
|autoScaling|[ClusterAutoScalingSettings](#schemaclusterautoscalingsettings)|false|none|Range of instance sizes to which your cluster can scale.|
|backupEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether the cluster can perform backups. If set to `true`, the cluster can perform backups. You must set this value to `true` for NVMe clusters. Backup uses Cloud Backups for dedicated clusters and Shared Cluster Backups for tenant clusters. If set to `false`, the cluster doesn't use MongoDB Cloud backups.|
|biConnector|[BiConnector](#schemabiconnector)|false|none|Settings needed to configure the MongoDB Connector for Business Intelligence for this cluster.|
|clusterType|string|false|none|Configuration of nodes that comprise the cluster.|
|configServerManagementMode|string|false|none|Config Server Management Mode for creating or updating a sharded cluster. When configured as `ATLAS_MANAGED`, Atlas may automatically switch the cluster's config server type for optimal performance and savings. When configured as `FIXED_TO_DEDICATED`, the cluster will always use a dedicated config server.|
|configServerType|string|false|read-only|Describes a sharded cluster's config server type.|
|connectionStrings|[ClusterConnectionStrings](#schemaclusterconnectionstrings)|false|read-only|Collection of Uniform Resource Locators that point to the MongoDB database.|
|createDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud created this serverless instance. MongoDB Cloud represents this timestamp in ISO 8601 format in UTC.|
|databaseEdition|string|false|none|Available in Public Preview: Optional field that indicates whether your cluster will be Atlas INFINITE or CORE. This field applies only to flex and shared clusters. You can set it only when you create the cluster, or when you upgrade a flex cluster to a dedicated cluster. This value is immutable once the dedicated cluster exists; attempting to change it on an update request returns an error.|
|deleteAfterCreationHours|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of hours after cluster creation that this cluster will be automatically deleted.<br><br>This field is used to derive `deleteAfterDate` relative to `createDate`.<br><br>When set to null or zero on cluster creation, the cluster will not be automatically deleted.<br><br>When set to a positive value on cluster creation, the cluster will be automatically deleted after the specified number of hours.<br><br>When updating this field on an existing (non-deleted) cluster, and this is set to null, then existing values are preserved for this & `deleteAfterDate`.<br><br>When updating this field on an existing (non-deleted) cluster, and this is set to zero, then `deleteAfterDate` is reset to null (disable auto deletion) regardless of previous configurations.<br><br>When updating this field on an existing (non-deleted) cluster, and this is set to a positive value, then `createDate` + `deleteAfterCreationHours` must be later than now else the field update is ignored and existing values are preserved for this & `deleteAfterDate`.|
|deleteAfterDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|The date at which this cluster will be automatically deleted.<br><br>This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC and is derived based on the `createDate` + `deleteAfterCreationHours`.|
|diskSizeGB|number(double)|false|none|Storage capacity of instance data volumes expressed in gigabytes. Increase this number to add capacity.<br><br> This value is not configurable on M0/M2/M5 clusters.<br><br> MongoDB Cloud requires this parameter if you set `replicationSpecs`.<br><br> If you specify a disk size below the minimum (10 GB), this parameter defaults to the minimum disk size value. <br><br> Storage charge calculations depend on whether you choose the default value or a custom value.<br><br> The maximum value for disk storage cannot exceed 50 times the maximum RAM for the selected cluster. If you require more storage space, consider upgrading your cluster to a higher tier.|
|diskWarmingMode|string|false|none|Disk warming mode selection.|
|effectiveDatabaseEdition|string|false|read-only|Available in Public Preview: Field that represents whether your cluster is Atlas INFINITE or CORE. This field applies only to flex and shared clusters. This is read-only and always returned in the response. It reflects the actual cluster state. This value matches `databaseEdition` if it was set, otherwise it reflects the default database edition assigned to the cluster.|
|encryptionAtRestProvider|string|false|none|Cloud service provider that manages your customer keys to provide an additional layer of encryption at rest for the cluster. To enable customer key management for encryption at rest, the cluster `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].{type}Specs.instanceSize` setting must be `M10` or higher and `"backupEnabled" : false` or omitted entirely.|
|featureCompatibilityVersion|string|false|read-only|Feature compatibility version of the cluster.|
|featureCompatibilityVersionExpirationDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Feature compatibility version expiration date. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|globalClusterSelfManagedSharding|boolean|false|none|Set this field to configure the Sharding Management Mode when creating a new Global Cluster.<br><br>When set to false, the management mode is set to Atlas-Managed Sharding. This mode fully manages the sharding of your Global Cluster and is built to provide a seamless deployment experience.<br><br>When set to true, the management mode is set to Self-Managed Sharding. This mode leaves the management of shards in your hands and is built to provide an advanced and flexible deployment experience.<br><br>This setting cannot be changed once the cluster is deployed.|
|groupId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal character string that identifies the project.|
|id|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the cluster.|
|labels|[[ComponentLabel](#schemacomponentlabel)]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Collection of key-value pairs between 1 to 255 characters in length that tag and categorize the cluster. The MongoDB Cloud console doesn't display your labels.<br><br>Cluster labels are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. We strongly recommend that you use Resource Tags instead.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|read-only|List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships.|
|mongoDBEmployeeAccessGrant|[EmployeeAccessGrantView](#schemaemployeeaccessgrantview)|false|read-only|MongoDB employee granted access level and expiration for a cluster.|
|mongoDBMajorVersion|string|false|none|MongoDB major version of the cluster.<br><br>On creation: Choose from the available versions of MongoDB, or leave unspecified for the current recommended default in the MongoDB Cloud platform. The recommended version is a recent Long Term Support version. The default is not guaranteed to be the most recently released version throughout the entire release cycle. For versions available in a specific project, see the linked documentation or use the API endpoint for [project LTS versions endpoint](#tag/Projects/operation/getProjectLTSVersions).<br><br> On update: Increase version only by 1 major version at a time. If the cluster is pinned to a MongoDB feature compatibility version exactly one major version below the current MongoDB version, the MongoDB version can be downgraded to the previous major version.|
|mongoDBVersion|string|false|none|Version of MongoDB that the cluster runs.|
|mongoURI|string|false|read-only|Base connection string that you can use to connect to the cluster. MongoDB Cloud displays the string only after the cluster starts, not while it builds the cluster.|
|mongoURIUpdated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time when someone last updated the connection string. MongoDB Cloud represents this timestamp in ISO 8601 format in UTC.|
|mongoURIWithOptions|string|false|read-only|Connection string that you can use to connect to the cluster including the `replicaSet`, `ssl`, and `authSource` query parameters with values appropriate for the cluster. You may need to add MongoDB database users. The response returns this parameter once the cluster can receive requests, not while it builds the cluster.|
|name|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|numShards|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of shards up to 50 to deploy for a sharded cluster. The resource returns `1` to indicate a replica set and values of `2` and higher to indicate a sharded cluster. The returned value equals the number of shards in the cluster.|
|paused|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether the cluster is paused.|
|pitEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether the cluster uses continuous cloud backups.|
|providerBackupEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether the M10 or higher cluster can perform Cloud Backups. If set to `true`, the cluster can perform backups. If this and `backupEnabled` are set to `false`, the cluster doesn't use MongoDB Cloud backups.|
|providerSettings|[ClusterProviderSettings](#schemaclusterprovidersettings)|false|none|Group of cloud provider settings that configure the provisioned MongoDB hosts.|
|replicaSetScalingStrategy|string|false|none|Set this field to configure the replica set scaling mode for your cluster.<br><br>By default, Atlas scales under `WORKLOAD_TYPE`. This mode allows Atlas to scale your analytics nodes in parallel to your operational nodes.<br><br>When configured as `SEQUENTIAL`, Atlas scales all nodes sequentially. This mode is intended for steady-state workloads and applications performing latency-sensitive secondary reads.<br><br>When configured as `NODE_TYPE`, Atlas scales your electable nodes in parallel with your read-only and analytics nodes. This mode is intended for large, dynamic workloads requiring frequent and timely cluster tier scaling. This is the fastest scaling strategy, but it might impact latency of workloads when performing extensive secondary reads.|
|replicationFactor|integer(int32)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Number of members that belong to the replica set. Each member retains a copy of your databases, providing high availability and data redundancy. Use `replicationSpecs` instead.|
|replicationSpec|object|false|none|Physical location where MongoDB Cloud provisions cluster nodes.|
|replicationSpecs|[[LegacyReplicationSpec](#schemalegacyreplicationspec)]|false|none|List of settings that configure your cluster regions.<br><br>- For Global Clusters, each object in the array represents one zone where MongoDB Cloud deploys your clusters nodes.<br>- For non-Global sharded clusters and replica sets, the single object represents where MongoDB Cloud deploys your clusters nodes.|
|rootCertType|string|false|none|Root Certificate Authority that MongoDB Atlas cluster uses. MongoDB Cloud supports Internet Security Research Group.|
|srvAddress|string|false|read-only|Connection string that you can use to connect to the cluster. The `+srv` modifier forces the connection to use Transport Layer Security (TLS). The `mongoURI` parameter lists additional options.|
|stateName|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label that indicates any current activity being taken on this cluster by the Atlas control plane. With the exception of CREATING and DELETING states, clusters should always be available and have a Primary node even when in states indicating ongoing activity.<br><br> - `IDLE`: Atlas is making no changes to this cluster and all changes requested via the UI or API can be assumed to have been applied.<br> - `CREATING`: A cluster being provisioned for the very first time returns state CREATING until it is ready for connections. Ensure IP Access List and DB Users are configured before attempting to connect.<br> - `UPDATING`: A change requested via the UI, API, AutoScaling, or other scheduled activity is taking place.<br> - `DELETING`: The cluster is in the process of deletion and will soon be deleted.<br> - `REPAIRING`: One or more nodes in the cluster are being returned to service by the Atlas control plane. Other nodes should continue to provide service as normal.|
|tags|[[ResourceTag](#schemaresourcetag)]|false|none|List that contains key-value pairs between 1 to 255 characters in length for tagging and categorizing the cluster.|
|terminationProtectionEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether termination protection is enabled on the cluster. If set to `true`, MongoDB Cloud won't delete the cluster. If set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud will delete the cluster.|
|versionReleaseSystem|string|false|none|Method by which the cluster maintains the MongoDB versions. If value is `CONTINUOUS`, you must not specify `mongoDBMajorVersion`.|

For versions available in a specific project, see the linked documentation or use the API endpoint for [project LTS versions endpoint](#tag/Projects/operation/getProjectLTSVersions).<br><br> On update: Increase version only by 1 major version at a time. If the cluster is pinned to a MongoDB feature compatibility version exactly one major version below the current MongoDB version, the MongoDB version can be downgraded to the previous major version.|
|mongoDBVersion|string|false|none|Version of MongoDB that the cluster runs.|
|mongoURI|string|false|read-only|Base connection string that you can use to connect to the cluster. MongoDB Cloud displays the string only after the cluster starts, not while it builds the cluster.|
|mongoURIUpdated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time when someone last updated the connection string. MongoDB Cloud represents this timestamp in ISO 8601 format in UTC.|
|mongoURIWithOptions|string|false|read-only|Connection string that you can use to connect to the cluster including the `replicaSet`, `ssl`, and `authSource` query parameters with values appropriate for the cluster. You may need to add MongoDB database users. The response returns this parameter once the cluster can receive requests, not while it builds the cluster.|
|name|string|true|none|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster.|
|numShards|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of shards up to 50 to deploy for a sharded cluster. The resource returns `1` to indicate a replica set and values of `2` and higher to indicate a sharded cluster. The returned value equals the number of shards in the cluster.|
|paused|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether the cluster is paused.|
|pitEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether the cluster uses continuous cloud backups.|
|providerBackupEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether the M10 or higher cluster can perform Cloud Backups. If set to `true`, the cluster can perform backups. If this and `backupEnabled` are set to `false`, the cluster doesn't use MongoDB Cloud backups.|
|providerSettings|[ClusterProviderSettings](#schemaclusterprovidersettings)|false|none|Group of cloud provider settings that configure the provisioned MongoDB hosts.|
|replicaSetScalingStrategy|string|false|none|Set this field to configure the replica set scaling mode for your cluster.<br><br>By default, Atlas scales under `WORKLOAD_TYPE`. This mode allows Atlas to scale your analytics nodes in parallel to your operational nodes.<br><br>When configured as `SEQUENTIAL`, Atlas scales all nodes sequentially. This mode is intended for steady-state workloads and applications performing latency-sensitive secondary reads.<br><br>When configured as `NODE_TYPE`, Atlas scales your electable nodes in parallel with your read-only and analytics nodes. This mode is intended for large, dynamic workloads requiring frequent and timely cluster tier scaling. This is the fastest scaling strategy, but it might impact latency of workloads when performing extensive secondary reads.|
|replicationFactor|integer(int32)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Number of members that belong to the replica set. Each member retains a copy of your databases, providing high availability and data redundancy. Use `replicationSpecs` instead.|
|replicationSpec|object|false|none|Physical location where MongoDB Cloud provisions cluster nodes.|
|replicationSpecs|[[LegacyReplicationSpec](#schemalegacyreplicationspec)]|false|none|List of settings that configure your cluster regions.<br><br>- For Global Clusters, each object in the array represents one zone where MongoDB Cloud deploys your clusters nodes.<br>- For non-Global sharded clusters and replica sets, the single object represents where MongoDB Cloud deploys your clusters nodes.|
|rootCertType|string|false|none|Root Certificate Authority that MongoDB Atlas cluster uses. MongoDB Cloud supports Internet Security Research Group.|
|srvAddress|string|false|read-only|Connection string that you can use to connect to the cluster. The `+srv` modifier forces the connection to use Transport Layer Security (TLS). The `mongoURI` parameter lists additional options.|
|stateName|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label that indicates any current activity being taken on this cluster by the Atlas control plane. With the exception of CREATING and DELETING states, clusters should always be available and have a Primary node even when in states indicating ongoing activity.<br><br> - `IDLE`: Atlas is making no changes to this cluster and all changes requested via the UI or API can be assumed to have been applied.<br> - `CREATING`: A cluster being provisioned for the very first time returns state CREATING until it is ready for connections. Ensure IP Access List and DB Users are configured before attempting to connect.<br> - `UPDATING`: A change requested via the UI, API, AutoScaling, or other scheduled activity is taking place.<br> - `DELETING`: The cluster is in the process of deletion and will soon be deleted.<br> - `REPAIRING`: One or more nodes in the cluster are being returned to service by the Atlas control plane. Other nodes should continue to provide service as normal.|
|tags|[[ResourceTag](#schemaresourcetag)]|false|none|List that contains key-value pairs between 1 to 255 characters in length for tagging and categorizing the cluster.|
|terminationProtectionEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether termination protection is enabled on the cluster. If set to `true`, MongoDB Cloud won't delete the cluster. If set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud will delete the cluster.|
|versionReleaseSystem|string|false|none|Method by which the cluster maintains the MongoDB versions. If value is `CONTINUOUS`, you must not specify `mongoDBMajorVersion`.|

```json
{
  "collection": "string",
  "customShardKey": "string",
  "db": "string",
  "isCustomShardKeyHashed": false,
  "isShardKeyUnique": false,
  "numInitialChunks": 0,
  "presplitHashedZones": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|collection|string|true|none|Human-readable label of the collection to manage for this Global Cluster.|
|customShardKey|string|true|none|Database parameter used to divide the *collection* into shards. Global clusters require a compound shard key. This compound shard key combines the location parameter and the user-selected custom key.|
|db|string|true|none|Human-readable label of the database to manage for this Global Cluster.|
|isCustomShardKeyHashed|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether someone hashed the custom shard key for the specified collection. If you set this value to `false`, MongoDB Cloud uses ranged sharding.|
|isShardKeyUnique|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether someone [hashed](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/sh.shardCollection/#hashed-shard-keys) the custom shard key. If this parameter returns `false`, this cluster uses [ranged sharding](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/ranged-sharding/).|
|numInitialChunks|integer(int64)|false|none|Minimum number of chunks to create initially when sharding an empty collection with a [hashed shard key](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/hashed-sharding/).|
|presplitHashedZones|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud should create and distribute initial chunks for an empty or non-existing collection. MongoDB Cloud distributes data based on the defined zones and zone ranges for the collection.|

Request schema for creating a metric integration.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregationTemporality|string|true|none|The temporality to send to the metric integration.|

|endpoint|string|true|none|OpenTelemetry collector endpoint URL. Must use HTTPS.|
|headers|[[Header](#schemaheader)]|false|write-only|HTTP headers for authentication and configuration. Total size limit 2KB. Required when `authType` is `HEADER`.|
|integrationType|string|true|none|Type of metric integration. Identifies which protocol will be used for the integration. This value cannot be modified after the integration is created.|
|metricSelection|[string]|true|none|Array of metric categories to export. Determines which types of metrics are sent to the integration.|
|oauth|[OAuthConfigRequest](#schemaoauthconfigrequest)|false|none|OAuth 2.0 client credentials configuration. Required when `authType` is `OAUTH2`. Secrets are never returned.|
|providerType|string|true|none|The provider type for the metric integration. Identifies the third-party service provider.|

<a id="schema_MetricIntegrationUpdateRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSmetricintegrationupdaterequest"></a>
<a id="tocsmetricintegrationupdaterequest"></a>

```json
{
  "aggregationTemporality": "DELTA",
  "authType": "HEADER",
  "endpoint": "https://otel-collector.example.com:4318/v1/metrics",
  "headers": [
    {
      "name": "Authorization",
      "value": "Bearer token123"
    }
  ],
  "integrationType": "OTEL",
  "metricSelection": [
    "ATLAS_STREAM_PROCESSING"
  ],
  "oauth": {
    "clientAuthMethod": "CLIENT_SECRET",
    "clientId": "atlas-otel",
    "clientSecret": "password",
    "scopes": [
      "string"
    ],
    "tokenEndpoint": "https://idp.example.com/oauth2/token",
    "tokenRequestParams": {
      "resource": "https://otel.example.com/metrics"
    }
  },
  "providerType": "CUSTOM"
}
```

Request schema for updating a metric integration. Omitted OAuth fields keep their stored values. An explicit null, an empty `scopes` array, or an empty `tokenRequestParams` object clears that field. Omitting `clientSecret` keeps the stored secret.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregationTemporality|string|true|none|The temporality to send to the metric integration.|
|authType|string|true|none|Authentication method the integration uses when exporting metrics to the endpoint. `HEADER` authenticates with the static HTTP headers provided in the `headers` field, which must be set when this value is used. `OAUTH2` acquires a bearer token from an OAuth 2.0 token endpoint using the `oauth` field.|
|endpoint|string|true|none|OpenTelemetry collector endpoint URL. Must use HTTPS.|
|headers|[[Header](#schemaheader)]|false|write-only|HTTP headers for authentication and configuration. Total size limit 2KB. Required when `authType` is `HEADER`.|
|integrationType|string|true|none|Type of metric integration. Identifies which protocol will be used for the integration. This value cannot be modified after the integration is created.|
|metricSelection|[string]|true|none|Array of metric categories to export. Determines which types of metrics are sent to the integration.|
|oauth|[OAuthConfigRequest](#schemaoauthconfigrequest)|false|none|OAuth 2.0 client credentials configuration. Required when `authType` is `OAUTH2`. Secrets are never returned.|
|providerType|string|true|none|The provider type for the metric integration. Identifies the third-party service provider.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|aggregationTemporality|DELTA|
|aggregationTemporality|CUMULATIVE|
|authType|HEADER|
|authType|OAUTH2|
|integrationType|OTEL|
|metricSelection|ATLAS_STREAM_PROCESSING|
|metricSelection|MONGODB_METRICS|
|metricSelection|HARDWARE_METRICS|
|providerType|CUSTOM|
|providerType|DATADOG|
|providerType|DYNATRACE|
|providerType|NEW_RELIC|

<h2 id="tocS_MicrosoftTeamsNotification">MicrosoftTeamsNotification</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamicrosoftteamsnotification"></a>
<a id="schema_MicrosoftTeamsNotification"></a>
<a id="tocSmicrosoftteamsnotification"></a>
<a id="tocsmicrosoftteamsnotification"></a>

```json
{
  "delayMin": 0,
  "integrationId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "intervalMin": 5,
  "microsoftTeamsWebhookUrl": "https://webhook.com/****",
  "notifierId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "typeName": "MICROSOFT_TEAMS"
}
```

Microsoft Teams notification configuration for MongoDB Cloud to send information when an event triggers an alert condition.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delayMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes that MongoDB Cloud waits after detecting an alert condition before it sends out the first notification.|
|integrationId|string|false|none|The id of the associated integration, the credentials of which to use for requests.|
|intervalMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes to wait between successive notifications. MongoDB Cloud sends notifications until someone acknowledges the unacknowledged alert.<br><br>PagerDuty, VictorOps, and OpsGenie notifications don't return this element. Configure and manage the notification interval within each of those services.|
|microsoftTeamsWebhookUrl|string|false|none|Microsoft Teams Webhook Uniform Resource Locator (URL) that MongoDB Cloud needs to send this notification via Microsoft Teams. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "MICROSOFT_TEAMS"`. If the URL later becomes invalid, MongoDB Cloud sends an email to the project owners. If the key remains invalid, MongoDB Cloud removes it.<br><br>**NOTE**: When you view or edit the alert for a Microsoft Teams notification, the URL appears partially redacted.|
|notifierId|string|false|none|The `notifierId` is a system-generated unique identifier assigned to each notification method. This is needed when updating third-party notifications without requiring explicit authentication credentials.|
|typeName|string|true|none|Human-readable label that displays the alert notification type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|typeName|MICROSOFT_TEAMS|

|timestamp|string|false|read-only|Date and time when someone made this authentication attempt. MongoDB Cloud represents this timestamp in ISO 8601 format in UTC.|
|username|string|false|read-only|Username used to authenticate against the database.|

|groupId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the project that owns this alert configuration.|

|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|read-only|List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships.|
|matchers|[[AlertMatcher](#schemaalertmatcher)]|false|none|Matching conditions for target resources.|
|notifications|[[AlertsNotificationRootForGroup](#schemaalertsnotificationrootforgroup)]|true|none|List that contains the targets that MongoDB Cloud sends notifications.|
|severityOverride|[EventSeverity](#schemaeventseverity)|false|none|Severity of the event.|
|updated|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time when someone last updated this alert configuration. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|

|threshold|number(double)|false|none|Value of metric that, when exceeded, triggers an alert.|
|units|[RawMetricUnits](#schemarawmetricunits)|false|none|Element used to express the quantity. This can be an element of time, storage capacity, and the like.|

Audit saving information about Atlas cloud provider and other Atlas related details.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiKeyId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the API Key that triggered the event. If this resource returns this parameter, it doesn't return the `userId` parameter.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Date and time when this event occurred. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|dbUserUsername|string|false|read-only|The username of the MongoDB User that was created, deleted, or edited.|
|delegatePrincipal|[Principal](#schemaprincipal)|false|read-only|Information about a principal, such as an OAuth application, that triggered the event through delegated access.|
|eventTypeName|[NDSAuditTypeViewForNdsGroup](#schemandsaudittypeviewforndsgroup)|true|none|Unique identifier of event type.|
|groupId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the project in which the event occurred. The `eventId` identifies the specific event.|
|id|string|true|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the event.|
|isGlobalAdmin|boolean|false|read-only|Flag that indicates whether a MongoDB employee triggered the specified event.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|read-only|List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships.|
|orgId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization to which these events apply.|
|publicKey|string|false|read-only|Public part of the API key that triggered the event. If this resource returns this parameter, it doesn't return the **username** parameter.|
|raw|[raw](#schemaraw)|false|read-only|Additional meta information captured about this event. The response returns this parameter as a JSON object when the query parameter `includeRaw=true`. The list of fields in the raw document may change. Don't rely on raw values for formal monitoring.|
|remoteAddress|string|false|read-only|IPv4 or IPv6 address from which the user triggered this event.|
|userId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the console user who triggered the event. If this resource returns this parameter, it doesn't return the `apiKeyId` parameter.|
|username|string(email)|false|read-only|Email address for the user who triggered this event. If this resource returns this parameter, it doesn't return the `publicApiKey` parameter.|
|whitelistEntry|string|false|read-only|Entry in the list of source host addresses that the API key accepts and this event targets.|

```json
{
  "awsSecurityGroup": "string",
  "cidrBlock": "string",
  "comment": "string",
  "deleteAfterDate": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "groupId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "ipAddress": "string",
  "links": [
    {
      "href": "https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas",
      "rel": "self"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|awsSecurityGroup|string|false|none|Unique string of the Amazon Web Services (AWS) security group that you want to add to the project's IP access list. Your IP access list entry can be one `awsSecurityGroup`, one `cidrBlock`, or one `ipAddress`. You must configure Virtual Private Connection (VPC) peering for your project before you can add an AWS security group to an IP access list. You cannot set AWS security groups as temporary access list entries. Don't set this parameter if you set `cidrBlock` or `ipAddress`.|
|cidrBlock|string|false|none|Range of IP addresses in Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) notation that you want to add to the project's IP access list. Your IP access list entry can be one `awsSecurityGroup`, one `cidrBlock`, or one `ipAddress`. Don't set this parameter if you set `awsSecurityGroup` or `ipAddress`.|
|comment|string|false|none|Remark that explains the purpose or scope of this IP access list entry.|
|deleteAfterDate|string(date-time)|false|none|Date and time after which MongoDB Cloud deletes the temporary access list entry. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC and can include the time zone designation. The date must be later than the current date but no later than one week after you submit this request. The resource returns this parameter if you specified an expiration date when creating this IP access list entry.|
|groupId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the project that contains the IP access list to which you want to add one or more entries.|
|ipAddress|string|false|none|IP address that you want to add to the project's IP access list. Your IP access list entry can be one `awsSecurityGroup`, one `cidrBlock`, or one `ipAddress`. Don't set this parameter if you set `awsSecurityGroup` or `cidrBlock`.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|read-only|List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships.|

Details to integrate one New Relic account with one MongoDB Cloud project.

***IMPORTANT**: Effective Wednesday, June 16th, 2021, New Relic no longer supports the plugin-based integration with MongoDB. We do not recommend that you sign up for the plugin-based integration.

Consider configuring an alternative monitoring integration before June 16th to maintain visibility into your MongoDB deployments.

|licenseKey|string|true|none|Unique 40-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your New Relic license.<br><br>**IMPORTANT**: Effective Wednesday, June 16th, 2021, New Relic no longer supports the plugin-based integration with MongoDB. We do not recommend that you sign up for the plugin-based integration.<br>Consider configuring an alternative monitoring integration before June 16th to maintain visibility into your MongoDB deployments.|
|readToken|string|true|none|Query key used to access your New Relic account.|
|type|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the service to which you want to integrate with MongoDB Cloud. The value must match the third-party service integration type.|
|writeToken|string|true|none|Insert key associated with your New Relic account.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|acknowledgedUntil|string(date-time)|false|none|Date and time until which this alert has been acknowledged. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. The resource returns this parameter if a MongoDB User previously acknowledged this alert.<br><br>- To acknowledge this alert forever, set the parameter value to 100 years in the future.<br><br>- To unacknowledge a previously acknowledged alert, do not set this parameter value.|
|acknowledgementComment|string|false|none|Comment that a MongoDB Cloud user submitted when acknowledging the alert.|
|acknowledgingUsername|string(email)|false|read-only|MongoDB Cloud username of the person who acknowledged the alert. The response returns this parameter if a MongoDB Cloud user previously acknowledged this alert.|

|clusterName|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster to which this alert applies. This resource returns this parameter for alerts of events impacting backups, replica sets, or sharded clusters.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud created this alert. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|currentValue|[NumberMetricValueView](#schemanumbermetricvalueview)|false|read-only|Measurement of the `metricName` recorded at the time of the event.|
|eventTypeName|[HostMetricEventTypeViewAlertable](#schemahostmetriceventtypeviewalertable)|true|none|Event type that triggers an alert.|
|groupId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the project that owns this alert.|
|hostnameAndPort|string|false|read-only|Hostname and port of the host to which this alert applies. The resource returns this parameter for alerts of events impacting hosts or replica sets.|
|id|string|true|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies this alert.|
|lastNotified|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time that any notifications were last sent for this alert. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. The resource returns this parameter if MongoDB Cloud has sent notifications for this alert.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|read-only|List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships.|
|metricName|string|false|read-only|Name of the metric against which Atlas checks the configured `metricThreshold.threshold`.<br><br>To learn more about the available metrics, see <a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-host-metrics/#std-label-measurement-types" target="_blank">Host Metrics</a>.<br><br>**NOTE**: If you set `eventTypeName` to `OUTSIDE_SERVERLESS_METRIC_THRESHOLD`, you can specify only metrics available for serverless. To learn more, see <a href="https://dochub.mongodb.org/core/alert-config-serverless-measurements" target="_blank">Serverless Measurements</a>.|
|orgId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal character string that identifies the organization that owns the project to which this alert applies.|
|replicaSetName|string|false|read-only|Name of the replica set to which this alert applies. The response returns this parameter for alerts of events impacting backups, hosts, or replica sets.|
|resolved|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time that this alert changed to `"status" : "CLOSED"`. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. The resource returns this parameter once `"status" : "CLOSED"`.|
|severity|string|false|read-only|Severity of the event.|
|status|string|true|read-only|State of this alert at the time you requested its details. TRACKING indicates the alert condition exists but has not persisted for the minimum notification delay. OPEN indicates the alert condition currently exists. CLOSED indicates the alert condition has been resolved.|
|updated|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Date and time when someone last updated this alert. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|

|userId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the console user who triggered the event. If this resource returns this parameter, it doesn't return the `apiKeyId` parameter.|

```json
  "clientId": "atlas-otel",
  "clientSecret": "password",
  "scopes": [
    "string"
  ],
  "tokenEndpoint": "https://idp.example.com/oauth2/token",
  "tokenRequestParams": {
    "resource": "https://otel.example.com/metrics"
  }
}
```

OAuth 2.0 client credentials configuration. Required when `authType` is `OAUTH2`. Secrets are never returned.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clientAuthMethod|string|true|none|How the client authenticates to the token endpoint. `CLIENT_SECRET` sends a shared secret. `PRIVATE_KEY_JWT` signs a client assertion with an Atlas-generated, Atlas-managed key. Register the returned JWKS URL with your identity provider.|
|clientId|string|true|none|OAuth 2.0 client identifier registered with the token endpoint.|
|clientSecret|string(password)|false|write-only|Shared client secret. Required when `clientAuthMethod` is `CLIENT_SECRET`, and rejected for `PRIVATE_KEY_JWT`. Encrypted at rest and never returned.|
|scopes|[string]|false|none|Optional OAuth 2.0 scopes requested on the token, sent as a space delimited `scope` parameter. Applies to both client authentication methods.|
|tokenEndpoint|string|true|none|OAuth 2.0 token endpoint URL. Must use HTTPS.|
|tokenRequestParams|object|false|none|Optional provider-specific parameters added to the token request, for example a resource indicator. Applies to both client authentication methods.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|clientAuthMethod|CLIENT_SECRET|
|clientAuthMethod|PRIVATE_KEY_JWT|

```json
  },
```

```json
  "progress": {

    "total": 0,

  },
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|estimatedCompletionTime|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|Estimated completion time in ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|expiresAt|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Expiration time in ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|operationId|string|true|read-only|Unique identifier of the operation.|
|operationType|string|true|read-only|Type of mutation performed by the operation.|
|progress|[OperationProgress](#schemaoperationprogress)|false|read-only|Progress made by an active operation.|
|resultHref|string(uri) \| null|false|read-only|URI of the affected resource. Required when status is SUCCEEDED.|
|retryAfterSeconds|integer(int32) \| null|false|read-only|Recommended polling delay. Required while the operation is active.|
|status|string|true|read-only|State of the operation.|
|statusMessage|string \| null|false|read-only|Human-readable operation status.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Last update time in ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|operationType|UPDATE|
|operationType|DELETE|
|operationType|CUSTOM|
|status|PENDING|
|status|IN_PROGRESS|
|status|SUCCEEDED|
|status|FAILED|
|status|CANCELED|
|status|SUPERSEDED|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delayMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes that MongoDB Cloud waits after detecting an alert condition before it sends out the first notification.|
|integrationId|string|false|none|The id of the associated integration, the credentials of which to use for requests.|
|intervalMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes to wait between successive notifications. MongoDB Cloud sends notifications until someone acknowledges the unacknowledged alert.<br><br>PagerDuty, VictorOps, and OpsGenie notifications don't return this element. Configure and manage the notification interval within each of those services.|
|notifierId|string|false|none|The `notifierId` is a system-generated unique identifier assigned to each notification method. This is needed when updating third-party notifications without requiring explicit authentication credentials.|
|opsGenieApiKey|string|false|none|API Key that MongoDB Cloud needs to send this notification via OpsGenie. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "OPS_GENIE"`. If the key later becomes invalid, MongoDB Cloud sends an email to the project owners. If the key remains invalid, MongoDB Cloud removes it.<br><br>**NOTE**: After you create a notification which requires an API or integration key, the key appears partially redacted when you:<br><br>* View or edit the alert through the Atlas UI.<br><br>* Query the alert for the notification through the Atlas Administration API.|

|typeName|string|true|none|Human-readable label that displays the alert notification type.|

```json
  "roles": [
    "ORG_OWNER"
  ],
  "smsEnabled": true,
  "typeName": "ORG"
}
```

Organization notification configuration for MongoDB Cloud to send information when an event triggers an alert condition.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delayMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes that MongoDB Cloud waits after detecting an alert condition before it sends out the first notification.|
|emailEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud should send email notifications. The resource requires this parameter when one of the following values have been set:<br><br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "ORG"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "GROUP"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "USER"`|
|intervalMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes to wait between successive notifications. MongoDB Cloud sends notifications until someone acknowledges the unacknowledged alert.<br><br>PagerDuty, VictorOps, and OpsGenie notifications don't return this element. Configure and manage the notification interval within each of those services.|
|notifierId|string|false|none|The `notifierId` is a system-generated unique identifier assigned to each notification method. This is needed when updating third-party notifications without requiring explicit authentication credentials.|
|roles|[string]|false|none|List that contains the one or more organization roles that receive the configured alert. This parameter is available when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "GROUP"` or `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "ORG"`. If you include this parameter, MongoDB Cloud sends alerts only to users assigned the roles you specify in the array. If you omit this parameter, MongoDB Cloud sends alerts to users assigned any role.|
|smsEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud should send text message notifications. The resource requires this parameter when one of the following values have been set:<br><br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "ORG"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "GROUP"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "USER"`|
|typeName|string|true|none|Human-readable label that displays the alert notification type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|roles|ORG_OWNER|
|roles|ORG_MEMBER|
|roles|ORG_GROUP_CREATOR|
|roles|ORG_BILLING_ADMIN|
|roles|ORG_BILLING_READ_ONLY|
|roles|ORG_READ_ONLY|
|typeName|ORG|

```json
}
```

Maintenance configuration settings for an organization.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|effectiveWaveAssignmentMode|string|false|read-only|Wave assignment mode that Atlas uses when scheduling maintenance for projects in this organization. This read-only field takes precedence over `waveAssignmentMode` for scheduling. It matches `waveAssignmentMode` except when cross-organization maintenance sequencing is enabled and this organization is a linked non-paying organization, in which case it reflects the paying organization's `waveAssignmentMode`. Possible values are `MANUAL` and `ENV_TAG_MAPPING`. Defaults to `MANUAL` when no mode is configured. Omitted from GET responses when maintenance sequencing is disabled for this organization.|
|waveAssignmentMode|string \| null|false|none|Mode explicitly configured for this organization that determines how maintenance waves are assigned to projects. Possible values are `MANUAL` and `ENV_TAG_MAPPING`. Omitted from the response when no explicit preference has been set; in that case `effectiveWaveAssignmentMode` reflects the value the system uses (`MANUAL` by default). Atlas uses read-only `effectiveWaveAssignmentMode` (not this field) for scheduling. In a cross-organization billing hierarchy, a linked non-paying organization cannot update its `effectiveWaveAssignmentMode` field, which inherits from the paying organization's `waveAssignmentMode`. In this case, a linked non-paying organization's `effectiveWaveAssignmentMode` and `waveAssignmentMode` might differ.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|effectiveWaveAssignmentMode|MANUAL|
|effectiveWaveAssignmentMode|ENV_TAG_MAPPING|
|waveAssignmentMode|MANUAL|
|waveAssignmentMode|ENV_TAG_MAPPING|

```json
{
  "waveAssignmentMode": "MANUAL"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|waveAssignmentMode|string|false|none|Mode configured for this organization that determines how maintenance waves are assigned to projects. Possible values are `MANUAL` and `ENV_TAG_MAPPING`. Defaults to `MANUAL` when unset. Set the organization to `ENV_TAG_MAPPING` mode to have Atlas derive the maintenance wave from each project's environment tag. The tag key must be `environment`. The tag value determines the wave: `development` or `test` maps to Wave 1, `staging` maps to Wave 2, and `production` maps to Wave 3. Only this field can be updated; Atlas derives read-only `effectiveWaveAssignmentMode` on GET responses and uses that value for scheduling when it differs from `waveAssignmentMode`. Omit this field to leave the current value unchanged. Specify null to reset to the default value (`MANUAL`).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|waveAssignmentMode|MANUAL|
|waveAssignmentMode|ENV_TAG_MAPPING|

Collection of settings that configures the organization.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|apiAccessListRequired|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether to require API operations to originate from an IP Address added to the API access list for the specified organization.|
|customSessionTimeouts|[CustomSessionTimeouts](#schemacustomsessiontimeouts)|false|none|Defines the session timeout settings for managing user sessions at the organization level. When set to null, the field's value is unset, and the default timeout settings are applied.|
|genAIFeaturesEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether this organization has access to generative AI features. This setting only applies to Atlas Commercial and is enabled by default. Once this setting is turned on, Project Owners may be able to enable or disable individual AI features at the project level.|
|maxServiceAccountSecretValidityInHours|integer(int32)|false|none|Number that represents the maximum period before expiry in hours for new Atlas Admin API Service Account secrets within the specified organization.|
|multiFactorAuthRequired|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether to require users to set up Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) before accessing the specified organization. To learn more, see: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-multi-factor-authentication/.|
|operationsContact|string \| null|false|none|String that specifies a distribution list email address for the specified organization to receive proactive notifications about its infrastructure. The operations contact is used for notifications only and is not authorized to make decisions or approvals. Passing an explicit null clears the existing operations contact (if any). An empty string is invalid and is rejected with a validation error.|
|restrictEmployeeAccess|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether to block MongoDB Support from accessing Atlas infrastructure and cluster logs for any deployment in the specified organization without explicit permission. Once this setting is turned on, you can grant MongoDB Support a 24-hour bypass access to the Atlas deployment to resolve support issues. To learn more, see: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-restrict-support-access/.|
|securityContact|string|false|none|String that specifies a single email address for the specified organization to receive security-related notifications. Specifying a security contact does not grant them authorization or access to Atlas for security decisions or approvals. An empty string is valid and clears the existing security contact (if any).|
|streamsCrossGroupEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether a group's Atlas Stream Processing workspaces in this organization can create connections to other group's clusters in the same organization.|

```json
{
  "delayMin": 0,
  "integrationId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "intervalMin": 5,
  "notifierId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "region": "US",
  "serviceKey": "****************************7890",
  "typeName": "PAGER_DUTY"
}
```

PagerDuty notification configuration for MongoDB Cloud to send information when an event triggers an alert condition.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delayMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes that MongoDB Cloud waits after detecting an alert condition before it sends out the first notification.|
|integrationId|string|false|none|The id of the associated integration, the credentials of which to use for requests.|
|intervalMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes to wait between successive notifications. MongoDB Cloud sends notifications until someone acknowledges the unacknowledged alert.<br><br>PagerDuty, VictorOps, and OpsGenie notifications don't return this element. Configure and manage the notification interval within each of those services.|
|notifierId|string|false|none|The `notifierId` is a system-generated unique identifier assigned to each notification method. This is needed when updating third-party notifications without requiring explicit authentication credentials.|
|region|string|false|none|PagerDuty region that indicates which API Uniform Resource Locator (URL) to use.|
|serviceKey|string|false|none|PagerDuty service key that MongoDB Cloud needs to send notifications via PagerDuty. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "PAGER_DUTY"`. If the key later becomes invalid, MongoDB Cloud sends an email to the project owners. If the key remains invalid, MongoDB Cloud removes it.<br><br>**NOTE**: After you create a notification which requires an API or integration key, the key appears partially redacted when you:<br><br>* View or edit the alert through the Atlas UI.<br><br>* Query the alert for the notification through the Atlas Administration API.|
|typeName|string|true|none|Human-readable label that displays the alert notification type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|region|US|
|region|EU|
|typeName|PAGER_DUTY|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|avgObjSize|number(double)|false|read-only|The average size of an object in the collection of this index.|
|collation|object|false|read-only|Collation the queries behind this suggestion run with. An index only serves a query when the two share a collation, so an index created from this suggestion must be created with it. Absent when those queries use the default (simple) collation.|
|id|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies this index.|
|impact|[string]|false|read-only|List that contains unique 24-hexadecimal character string that identifies the query shapes in this response that the Performance Advisor suggests.|
|index|[object]|false|read-only|List that contains documents that specify a key in the index and its sort order.|
|namespace|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label that identifies the namespace on the specified host. The resource expresses this parameter value as `<database>.<collection>`.|
|weight|number(double)|false|read-only|Estimated performance improvement that the suggested index provides. This value corresponds to **Impact** in the Performance Advisor user interface.|

<h2 id="tocS_PerformanceAdvisorSlowQueryMetrics">PerformanceAdvisorSlowQueryMetrics</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaperformanceadvisorslowquerymetrics"></a>

```json
{
  "docsExamined": 0,
  "docsExaminedReturnedRatio": 0,
  "docsReturned": 0,
  "fromUserConnection": true,
  "hasAutoEmbedding": true,
  "hasIndexCoverage": true,
  "hasRerank": true,
  "hasSort": true,
  "keysExamined": 0,
  "keysExaminedReturnedRatio": 0,
  "numYields": 0,
  "operationExecutionTime": 0,
  "responseLength": 0,
  "tokensUsed": 363
}
```

Metrics from a slow query log.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|docsExamined|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The number of documents in the collection that MongoDB scanned in order to carry out the operation.|
|docsExaminedReturnedRatio|number(double)|false|read-only|Ratio of documents examined to documents returned.|
|docsReturned|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The number of documents returned by the operation.|
|fromUserConnection|boolean|false|read-only|This boolean will be true when the server can identify the query source as non-server. This field is only available for MDB 8.0+.|
|hasAutoEmbedding|boolean|false|read-only|Flag that indicates whether the slow query used automated embedding, where MongoDB Cloud generates embeddings from raw text at query time instead of the client supplying a precomputed vector.|
|hasIndexCoverage|boolean|false|read-only|Indicates if the query has index coverage.|
|hasRerank|boolean|false|read-only|Flag that indicates whether the slow query used the `$rerank` aggregation stage, which reorders results using Voyage AI reranking models. Always `false` for MongoDB deployments earlier than 8.3.|
|hasSort|boolean|false|read-only|This boolean will be true when a query cannot use the ordering in the index to return the requested sorted results; i.e. MongoDB must sort the documents after it receives the documents from a cursor.|
|keysExamined|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The number of index keys that MongoDB scanned in order to carry out the operation.|
|keysExaminedReturnedRatio|number(double)|false|read-only|Ratio of keys examined to documents returned.|
|numYields|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The number of times the operation yielded to allow other operations to complete.|
|operationExecutionTime|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Total execution time of a query in milliseconds.|
|responseLength|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The length in bytes of the operation's result document.|
|tokensUsed|integer(int64)|false|read-only|The total inference tokens consumed by this operation, including tokens used by `$rerank`. Returned only for inference queries that consumed tokens; it is omitted otherwise, including for MongoDB deployments earlier than 8.3.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connectionString|string|false|read-only|Private endpoint-aware connection string that uses the `mongodb://` protocol to connect to this cluster through the selected private endpoints. MongoDB Cloud returns this value when `status` is `AVAILABLE`. After you submit an update, MongoDB Cloud continues to return the existing connection string until the updated connection string becomes available.|
|connectionStringId|string|true|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies this private endpoint connection string. This value is the `connectionStringId` path parameter of this resource's endpoints.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud created this private endpoint connection string. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|errorMessage|string|false|read-only|Error message that explains why this private endpoint connection string is in the `FAILED` state, including the remediation, for example when a selected endpoint was deleted mid-flight. Present only when `status` is `FAILED`.|
|managementType|string|true|read-only|Party that manages this private endpoint connection string. MongoDB Cloud returns `SELF_MANAGED` for connection strings that you create and maintain through this resource, and `IMPORTED` for records that preserve the private endpoint connection strings that this cluster exposed before migration. You can delete an imported record but not update it.|
|name|string|true|none|Human-readable label of at most 64 characters that identifies this private endpoint connection string. You can change this label without changing the connection string.|
|optimizedModeEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether this private endpoint connection string uses the optimized load-balanced mode. This mode requires a sharded cluster and a private endpoint selection that satisfies the optimized connection string requirements.|
|privateEndpointIds|[string]|true|none|Set of private endpoints that this connection string covers. MongoDB Cloud stores this set as a snapshot of your selection and never adds newly created private endpoints to it. The set accepts at most one private endpoint per cloud provider region, and can include private endpoints that the cluster does not use yet. Order is not significant and MongoDB Cloud rejects duplicate values.|
|slug|string|false|read-only|Short generated pin of at most 64 characters, unique per project. Present only when `managementType` is `SELF_MANAGED`. A self-managed connection string embeds this value in its DNS names, and its replica set horizon name is `cs-` plus this value.|
|srvConnectionString|string|false|read-only|Private endpoint-aware connection string that uses the `mongodb+srv://` protocol to connect to this cluster through the selected private endpoints. MongoDB Cloud returns this value when `status` is `AVAILABLE`. After you submit an update, MongoDB Cloud continues to return the existing connection string until the updated connection string becomes available.|
|status|string|true|read-only|State of this private endpoint connection string. MongoDB Cloud returns `PENDING` while it reconfigures the cluster, `AVAILABLE` once the connection string is usable, and `FAILED` when creation cannot complete.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud last updated this private endpoint connection string. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|


Query sampling state for one namespace of one cluster. Sampled queries feed the shard key analysis for the namespace.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|true|read-only|Flag that indicates whether query sampling is observably running on the namespace. May still be `false` in the response to a successful create request; it becomes `true` asynchronously once the cluster applies the sampling configuration.|
|namespace|string|true|none|Human-readable label that identifies the namespace (`<database>.<collection>`) on which queries are sampled.|
|sampledReadsBytes|integer(int64) \| null|false|read-only|Total size in bytes of the read operations sampled on the namespace.|
|sampledReadsCount|integer(int64) \| null|false|read-only|Number of read operations sampled on the namespace.|
|sampledWritesBytes|integer(int64) \| null|false|read-only|Total size in bytes of the write operations sampled on the namespace.|
|sampledWritesCount|integer(int64) \| null|false|read-only|Number of write operations sampled on the namespace.|
|samplesPerSecond|number(double) \| null|false|read-only|Maximum number of queries sampled per second on the namespace. MongoDB Cloud sets this rate.|
|startTime|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|Date and time when query sampling started on the namespace. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|command|string|false|read-only|The MongoDB command type issued for a query shape. The INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE commands appear only for clusters running MongoDB 9.0 or later.|
|namespace|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label that identifies the namespace on the specified host. The resource expresses this parameter value as `<database>.<collection>`.|
|queryShape|string|false|read-only|A query shape is a set of specifications that group similar queries together. Specifications can include filters, sorts, projections, aggregation pipeline stages, a namespace, and others. Queries that have similar specifications have the same query shape. This field may be null if the user lacks PII view access.|
|queryShapeHash|string|true|read-only|A hexadecimal string that represents the hash of a MongoDB query shape.|

<h2 id="tocS_QueryStatsSummary">QueryStatsSummary</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaquerystatssummary"></a>
<a id="schema_QueryStatsSummary"></a>
<a id="tocSquerystatssummary"></a>
<a id="tocsquerystatssummary"></a>

```json
{
  "avgTimeToResponseMicros": 0,
  "avgWorkingMillis": 0,
  "bytesRead": 0,
  "command": "find",
  "cpuTime": 0,
  "docsExamined": 0,
  "docsExaminedRatio": 0,
  "docsReturned": 0,
  "execCount": 0,
  "keysDeleted": 0,
  "keysExamined": 0,
  "keysExaminedRatio": 0,
  "keysInserted": 0,
  "lastExecMicros": 0,
  "nDeleted": 0,
  "nInserted": 0,
  "nMatched": 0,
  "nModified": 0,
  "nUpserted": 0,
  "namespace": "string",
  "p50ExecMicros": 0,
  "p90ExecMicros": 0,
  "p99ExecMicros": 0,
  "queryShape": "string",
  "queryShapeHash": "string",
  "systemQuery": true,
  "totalTimeToResponseMicros": 0,
  "totalWorkingMillis": 0
}
```

A summary of execution statistics for a given query shape.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|avgTimeToResponseMicros|number(double)|false|none|Average time in microseconds from the beginning of query processing to the first server response, per execution of queries with the given query shape. Calculated as `totalTimeToResponseMicros` divided by `execCount` over the requested time range. As a duration it can be longer or shorter than `avgWorkingMillis` (reported in milliseconds, so convert before comparing): longer when executions spent time blocked on locks or flow control rather than working, shorter when they kept working after the first batch to return later `getMore` batches.|
|avgWorkingMillis|number(double)|false|none|Average active execution time in milliseconds per execution of queries with the given query shape, calculated as `totalWorkingMillis` divided by `execCount` over the requested time range. Excludes intentional pauses such as time waiting on locks or flow control.|
|bytesRead|number(double)|false|none|The number of bytes read by the given query shape from the disk to the cache.|
|command|string|false|none|The MongoDB command issued for this query shape. The insert, update, and delete commands appear only for clusters running MongoDB 9.0 or later.|
|cpuTime|number(double) \| null|false|none|Total CPU time in nanoseconds consumed by queries with the given query shape. Available for MDB 8.2 and higher.|
|docsExamined|number(double)|false|none|Total number of documents examined by queries with the given query shape.|
|docsExaminedRatio|number(double)|false|none|Ratio of documents examined to documents returned by queries with the given query shape.|
|docsReturned|number(double)|false|none|Total number of documents returned by queries with the given query shape.|
|execCount|number(double)|false|none|Total number of times that queries with the given query shape have been executed.|
|keysDeleted|number(double) \| null|false|none|Total number of index keys deleted by queries with the given query shape. Available for MongoDB 9.0+ write commands.|
|keysExamined|number(double)|false|none|Total number of in-bounds and out-of-bounds index keys examined by queries with the given query shape.|
|keysExaminedRatio|number(double)|false|none|Ratio of in-bounds and out-of-bounds index keys examined to indexes containing documents returned by queries with the given query shape.|
|keysInserted|number(double) \| null|false|none|Total number of index keys inserted by queries with the given query shape. Available for MongoDB 9.0+ write commands.|
|lastExecMicros|number(double)|false|none|Execution runtime in microseconds for the most recent query with the given query shape.|
|nDeleted|number(double) \| null|false|none|Total number of documents deleted by queries with the given query shape. Available for MongoDB 9.0+ write commands.|
|nInserted|number(double) \| null|false|none|Total number of documents inserted by queries with the given query shape. Available for MongoDB 9.0+ write commands.|
|nMatched|number(double) \| null|false|none|Total number of documents matched by queries with the given query shape. Available for MongoDB 9.0+ write commands.|
|nModified|number(double) \| null|false|none|Total number of documents modified by queries with the given query shape. Available for MongoDB 9.0+ write commands.|
|nUpserted|number(double) \| null|false|none|Total number of documents upserted by queries with the given query shape. Available for MongoDB 9.0+ write commands.|
|namespace|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the namespace on the specified host. The resource expresses this parameter value as `<database>.<collection>`.|
|p50ExecMicros|number(double)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The 50th percentile value of execution time in microseconds. This field is deprecated as the values it reports may be inaccurate. It will be removed in a future release.|
|p90ExecMicros|number(double)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The 90th percentile value of execution time in microseconds. This field is deprecated as the values it reports may be inaccurate. It will be removed in a future release.|
|p99ExecMicros|number(double)|false|none|**Deprecated.** The 99th percentile value of execution time in microseconds. This field is deprecated as the values it reports may be inaccurate. It will be removed in a future release.|
|queryShape|string|false|none|A query shape is a set of specifications that group similar queries together. Specifications can include filters, sorts, projections, aggregation pipeline stages, a namespace, and others. Queries that have similar specifications have the same query shape.|
|queryShapeHash|string|false|none|A hexadecimal string that represents the hash of a MongoDB query shape.|
|systemQuery|boolean|false|none|Indicates whether this query shape represents a system-initiated query.|
|totalTimeToResponseMicros|number(double)|false|none|Total time in microseconds from the beginning of query processing to the first server response, summed across executions of queries with the given query shape. Includes time spent waiting on locks or flow control. Stops at the first batch of results, so time spent serving later `getMore` batches is not counted.|
|totalWorkingMillis|number(double)|false|none|Total time in milliseconds that queries with the given query shape spent actively executing, summed across executions, including time spent processing `getMore` requests. Excludes intentional pauses such as time waiting on locks or flow control, and time spent waiting for the client.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|command|find|
|command|distinct|
|command|aggregate|
|command|count|
|command|insert|
|command|update|
|command|delete|

```json
    {
      "electableSpecs": {
        "diskIOPS": 0,
        "diskThroughput": 0,
        "ebsVolumeType": "STANDARD",
        "instanceSize": "M10",
        "nodeCount": 0
      },
      "priority": 0,
      "providerName": "AWS",
      "regionName": "US_GOV_WEST_1"
    }
  ],
  "zoneId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "zoneName": "string"
}
```

Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data on the specified MongoDB database.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the replication object for a zone in a Multi-Cloud Cluster. If you include existing zones in the request, you must specify this parameter. If you add a new zone to an existing Multi-Cloud Cluster, you may specify this parameter. The request deletes any existing zones in the Multi-Cloud Cluster that you exclude from the request.|
|numShards|integer(int32)|false|none|Positive integer that specifies the number of shards to deploy in each specified zone. If you set this value to `1` and `clusterType` is `SHARDED`, MongoDB Cloud deploys a single-shard sharded cluster. Don't create a sharded cluster with a single shard for production environments. Single-shard sharded clusters don't provide the same benefits as multi-shard configurations.<br><br> If you are upgrading a replica set to a sharded cluster, you cannot increase the number of shards in the same update request.  You should wait until after the cluster has completed upgrading to sharded and you have reconnected all application clients to the MongoDB router before adding additional shards. Otherwise, your data might become inconsistent once MongoDB Cloud begins distributing data across shards.|
|regionConfigs|[[CloudRegionConfig](#schemacloudregionconfig)]|false|none|Hardware specifications for nodes set for a given region. Each `regionConfigs` object must be unique by region and cloud provider within the `replicationSpec`. Each `regionConfigs` object describes the region's priority in elections and the number and type of MongoDB nodes that MongoDB Cloud deploys to the region. Each `regionConfigs` object must have either an `analyticsSpecs` object, `electableSpecs` object, or `readOnlySpecs` object. Tenant clusters only require `electableSpecs`. Dedicated clusters can specify any of these specifications, but must have at least one `electableSpecs` object within a `replicationSpec`. Every hardware specification must use the same `instanceSize`.<br><br>**Example:**<br><br>If you set `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].analyticsSpecs.instanceSize` : `M30`, set `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].electableSpecs.instanceSize` : `M30` if you have electable nodes and `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].readOnlySpecs.instanceSize` : `M30` if you have read-only nodes.|
|zoneId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies a zone in a Global Cluster.|
|zoneName|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the zone in a Global Cluster. Provide this value only if `"clusterType" : "GEOSHARDED"`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the replication object for a shard in a Cluster. If you include existing shard replication configurations in the request, you must specify this parameter. If you add a new shard to an existing Cluster, you may specify this parameter. The request deletes any existing shards  in the Cluster that you exclude from the request. This corresponds to Shard ID displayed in the UI.|
|regionConfigs|[[CloudRegionConfig20240805](#schemacloudregionconfig20240805)]|false|none|Hardware specifications for nodes set for a given region. Each `regionConfigs` object must be unique by region and cloud provider within the `replicationSpec`. Each `regionConfigs` object describes the region's priority in elections and the number and type of MongoDB nodes that MongoDB Cloud deploys to the region. Each `regionConfigs` object must have either an `analyticsSpecs` object, `electableSpecs` object, or `readOnlySpecs` object. Tenant clusters only require `electableSpecs`. Dedicated clusters can specify any of these specifications, but must have at least one `electableSpecs` object within a `replicationSpec`.<br><br>**Example:**<br><br>If you set `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].analyticsSpecs.instanceSize` : `M30`, set `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].electableSpecs.instanceSize` : `M30` if you have electable nodes and `replicationSpecs[n].regionConfigs[m].readOnlySpecs.instanceSize` : `M30` if you have read-only nodes.|
|zoneId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the zone in a Global Cluster. This value can be used to configure Global Cluster backup policies.|
|zoneName|string|false|none|Human-readable label that describes the zone this shard belongs to in a Global Cluster. Provide this value only if `clusterType` : `GEOSHARDED` but not `selfManagedSharding` : `true`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|collectionName|string|true|none|Human-readable label that identifies the collection that contains one or more Atlas Search indexes.|
|database|string|true|none|Human-readable label that identifies the database that contains the collection with one or more Atlas Search indexes.|
|indexID|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies this Atlas Search index.|
|name|string|true|none|Human-readable label that identifies this index. Within each namespace, names of all indexes in the namespace must be unique.|
|numPartitions|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of index partitions. Allowed values are [1, 2, 4].|
|status|string|false|read-only|Condition of the search index when you made this request.<br><br>- `IN_PROGRESS`: Atlas is building or re-building the index after an edit.<br>- `STEADY`: You can use this search index.<br>- `FAILED`: Atlas could not build the index.<br>- `MIGRATING`: Atlas is upgrading the underlying cluster tier and migrating indexes.<br>- `PAUSED`: The cluster is paused.|
|storedSource|object|false|none|Flag that indicates whether to store all fields (true) on Atlas Search. By default, Atlas doesn't store (false) the fields on Atlas Search.  Alternatively, you can specify an object that only contains the list of fields to store (include) or not store (exclude) on Atlas Search. Note that storing all fields (true) is not allowed for vector search indexes. To learn more, see documentation.|
|type|string|false|none|Type of the index. Default type is search.|
|analyzer|string|false|none|Specific pre-defined method chosen to convert database field text into searchable words. This conversion reduces the text of fields into the smallest units of text. These units are called a **term** or **token**. This process, known as tokenization, involves a variety of changes made to the text in fields:<br><br>- extracting words<br>- removing punctuation<br>- removing accents<br>- changing to lowercase<br>- removing common words<br>- reducing words to their root form (stemming)<br>- changing words to their base form (lemmatization)<br> MongoDB Cloud uses the selected process to build the Atlas Search index.|
|analyzers|[[ApiAtlasFTSAnalyzersViewManual](#schemaapiatlasftsanalyzersviewmanual)]|false|none|List of user-defined methods to convert database field text into searchable words.|
|mappings|[ApiAtlasFTSMappingsViewManual](#schemaapiatlasftsmappingsviewmanual)|false|none|Index specifications for the collection's fields.|
|searchAnalyzer|string|false|none|Method applied to identify words when searching this index.|
|synonyms|[[SearchSynonymMappingDefinition](#schemasearchsynonymmappingdefinition)]|false|none|Rule sets that map words to their synonyms in this index.|

```json
        "field1",
        "field2"
      ]
    }
```
```json
  },
  "definitionVersion": {
    "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "version": 0
  },
```
