```json
  "status": "DELETING"
}
```

Contains status information about an index building in the background.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|definition|[SearchIndexDefinition](#schemasearchindexdefinition)|false|none|The search index definition set by the user.|
|definitionVersion|[SearchIndexDefinitionVersion](#schemasearchindexdefinitionversion)|false|none|Object which includes the version number of the index definition and the time that the index definition was created.|
|message|string|false|none|Optional message describing an error.|
|queryable|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether the index generation is queryable on the host.|
|status|string|false|none|Condition of the search index when you made this request.<br><br>- `DELETING`: The index is being deleted.<br>- `FAILED` The index build failed. Indexes can enter the FAILED state due to an invalid index definition.<br>- `STALE`: The index is queryable but has stopped replicating data from the indexed collection. Searches on the index may return out-of-date data.<br>- `PENDING`: Atlas has not yet started building the index.<br>- `BUILDING`: Atlas is building or re-building the index after an edit.<br>- `READY`: The index is ready and can support queries.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|DELETING|
|status|FAILED|
|status|STALE|
|status|PENDING|
|status|BUILDING|
|status|READY|
|status|DOES_NOT_EXIST|

Group of settings that configure a MongoDB serverless instance.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connectionStrings|[ServerlessInstanceDescriptionConnectionStrings](#schemaserverlessinstancedescriptionconnectionstrings)|false|read-only|Collection of Uniform Resource Locators that point to the MongoDB database.|
|createDate|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud created this serverless instance. MongoDB Cloud represents this timestamp in ISO 8601 format in UTC.|
|groupId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal character string that identifies the project.|
|id|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the serverless instance.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|read-only|List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships.|
|mongoDBVersion|string|false|read-only|Version of MongoDB that the serverless instance runs.|
|name|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the serverless instance.|
|providerSettings|[ServerlessProviderSettings](#schemaserverlessprovidersettings)|true|none|Group of cloud provider settings that configure the provisioned MongoDB serverless instance.|
|serverlessBackupOptions|[ClusterServerlessBackupOptions](#schemaclusterserverlessbackupoptions)|false|none|Group of settings that configure serverless backup.|
|stateName|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label that indicates any current activity being taken on this cluster by the Atlas control plane. With the exception of CREATING and DELETING states, clusters should always be available and have a Primary node even when in states indicating ongoing activity.<br><br> - `IDLE`: Atlas is making no changes to this cluster and all changes requested via the UI or API can be assumed to have been applied.<br> - `CREATING`: A cluster being provisioned for the very first time returns state CREATING until it is ready for connections. Ensure IP Access List and DB Users are configured before attempting to connect.<br> - `UPDATING`: A change requested via the UI, API, AutoScaling, or other scheduled activity is taking place.<br> - `DELETING`: The cluster is in the process of deletion and will soon be deleted.<br> - `REPAIRING`: One or more nodes in the cluster are being returned to service by the Atlas control plane. Other nodes should continue to provide service as normal.|
|tags|[[ResourceTag](#schemaresourcetag)]|false|none|List that contains key-value pairs between 1 to 255 characters in length for tagging and categorizing the serverless instance.|
|terminationProtectionEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether termination protection is enabled on the serverless instance. If set to `true`, MongoDB Cloud won't delete the serverless instance. If set to `false`, MongoDB Cloud will delete the serverless instance.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|stateName|IDLE|
|stateName|CREATING|
|stateName|UPDATING|
|stateName|DELETING|
|stateName|REPAIRING|

|lastUsedAddress|string \| null|false|read-only|Network address that issued the most recent request to the API. This parameter requires the address to be expressed as one Internet Protocol version 4 or version 6 address. The resource returns this parameter after this IP address makes at least one request.|
|lastUsedAt|string(date-time) \| null|false|read-only|Date when MongoDB Cloud received the most recent request that originated from this Internet Protocol version 4 or version 6 address. The resource returns this parameter when at least one request originates from this IP address. MongoDB Cloud updates this parameter each time a client accesses the permitted resource, with a delay of up to 5 minutes. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|

### Properties

|code|string|true|read-only|Reason that the shard key analysis failed. MongoDB Cloud may report additional values in the future without a new resource version, so treat a value this description does not list as a generic failure.|
|message|string|true|read-only|Human-readable explanation of the failure. This message describes the classified failure and is not the raw error text from the cluster.|
|retryStrategy|string|false|read-only|How to retry a failed shard key analysis. `BACKOFF` indicates that resubmitting the same request after a delay may succeed. `NONE` indicates that the failure describes the collection or the candidate shard key and that resubmitting the same request will fail the same way.|
|retryable|boolean|true|read-only|Flag that indicates whether submitting the same request again may succeed. This flag is `false` when the failure describes the collection or the candidate shard key, because the same request then fails the same way.|

|code|SUPPORTING_INDEX_AMBIGUOUS|

|code|SHARD_KEY_ANALYSIS_FAILED|

```json
  "updatedAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"

```

Progress of one shard key analysis. Poll this resource until `status` reaches a terminal value, then follow `resultHref` to read the analysis.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud accepted this operation (ISO 8601 format in UTC).|
|error|[ShardKeyAnalysisError](#schemashardkeyanalysiserror)|false|read-only|Details of the failure that ended the shard key analysis operation.|
|expiresAt|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud stops returning this operation (ISO 8601 format in UTC). Reads after this time return an HTTP 404 status. This value derives from `updatedAt`, so it advances with each state change while the operation is running and settles only once the operation is terminal.|
|operationId|string|true|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies this operation. When the operation succeeds, the analysis it created carries the same identifier.|
|operationType|string|true|read-only|Kind of change the operation makes. Submitting a shard key analysis creates an analysis resource, so the operation type is always `CREATE`.|
|resultHref|string|false|read-only|URI of the analysis this operation created. MongoDB Cloud returns this parameter only when `status` is `SUCCEEDED`.|
|retryAfterSeconds|integer(int32)|false|read-only|Number of seconds to wait before polling this operation again. MongoDB Cloud returns this parameter only while `status` is not terminal.|
|status|string|true|read-only|State of the shard key analysis operation. `PENDING` and `IN_PROGRESS` are non-terminal; `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED` and `SUPERSEDED` are terminal. MongoDB Cloud currently reports only `PENDING`, `SUCCEEDED` and `FAILED`. The remaining values are reserved and may be reported in the future without a new resource version.|
|updatedAt|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Date and time when this operation last changed state (ISO 8601 format in UTC). Once the operation is terminal, this is when it finished.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|status|PENDING|
|status|IN_PROGRESS|
|status|SUCCEEDED|
|status|FAILED|
|status|CANCELED|
|status|SUPERSEDED|

Shard key to analyze for one collection.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|includeKeyCharacteristics|boolean|false|write-only|Flag that indicates whether to return the cardinality, frequency and monotonicity of the candidate shard key.|
|includeReadWriteDistribution|boolean|false|write-only|Flag that indicates whether to return how reads and writes would be routed across shards under the candidate shard key. This requires query sampling to have collected operations for the namespace.|
|namespace|string|true|none|Combination of the database and collection to analyze, written as `<database>.<collection>`.|
|shardKey|[object]|true|none|Candidate shard key, given as one object per shard key field in the order the fields form the key. Field order is significant: `[{"a": "1"}, {"b": "1"}]` and `[{"b": "1"}, {"a": "1"}]` are different shard keys. At most one field may be `hashed`.|

```json
  "numOrphanDocs": 0,
  "percentageOfMultiShardReads": 0,
  "percentageOfMultiShardWrites": 0,
  "percentageOfScatterGatherReads": 0,
  "percentageOfScatterGatherWrites": 0,
  "percentageOfSingleShardReads": 0,
  "percentageOfSingleShardWrites": 0,

    "aggregate": 0,

    "distinct": 0,
    "find": 0,

  },

    {
      "property1": "string",
      "property2": "string"
    }
  ],
  "writeSampleSize": {
    "delete": 0,
    "findAndModify": 0,
    "total": 0,
    "update": 0
  }
}
```

Completed analysis of one candidate shard key, describing how well the key would distribute the collection's documents and operations across shards.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|avgDocSizeBytes|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Average size of one document in the collection, in bytes.|
|correlationCoefficient|number(double)|false|read-only|Correlation between the candidate shard key and the order in which documents were inserted, from `-1` to `1`. Values near `1` or `-1` indicate a monotonically changing key, which directs all inserts to one shard. This parameter is absent when the shard key has no supporting index or the collection is clustered, in which case MongoDB Cloud does not compute it.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Date and time when this shard key analysis was requested (ISO 8601 format in UTC). This is when the analysis was submitted, not when it completed; the completion time is the `updatedAt` of the operation that produced it.|
|expiresAt|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud stops returning this shard key analysis (ISO 8601 format in UTC). Reads after this time return an HTTP 404 status.|
|id|string|true|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies this shard key analysis. This is the same identifier as the `operationId` of the operation that produced it.|
|isUnique|boolean|false|read-only|Flag that indicates whether the index supporting the candidate shard key enforces a uniqueness constraint.|
|monotonicity|string|false|read-only|Whether the shard key value increases or decreases with the order in which documents were inserted. A monotonically changing shard key directs all inserts to one shard. `UNKNOWN` indicates that MongoDB Cloud could not determine monotonicity, which happens when the shard key has no supporting index or the collection is clustered.|
|mostCommonValues|[[ShardKeyMostCommonValue](#schemashardkeymostcommonvalue)]|false|read-only|Shard key values that occur most frequently in the sampled documents, with how often each occurs. MongoDB Cloud returns this parameter only to callers that can read the collection's data, because it carries values out of the collection rather than statistics about them.|
|namespace|string|true|none|Combination of the database and collection that was analyzed, written as `<database>.<collection>`.|
|note|string|false|read-only|Guidance from MongoDB on how to interpret the metrics in this analysis. This parameter is absent when the analysis carries no guidance.|
|numDistinctValues|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Number of distinct values that the candidate shard key takes across the sampled documents. A value close to `numDocsSampled` indicates high cardinality, which distributes documents well.|
|numDocsSampled|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Number of documents that MongoDB Cloud sampled to compute these metrics.|
|numDocsTotal|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Number of documents in the collection.|
|numOrphanDocs|integer(int64)|false|read-only|Number of orphaned documents in the collection. This parameter is absent for collections that have none.|
|percentageOfMultiShardReads|number(double)|false|read-only|Percentage of sampled reads that the candidate shard key would route to more than one shard but not to every shard.|
|percentageOfMultiShardWrites|number(double)|false|read-only|Percentage of sampled writes that the candidate shard key would route to more than one shard but not to every shard.|
|percentageOfScatterGatherReads|number(double)|false|read-only|Percentage of sampled reads that the candidate shard key would broadcast to every shard. Lower is better.|
|percentageOfScatterGatherWrites|number(double)|false|read-only|Percentage of sampled writes that the candidate shard key would broadcast to every shard. Lower is better.|
|percentageOfSingleShardReads|number(double)|false|read-only|Percentage of sampled reads that the candidate shard key would route to exactly one shard. Higher is better.|
|percentageOfSingleShardWrites|number(double)|false|read-only|Percentage of sampled writes that the candidate shard key would route to exactly one shard. Higher is better.|
|rawOutput|string|false|read-only|Unmodified result of the `analyzeShardKey` command, as a JSON string. Its content tracks the MongoDB server version of the analyzed cluster rather than the version of this resource, so members outside the parameters above may appear or change without a new resource version. Do not parse it as a stable contract. `mostCommonValues` is removed from it for callers that cannot read the collection's data. This parameter is absent if MongoDB Cloud could not serialize the command result, which costs the raw view but not the analysis.|
|readSampleSize|[ShardKeyReadSampleSize](#schemashardkeyreadsamplesize)|false|read-only|Number of sampled read operations that MongoDB Cloud used to compute the read distribution, broken down by the command that issued them.|
|shardKey|[object]|false|none|Candidate shard key that was analyzed, given as one object per shard key field in the order the fields form the key. This parameter is absent when MongoDB Cloud has no shard key recorded for the analysis.|
|writeSampleSize|[ShardKeyWriteSampleSize](#schemashardkeywritesamplesize)|false|read-only|Number of sampled write operations that MongoDB Cloud used to compute the write distribution, broken down by the command that issued them.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|monotonicity|MONOTONIC|
|monotonicity|NOT_MONOTONIC|
|monotonicity|UNKNOWN|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|cpuUtilization|[ShardCpuUtilization](#schemashardcpuutilization)|true|none|CPU utilization of the shard's nodes over the last hour, as a percentage.|
|dataSizeBytes|integer(int64)|true|read-only|Total size of the user data stored on this shard. The resource expresses this value in bytes.|
|rangeDeleterTasks|number(double)|false|read-only|Average number of range deletion tasks queued across the shard's nodes, measured at the time of the request.|
|readLatencyMicroseconds|number(double)|false|read-only|Average latency of the read operations this shard served over the last hour, in microseconds.|
|readOperationsPerSecond|[ShardOperations](#schemashardoperations)|true|none|Operations per second that the shard served over the last hour.|
|replicaSetName|string|true|read-only|Name of the shard's replica set. This is the name that identifies the same shard on the processes, alerts, events, and backup resources.|
|shardedCollections|integer(int32)|true|read-only|Number of sharded collections with data on this shard.|
|warnings|[string]|true|read-only|Conditions that MongoDB Cloud observed on this shard relative to the rest of the cluster. `HOTSPOT` means this shard's average CPU utilization is more than twice the average across all shards of the cluster. This is a cluster-scoped comparison, so its value depends on how loaded the other shards are and not only on this shard.|
|writeOperationsPerSecond|[ShardOperations](#schemashardoperations)|true|none|Operations per second that the shard served over the last hour.|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

```json
{
  "endTime": "06:00",
  "startTime": "02:00",
  "status": "CONFIGURED"
}
```

Balancing window configured on the sharded cluster. When configured, the balancer moves data only during the daily interval between `startTime` and `endTime`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|endTime|string \| null|false|read-only|Time of day at which the balancing window ends, in 24-hour `HH:MM` format as configured on the cluster. Present only when `status` is `CONFIGURED`.|
|startTime|string \| null|false|read-only|Time of day at which the balancing window starts, in 24-hour `HH:MM` format as configured on the cluster. Present only when `status` is `CONFIGURED`.|
|status|string|true|read-only|State of the balancing window. `CONFIGURED` means the cluster restricts balancing to the interval between `startTime` and `endTime`. `NOT_CONFIGURED` means the balancer may run at any time. `FAILED_INITIAL_METRIC_PENDING` means MongoDB Cloud has not yet collected balancer metrics for a recently created or converted cluster. `FAILED_TO_DETERMINE` means the window could not be resolved.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|CONFIGURED|
|status|NOT_CONFIGURED|
|status|FAILED_TO_DETERMINE|
|status|FAILED_INITIAL_METRIC_PENDING|

Cluster-level sharding state of one sharded cluster: shard count, balancer state, config server availability, and the configured balancing window.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|balancerState|string|true|read-only|State of the cluster balancer. `BALANCING` means a balancer round is in progress. `IDLE` means the balancer is enabled and no round is in progress. `DISABLED` means the balancer is turned off. `FAILED_TO_DETERMINE` means the balancer state could not be resolved.|
|balancingWindow|[ShardingInsightsBalancingWindow](#schemashardinginsightsbalancingwindow)|true|none|Balancing window configured on the sharded cluster. When configured, the balancer moves data only during the daily interval between `startTime` and `endTime`.|
|configServerStatus|string|true|read-only|Availability of the cluster's config servers. `AVAILABLE` means at least one config server reported recently. `UNAVAILABLE` means config servers exist but none has reported recently. `FAILED_TO_DETERMINE` means availability could not be resolved.|
|totalShards|integer(int32)|true|read-only|Number of shards in the cluster.|

#### Enumerated Values

|configServerStatus|FAILED_TO_DETERMINE|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|apiToken|string|false|none|Slack API token or Bot token that MongoDB Cloud needs to send alert notifications via Slack. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "SLACK"`. If the token later becomes invalid, MongoDB Cloud sends an email to the project owners. If the token remains invalid, MongoDB Cloud removes the token. <br><br>**NOTE**: After you create a notification which requires an API or integration key, the key appears partially redacted when you:<br><br>* View or edit the alert through the Atlas UI.<br><br>* Query the alert for the notification through the Atlas Administration API.|
|channelName|string|false|none|Name of the Slack channel to which MongoDB Cloud sends alert notifications. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "SLACK"`.|
|delayMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes that MongoDB Cloud waits after detecting an alert condition before it sends out the first notification.|
|integrationId|string|false|none|The id of the associated integration, the credentials of which to use for requests.|
|intervalMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes to wait between successive notifications. MongoDB Cloud sends notifications until someone acknowledges the unacknowledged alert.<br><br>PagerDuty, VictorOps, and OpsGenie notifications don't return this element. Configure and manage the notification interval within each of those services.|
|notifierId|string|false|none|The `notifierId` is a system-generated unique identifier assigned to each notification method. This is needed when updating third-party notifications without requiring explicit authentication credentials.|
|typeName|string|true|none|Human-readable label that displays the alert notification type.|

|Property|Value|

```json
  "shardSizeLimitGB": 1
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|shardSizeLimitGB|integer(int32) \| null|false|none|Available in Public Preview: Maximum data size that MongoDB Cloud allows each shard of this cluster to reach, expressed in gigabytes. MongoDB Cloud rejects writes to a shard that reaches the limit that it enforces. In `replicationSpecs`, this field reports the limit that you configured, and MongoDB Cloud omits it when you never configured one. In `effectiveReplicationSpecs`, this field reports the limit that MongoDB Cloud enforces: usually the limit that you configured, otherwise the default limit that MongoDB Cloud assigns when it creates or updates the cluster. This value may differ from the limit that you configured due to system-managed changes. This limit applies to every shard of the cluster; set the same value on each region configuration's `autoScaling`, as MongoDB Cloud rejects requests that specify differing values. You can set this only on Atlas INFINITE clusters: MongoDB Cloud rejects any request that names this field, including as `null`, for a cluster or node type that doesn't support it. In a request that includes `replicationSpecs`, omitting `shardSizeLimitGB` or sending it as `null` clears the limit. Omitting `replicationSpecs` preserves it.|

```json
  "minTier": "SP50"

```

Autoscaling configuration for a stream processor.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean \| null|false|none|Flag that indicates whether autoscaling is enabled.<br><br>- **Omitted, `null`, or `false`:**<br>  - On `CREATE`: a no-op, there is no persisted setting yet to disable or clear.<br>  - On `MODIFY` or `:startWith`: omitted preserves the current setting. `null` or `false` disables autoscaling and clears its configuration.<br>- **`true`** on `CREATE`, `MODIFY`, or `:startWith`: enables autoscaling.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|read-only|List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships.|
|maxTier|string \| null|false|none|Tier ceiling for autoscaling (scale-up limit).<br><br>- **Omitted:**<br>  - On `CREATE`: falls back to the workspace max tier (there is no current bound to preserve).<br>  - On `MODIFY` or `:startWith`: the current bound is preserved.<br>- **`null`** on `CREATE`, `MODIFY`, or `:startWith`: resets the bound to the workspace max tier.<br>- **A tier value** on `CREATE`, `MODIFY`, or `:startWith`: sets the bound to that tier.|
|minTier|string \| null|false|none|Tier floor for autoscaling (scale-down limit).<br><br>- **Omitted:**<br>  - On `CREATE`: defaults to the lower of the processor `tier` and the workspace default tier (there is no current bound to preserve).<br>  - On `MODIFY` or `:startWith`: the current bound is preserved.<br>- **`null`** on `CREATE`, `MODIFY`, or `:startWith`: resets the bound to the lower of the processor `tier` and the workspace default tier.<br>- **A tier value** on `CREATE`, `MODIFY`, or `:startWith`: sets the bound to that tier.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|maxTier|SP50|
|maxTier|SP30|
|maxTier|SP10|
|maxTier|SP5|
|maxTier|SP2|
|minTier|SP50|
|minTier|SP30|
|minTier|SP10|
|minTier|SP5|
|minTier|SP2|

<h2 id="tocS_StreamsStartProcessorFailover">StreamsStartProcessorFailover</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemastreamsstartprocessorfailover"></a>
<a id="schema_StreamsStartProcessorFailover"></a>
<a id="tocSstreamsstartprocessorfailover"></a>
<a id="tocsstreamsstartprocessorfailover"></a>

```json
{
  "clearCheckpoint": true,
  "dryRun": true,
  "mode": "GRACEFUL",
  "region": "VIRGINIA_USA"
}
```

Failover options for starting a stream processor.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clearCheckpoint|boolean|false|none|If true, clears the checkpoint so the failover processor does not resume from it. Applies only to FORCED failover; clearing may cause duplicate or missing records in the output.|
|dryRun|boolean|false|none|If true, simulates the operation without making any changes.|
|mode|string|false|none|Strategy for the processor: GRACEFUL - attempt to stop the processor, error if processor cannot be stopped. if stop was successful, start the processor in the new region with the latest checkpoint.  FORCED - attempt to stop the processor, proceed to starting the processor in the new region with checkpoints disabled regardless of whether or not the stop succeeds.|
|region|string|true|none|Cloud provider region where the stream processor should be started in failover mode. The region must be a valid region for the stream processor's cloud provider and must be included in the tenant's configured failover regions, or it may be the tenant's default (primary) region.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|GRACEFUL|
|mode|FORCED|

```json
  },

    {
      "href": "https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas",
      "rel": "self"
    }
  ],

  "startAtOperationTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "tier": "SP50"
}
```

A request to start a stream processor.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|autoscaling|[StreamsAutoscaling](#schemastreamsautoscaling)|false|none|Autoscaling configuration for a stream processor.|
|failover|[StreamsStartProcessorFailover](#schemastreamsstartprocessorfailover)|false|none|Failover options for starting a stream processor.|

|startAtOperationTime|string(date-time)|false|none|The operation time after which the change stream source should begin reporting. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|


Team notification configuration for MongoDB Cloud to send information when an event triggers an alert condition.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delayMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes that MongoDB Cloud waits after detecting an alert condition before it sends out the first notification.|
|emailEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud should send email notifications. The resource requires this parameter when one of the following values have been set:<br><br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "ORG"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "GROUP"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "USER"`|
|intervalMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes to wait between successive notifications. MongoDB Cloud sends notifications until someone acknowledges the unacknowledged alert.<br><br>PagerDuty, VictorOps, and OpsGenie notifications don't return this element. Configure and manage the notification interval within each of those services.|
|notifierId|string|false|none|The `notifierId` is a system-generated unique identifier assigned to each notification method. This is needed when updating third-party notifications without requiring explicit authentication credentials.|
|smsEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud should send text message notifications. The resource requires this parameter when one of the following values have been set:<br><br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "ORG"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "GROUP"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "USER"`|
|teamId|string|false|none|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies one MongoDB Cloud team. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "TEAM"`.|
|teamName|string|false|none|Name of the MongoDB Cloud team that receives this notification. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "TEAM"`.|
|typeName|string|true|none|Human-readable label that displays the alert notification type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|typeName|TEAM|

Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|electableSpecs|[HardwareSpec](#schemahardwarespec)|false|none|Hardware specifications for all electable nodes deployed in the region. Electable nodes can become the primary and can enable local reads. If you don't specify this option, MongoDB Cloud deploys no electable nodes to the region.|
|priority|integer(int32)|false|none|Precedence is given to this region when a primary election occurs. If your `regionConfigs` has only `readOnlySpecs`, `analyticsSpecs`, or both, set this value to `0`. If you have multiple `regionConfigs` objects (your cluster is multi-region or multi-cloud), they must have priorities in descending order. The highest priority is `7`.<br><br>**Example:** If you have three regions, their priorities would be `7`, `6`, and `5` respectively. If you added two more regions for supporting electable nodes, the priorities of those regions would be `4` and `3` respectively.|
|providerName|string|false|none|Cloud service provider on which MongoDB Cloud provisions the hosts. Set dedicated clusters to `AWS`, `GCP`, `AZURE` or `TENANT`.|
|regionName|object|false|none|Physical location of your MongoDB cluster nodes. The region you choose can affect network latency for clients accessing your databases. The region name is only returned in the response for single-region clusters. When MongoDB Cloud deploys a dedicated cluster, it checks if a VPC or VPC connection exists for that provider and region. If not, MongoDB Cloud creates them as part of the deployment. It assigns the VPC a Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) block. To limit a new VPC peering connection to one Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) block and region, create the connection first. Deploy the cluster after the connection starts. GCP Clusters and Multi-region clusters require one VPC peering connection for each region. MongoDB nodes can use only the peering connection that resides in the same region as the nodes to communicate with the peered VPC.|
|*oneOf*|[AWSRegionConfig](#schemaawsregionconfig)|false|none|Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.|
|*oneOf*|[AzureRegionConfig](#schemaazureregionconfig)|false|none|Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.|
|*oneOf*|[GCPRegionConfig](#schemagcpregionconfig)|false|none|Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.|
|*oneOf*|[TenantRegionConfig](#schematenantregionconfig)|false|none|Details that explain how MongoDB Cloud replicates data in one region on the specified MongoDB database.|
|backingProviderName|string|false|none|Cloud service provider on which MongoDB Cloud provisioned the multi-tenant cluster. The resource returns this parameter when `providerName` is `TENANT` and `electableSpecs.instanceSize` is `M0`, `M2` or `M5`. <br><br>Please note that using an `instanceSize` of M2 or M5 will create a Flex cluster instead. Support for the `instanceSize` of M2 or M5 will be discontinued in January 2026. We recommend using the Create Flex Cluster API for such configurations moving forward.|

|providerName|AWS|
|providerName|AZURE|
|providerName|GCP|
|providerName|TENANT|
|backingProviderName|AWS|
|backingProviderName|GCP|
|backingProviderName|AZURE|

The text search index definition set by the user.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|analyzer|string|false|none|Specific pre-defined method chosen to convert database field text into searchable words. This conversion reduces the text of fields into the smallest units of text. These units are called a **term** or **token**. This process, known as tokenization, involves making the following changes to the text in fields:<br><br>- extracting words<br>- removing punctuation<br>- removing accents<br>- changing to lowercase<br>- removing common words<br>- reducing words to their root form (stemming)<br>- changing words to their base form (lemmatization)<br> MongoDB Cloud uses the process you select to build the Atlas Search index.|
|analyzers|[[AtlasSearchAnalyzer](#schemaatlassearchanalyzer)]|false|none|List of user-defined methods to convert database field text into searchable words.|
|mappings|[SearchMappings](#schemasearchmappings)|true|none|Index specifications for the collection's fields.|
|numPartitions|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of index partitions. Allowed values are [1, 2, 4].|
|searchAnalyzer|string|false|none|Method applied to identify words when searching this index.|
|sort|object|false|none|Sort definition for the index. When defined, the index will be pre-sorted on the specified fields, which improves query sort performance for those fields. Supports two formats: simple format with field name and direction, or complex format with additional options. The `order` field is required (1=ascending, -1=descending).The `noData` field is optional and controls how missing values are sorted(default: "lowest").|
|storedSource|object|false|none|Flag that indicates whether to store all fields (true) on Atlas Search. By default, Atlas doesn't store (false) the fields on Atlas Search.  Alternatively, you can specify an object that only contains the list of fields to store (include) or not store (exclude) on Atlas Search. Note that storing all fields (true) is not allowed for vector search indexes. To learn more, see Stored Source Fields.|
|synonyms|[[SearchSynonymMappingDefinition](#schemasearchsynonymmappingdefinition)]|false|none|Rule sets that map words to their synonyms in this index.|
|typeSets|[[SearchTypeSets](#schemasearchtypesets)]|false|none|Type sets for the index.|

Indexes can enter the FAILED state due to an invalid index definition.<br>- `STALE`: The index is queryable but has stopped replicating data from the indexed collection. Searches on the index may return out-of-date data.<br>- `PENDING`: Atlas has not yet started building the index.<br>- `BUILDING`: Atlas is building or re-building the index after an edit.<br>- `READY`: The index is ready and can support queries.|
|statusDetail|[[SearchHostStatusDetail](#schemasearchhoststatusdetail)]|false|none|List of documents detailing index status on each host.|

|statusDetail|[[TextSearchHostStatusDetail](#schematextsearchhoststatusdetail)]|false|none|List of documents detailing index status on each host.|
|synonymMappingStatus|string|false|none|Status that describes this index's synonym mappings. This status appears only if the index has synonyms defined.|
|synonymMappingStatusDetail|[object]|false|none|A list of documents describing the status of the index's synonym mappings on each search host. Only appears if the index has synonyms defined.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|acknowledgedUntil|string(date-time)|false|none|Date and time until which this alert has been acknowledged. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. The resource returns this parameter if a MongoDB User previously acknowledged this alert.<br><br>- To acknowledge this alert forever, set the parameter value to 100 years in the future.<br><br>- To unacknowledge a previously acknowledged alert, do not set this parameter value.|
|acknowledgementComment|string|false|none|Comment that a MongoDB Cloud user submitted when acknowledging the alert.|
|acknowledgingUsername|string(email)|false|read-only|MongoDB Cloud username of the person who acknowledged the alert. The response returns this parameter if a MongoDB Cloud user previously acknowledged this alert.|
|alertConfigId|string|true|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the alert configuration that sets this alert.|
|clusterName|string|false|read-only|Human-readable label that identifies the cluster to which this alert applies. This resource returns this parameter for alerts of events impacting backups, replica sets, or sharded clusters.|
|created|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Date and time when MongoDB Cloud created this alert. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|currentValue|[TimeMetricValueView](#schematimemetricvalueview)|false|read-only|Measurement of the `metricName` recorded at the time of the event.|
|eventTypeName|[HostMetricEventTypeViewAlertable](#schemahostmetriceventtypeviewalertable)|true|none|Event type that triggers an alert.|
|groupId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the project that owns this alert.|
|hostnameAndPort|string|false|read-only|Hostname and port of the host to which this alert applies. The resource returns this parameter for alerts of events impacting hosts or replica sets.|
|id|string|true|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies this alert.|
|lastNotified|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time that any notifications were last sent for this alert. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. The resource returns this parameter if MongoDB Cloud has sent notifications for this alert.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|read-only|List of one or more Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) that point to API sub-resources, related API resources, or both. RFC 5988 outlines these relationships.|
|metricName|string|false|read-only|Name of the metric against which Atlas checks the configured `metricThreshold.threshold`.<br><br>To learn more about the available metrics, see <a href="https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-host-metrics/#std-label-measurement-types" target="_blank">Host Metrics</a>.<br><br>**NOTE**: If you set `eventTypeName` to `OUTSIDE_SERVERLESS_METRIC_THRESHOLD`, you can specify only metrics available for serverless. To learn more, see <a href="https://dochub.mongodb.org/core/alert-config-serverless-measurements" target="_blank">Serverless Measurements</a>.|
|orgId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal character string that identifies the organization that owns the project to which this alert applies.|
|replicaSetName|string|false|read-only|Name of the replica set to which this alert applies. The response returns this parameter for alerts of events impacting backups, hosts, or replica sets.|
|resolved|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time that this alert changed to `"status" : "CLOSED"`. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC. The resource returns this parameter once `"status" : "CLOSED"`.|
|severity|string|false|read-only|Severity of the event.|
|status|string|true|read-only|State of this alert at the time you requested its details. TRACKING indicates the alert condition exists but has not persisted for the minimum notification delay. OPEN indicates the alert condition currently exists. CLOSED indicates the alert condition has been resolved.|
|updated|string(date-time)|true|read-only|Date and time when someone last updated this alert. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|

|severity|WARNING|
|severity|ERROR|
|severity|CRITICAL|
|status|CANCELLED|
|status|CLOSED|
|status|OPEN|
|status|TRACKING|

```json
{
  "delayMin": 0,
  "emailEnabled": true,
  "intervalMin": 5,
  "notifierId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "smsEnabled": true,
  "typeName": "USER",
  "username": "user@example.com"
}
```

User notification configuration for MongoDB Cloud to send information when an event triggers an alert condition.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delayMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes that MongoDB Cloud waits after detecting an alert condition before it sends out the first notification.|
|emailEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud should send email notifications. The resource requires this parameter when one of the following values have been set:<br><br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "ORG"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "GROUP"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "USER"`|
|intervalMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes to wait between successive notifications. MongoDB Cloud sends notifications until someone acknowledges the unacknowledged alert.<br><br>PagerDuty, VictorOps, and OpsGenie notifications don't return this element. Configure and manage the notification interval within each of those services.|
|notifierId|string|false|none|The `notifierId` is a system-generated unique identifier assigned to each notification method. This is needed when updating third-party notifications without requiring explicit authentication credentials.|
|smsEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that indicates whether MongoDB Cloud should send text message notifications. The resource requires this parameter when one of the following values have been set:<br><br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "ORG"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "GROUP"`<br>- `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "USER"`|
|typeName|string|true|none|Human-readable label that displays the alert notification type.|
|username|string(email)|false|none|MongoDB Cloud username of the person to whom MongoDB Cloud sends notifications. Specify only MongoDB Cloud users who belong to the project that owns the alert configuration. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "USER"`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|typeName|USER|

User-to-Distinguished Name (DN) map that MongoDB Cloud uses to transform a Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) username into an LDAP DN.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ldapQuery|string|false|none|Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) query template that inserts the LDAP name that the regular expression matches into an LDAP query Uniform Resource Identifier (URI). The formatting for the query must conform to [RFC 4515](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4515) and [RFC 4516](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4516).|
|match|string|true|none|Regular expression that MongoDB Cloud uses to match against the provided Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) username. Each parenthesis-enclosed section represents a regular expression capture group that the substitution or `ldapQuery` template uses.|
|substitution|string|false|none|Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) Distinguished Name (DN) template that converts the LDAP username that matches regular expression in the *match* parameter into an LDAP Distinguished Name (DN).|

### Properties

|collectionName|string|true|none|Label that identifies the collection to create an Atlas Search index in.|
|database|string|true|none|Label that identifies the database that contains the collection to create an Atlas Search index in.|
|name|string|true|none|Label that identifies this index. Within each namespace, names of all indexes in the namespace must be unique.|
|type|string|false|none|Type of the index. The default type is search.|
|definition|[VectorSearchIndexDefinition](#schemavectorsearchindexdefinition)|true|none|The vector search index definition set by the user.|

```json
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    }
  ],
  "nestedRoot": "sections",
  "numPartitions": 1,

      "field1",
      "field2"
    ]
  }

```

The vector search index definition set by the user.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|[[BasicDBObject](#schemabasicdbobject)]|true|none|Settings that configure the fields, one per object, to index. You must define at least one "vector" type field. You can optionally define "filter" type fields also.|
|nestedRoot|string|false|none|Top-level path to the array that contains vector fields. When provided, vector fields under this path are treated as nested.|
|numPartitions|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of index partitions. Allowed values are [1, 2, 4].|
|storedSource|object|false|none|Flag that indicates whether to store all fields (true) on Atlas Search. By default, Atlas doesn't store (false) the fields on Atlas Search.  Alternatively, you can specify an object that only contains the list of fields to store (include) or not store (exclude) on Atlas Search. Note that storing all fields (true) is not allowed for vector search indexes. To learn more, see Stored Source Fields.|

<h2 id="tocS_VictorOpsNotification">VictorOpsNotification</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavictoropsnotification"></a>
<a id="schema_VictorOpsNotification"></a>
<a id="tocSvictoropsnotification"></a>
<a id="tocsvictoropsnotification"></a>

```json
{
  "delayMin": 0,
  "integrationId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "intervalMin": 5,
  "notifierId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "typeName": "VICTOR_OPS",
  "victorOpsApiKey": "********************************9abc",
  "victorOpsRoutingKey": "test routing"
}
```

VictorOps notification configuration for MongoDB Cloud to send information when an event triggers an alert condition.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|delayMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes that MongoDB Cloud waits after detecting an alert condition before it sends out the first notification.|
|integrationId|string|false|none|The id of the associated integration, the credentials of which to use for requests.|
|intervalMin|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of minutes to wait between successive notifications. MongoDB Cloud sends notifications until someone acknowledges the unacknowledged alert.<br><br>PagerDuty, VictorOps, and OpsGenie notifications don't return this element. Configure and manage the notification interval within each of those services.|
|notifierId|string|false|none|The `notifierId` is a system-generated unique identifier assigned to each notification method. This is needed when updating third-party notifications without requiring explicit authentication credentials.|
|typeName|string|true|none|Human-readable label that displays the alert notification type.|
|victorOpsApiKey|string|false|none|API key that MongoDB Cloud needs to send alert notifications to Splunk On-Call. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "VICTOR_OPS"`. If the key later becomes invalid, MongoDB Cloud sends an email to the project owners. If the key remains invalid, MongoDB Cloud removes it.<br><br>**NOTE**: After you create a notification which requires an API or integration key, the key appears partially redacted when you:<br><br>* View or edit the alert through the Atlas UI.<br><br>* Query the alert for the notification through the Atlas Administration API.|
|victorOpsRoutingKey|string|false|none|Routing key that MongoDB Cloud needs to send alert notifications to Splunk On-Call. The resource requires this parameter when `"notifications.[n].typeName" : "VICTOR_OPS"`. If the key later becomes invalid, MongoDB Cloud sends an email to the project owners. If the key remains invalid, MongoDB Cloud removes it.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|typeName|VICTOR_OPS|

<h2 id="tocS_Webhook">Webhook</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemawebhook"></a>
<a id="schema_Webhook"></a>
<a id="tocSwebhook"></a>
<a id="tocswebhook"></a>

```json
{
  "bodyTemplate": "{\"alert\":\"${id}\",\"severity\":\"${severity}\"}",
  "headersTemplate": "{\"X-Alert-Id\":\"${id}\",\"X-Event-Type\":\"${eventType}\"}",
  "id": "string",
  "secret": "password",
  "type": "WEBHOOK",
  "url": "https://webhook.com/****"
}
```

Details to integrate one webhook with one MongoDB Cloud project.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|bodyTemplate|string(password)|false|none|HTTP body template for a webhook-based alert. The rendered output MUST be valid JSON — MongoDB Cloud sends the rendered body with `Content-Type: application/json`. If the template fails to render, exceeds the 16 KB limit, or renders non-JSON output, MongoDB Cloud sends the webhook with its default JSON payload instead.|
|headersTemplate|string(password)|false|none|HTTP headers template for a webhook-based alert. The rendered output MUST be a JSON object mapping header name to header value (e.g. `{"X-Custom-Header": "static-value", "X-Alert-Id": "${id}"}`). Placeholders may reference any alert-view field plus `${eventType}`; the webhook secret and the signature header are NOT exposed to templates. If the template fails to render, exceeds the 4 KB limit, or renders output that is not a valid JSON name→value object, MongoDB Cloud sends the webhook with its default set of headers instead.|
|id|string \| null|false|none|Integration id.|
|secret|string(password)|false|none|An optional field returned if your webhook is configured with a secret.<br><br>**NOTE**: When you view or edit the alert for a webhook notification, the secret appears completely redacted.|
|type|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the service to which you want to integrate with MongoDB Cloud. The value must match the third-party service integration type.|
|url|string|true|none|Endpoint web address to which MongoDB Cloud sends notifications.<br><br>**NOTE**: When you view or edit the alert for a webhook notification, the URL appears partially redacted.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|WEBHOOK|

MongoDB Cloud sends notifications until someone acknowledges the unacknowledged alert.<br><br>PagerDuty, VictorOps, and OpsGenie notifications don't return this element. Configure and manage the notification interval within each of those services.|

```json
  "id": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "orgId": "32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8",
  "orgName": "Test Organization",
  "severity": "INFO"
}
```

Additional meta information captured about this event. The response returns this parameter as a JSON object when the query parameter `includeRaw=true`. The list of fields in the raw document may change. Don't rely on raw values for formal monitoring.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|_t|string|false|none|Unique identifier of event type.|
|alertConfigId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the alert configuration related to the event.|
|cid|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the project in which the event occurred.|
|cre|string(date-time)|false|read-only|Date and time when this event occurred. This parameter expresses its value in the ISO 8601 timestamp format in UTC.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|Description of the event.|
|gn|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the project.|
|id|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the event.|
|orgId|string|false|read-only|Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies the organization to which these events apply.|
|orgName|string|false|none|Human-readable label that identifies the organization that contains the project.|
|severity|string|false|none|Severity of the event.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|severity|INFO|
|severity|WARNING|
|severity|ERROR|
|severity|CRITICAL|

<h2 id="tocS_tokenFilterdaitchMokotoffSoundex">tokenFilterdaitchMokotoffSoundex</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematokenfilterdaitchmokotoffsoundex"></a>
<a id="schema_tokenFilterdaitchMokotoffSoundex"></a>
<a id="tocStokenfilterdaitchmokotoffsoundex"></a>
<a id="tocstokenfilterdaitchmokotoffsoundex"></a>

```json
{
  "originalTokens": "include",
  "type": "daitchMokotoffSoundex"
}
```

Filter that creates tokens for words that sound the same based on the Daitch-Mokotoff Soundex phonetic algorithm. This filter can generate multiple encodings for each input, where each encoded token is a 6 digit number.

**NOTE**: Don't use the `daitchMokotoffSoundex` token filter in:

-Synonym or autocomplete mapping definitions
- Operators where **fuzzy** is enabled. Atlas Search supports the **fuzzy** option only for the **autocomplete**, **term**, and **text** operators.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|originalTokens|string|false|none|Value that indicates whether to include or omit the original tokens in the output of the token filter.<br><br>Choose `include` if you want to support queries on both the original tokens as well as the converted forms.<br><br> Choose `omit` if you want to query only on the converted forms of the original tokens.|
|type|string|true|none|Human-readable label that identifies this token filter type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|originalTokens|omit|
|originalTokens|include|
|type|daitchMokotoffSoundex|
